subProcesses.name: Mortality & Longevity Experience Study
steps: Extract in-force and terminated policy records for life and annuity lines
Construct exposed-to-risk and observed death counts by age band, gender, and product
Calculate actual-to-expected (A/E) mortality ratios by cohort
Apply credibility weighting to company experience using Bühlmann or limited fluctuation methods
Benchmark company mortality to industry tables (VBT, SOA prescribed tables)
Assess mortality improvement trends and select future improvement scales
Analyze longevity risk for annuity in-payout block separately from life block
Review underwriting quality and select/ultimate distinctions in mortality data
Draft updated mortality and longevity assumptions with supporting analysis
Obtain Appointed Actuary and peer review approval of updated mortality assumptions
Document assumption change rationale in actuarial assumption governance register
Communicate updated assumptions to Reserving, Pricing, and Capital Modeling teams

subProcesses.name: Lapse, Surrender & Policyholder Behavior Study
steps: Extract policy lapse, surrender, and partial withdrawal data by product and duration
Calculate observed lapse rates by policy year, premium payment status, and distribution channel
Segment lapses by shock (surrender charge expiry) and base lapse components
Analyze dynamic lapse behavior relative to market interest rates for interest-sensitive products
Compare observed lapse rates to assumed rates used in pricing and PBR valuation
Investigate policyholder behavior by segment (premium financing, employer-sponsored)
Develop dynamic lapse function incorporating spread between credited and market rates
Apply credibility weighting to lapse study results by product and duration
Draft updated lapse and policyholder behavior assumptions
Coordinate review with Product Management and Distribution on behavioral drivers
Obtain Chief Actuary approval of updated lapse assumptions
Update assumption register and propagate changes to valuation and pricing models

subProcesses.name: Morbidity & Healthcare Utilization Study
steps: Extract claim frequency and severity data for health, disability, and long-term care lines
Compute claim incidence rates and claim duration patterns by benefit trigger and age
Analyze healthcare utilization trends (inpatient days, outpatient visits, Rx costs) by plan type
Adjust for benefit design changes and legislative mandates impacting utilization
Assess long-term care claim termination rates including mortality and recovery
Benchmark morbidity to LIMRA, SOA, or AHIP industry studies
Identify geographic and demographic drivers of morbidity variance
Develop updated claim cost, incidence, and duration assumptions
Coordinate with Medical Management team on care management trend impacts
Document assumption derivation and peer review findings
Obtain approval of updated morbidity assumptions from Chief Actuary
Distribute updated assumptions to Health Pricing and Reserving teams

subProcesses.name: Property & Casualty Loss Cost & Trend Study
steps: Compile historical paid and incurred loss data by line, coverage, and accident year
Develop and select loss development factors for tail completion
Calculate accident-year ultimate losses and loss ratios by coverage
Compute frequency trend rates using policy count-adjusted claim counts
Compute severity trend rates using developed average paid loss amounts
Identify external trend drivers (social inflation, medical CPI, litigation environment)
Apply claim count adjustment for changes in deductible distribution and retention
Derive pure premium trend rates for use in pricing indication models
Benchmark company trends against ISO, Verisk, and competitor data where available
Document trend selection rationale and sensitivity analysis
Present trend study findings to Pricing and Reserving Committees
Update trend assumption register with selected rates and effective dates

subProcesses.name: Expense Analysis & Allocation Study
steps: Extract general ledger expense data by department, cost center, and expense category
Classify expenses into underwriting acquisition, loss adjustment (ULAE/ALAE), and overhead categories
Develop expense allocation keys (premium, payroll, headcount, claims count) by cost driver
Compute expense ratios by line of business and distribution channel
Benchmark company expense ratios against industry peers using NAIC annual statement data
Identify expense categories with adverse year-over-year variance and investigate drivers
Coordinate with Finance to validate expense classification for statutory filing
Incorporate expense analysis results into pricing expense loads
Produce ULAE and ALAE factor study for reserve expense loading
Present expense study findings to CFO and Chief Actuary
Document expense allocation methodology in actuarial standards register
Update pricing models with approved expense loads for next rate filing cycle

subProcesses.name: Assumption Governance & Change Management
steps: Maintain actuarial assumption register documenting all active pricing and valuation assumptions
Establish annual assumption review calendar aligned to financial close and pricing cycles
Coordinate multi-team assumption review process (Actuarial, Risk, Finance, Product)
Document proposed assumption changes with analysis, rationale, and financial impact
Route assumption change proposals through defined approval hierarchy (peer review, Chief Actuary, Board)
Assess materiality of assumption changes for financial statement disclosure
Record final approved assumptions with effective date and approver in governance register
Communicate approved changes to all downstream model users via formal release note
Perform post-implementation review of assumption changes against emerging experience
Maintain version history and change log for all actuarial assumptions
Report assumption change summary to Audit Committee annually
Ensure assumption documentation satisfies regulatory examination and internal audit requirements

subProcesses.name: Rate Indication & Profitability Analysis
steps: Define scope of rate review and identify lines of business in scope
Extract and reconcile policy, premium, and loss data from source systems
Calculate earned premium and on-level adjustment factors for rate changes
Develop loss development factors using paid and incurred triangles
Apply trend factors to project historical losses to future policy period
Compute indicated rate change by coverage, territory, and class
Assess expense ratios and target profit margins against indicated needs
Benchmark indicated rates against market and competitive rate intelligence
Perform sensitivity analysis on key assumptions (trend, development, LDF)
Document rate indication memorandum and actuarial certification
Present findings and recommendations to Pricing Committee
Obtain sign-off and transmit approved indications to Product Management

subProcesses.name: Multivariate & Predictive Rating Model Development
steps: Define rating model objectives, target variable, and business constraints
Extract and validate historical policy and loss data for model training
Perform exploratory data analysis and identify candidate rating variables
Apply credibility and homogeneity tests to candidate variables
Build generalized linear model (GLM) or machine-learning model on training data
Evaluate model performance using lift curves, Gini coefficient, and holdout validation
Review model outputs with underwriting for business reasonableness
Document model assumptions, variable definitions, and selection rationale
Obtain model validation sign-off from Model Risk Management or peer reviewer
Translate approved model relativities into rating algorithm for policy system
Coordinate UAT with IT to confirm implemented factors match approved model
Monitor post-deployment model performance and schedule refresh cycle

subProcesses.name: Portfolio Performance & Assumption Refresh
steps: Compile quarter-end portfolio data by product, segment, and distribution channel
Compare actual loss ratios and frequency-severity trends to prior assumptions
Identify segments with material deviation from plan or prior period
Analyze policy count, retention, new business, and mix-of-business shifts
Review large-loss activity and catastrophe impacts on reported results
Update frequency and severity trend assumptions based on credibility-weighted data
Refresh expense and commission load assumptions with Finance input
Produce management report showing actual vs. expected across all segments
Escalate adverse segments to Pricing Committee for corrective action review
Archive updated assumptions in assumption governance register
Communicate refreshed assumptions to reserving and capital modeling teams
Obtain appointed actuary acknowledgment of assumption changes

subProcesses.name: Underwriting Guideline & Appetite Calibration
steps: Gather loss ratio and selection data segmented by risk characteristics
Identify underperforming risk segments using profitability heat maps
Consult with underwriting to understand current guideline intent and exceptions
Quantify financial impact of guideline relaxation or tightening scenarios
Propose revised appetite boundaries supported by actuarial analysis
Model premium and profit impact of proposed guideline changes
Present recommendations to Underwriting Leadership and Chief Actuary
Draft revised underwriting guidelines incorporating actuarial recommendations
Obtain approval from Underwriting Committee and document decision rationale
Communicate final guidelines to field underwriters with effective date
Monitor new-business quality metrics post-implementation
Schedule six-month follow-up review to assess guideline effectiveness

subProcesses.name: Reinsurance Pricing & Treaty Support
steps: Compile ceded premium, loss, and exposure statistics for treaty year
Develop loss development factors specific to ceded layers and attachment points
Calculate burning cost and expected loss ratio for treaty renewal
Model excess and catastrophe layer costs using internal and vendor models
Prepare actuarial support package for reinsurance brokers and markets
Evaluate reinsurer pricing proposals against internal benchmarks
Perform cost-benefit analysis on alternative treaty structures (quota share vs. XL)
Advise Reinsurance team on optimal retention levels and treaty terms
Produce post-bind actuarial summary documenting treaty pricing basis
Monitor in-force treaty loss development versus pricing assumptions
Update ceded loss estimates at each reserve cycle for treaty settlements
Report treaty performance to Chief Actuary and Finance quarterly

subProcesses.name: Rate Filing & Regulatory Submission
steps: Identify states and lines of business requiring rate or form filings
Compile actuarial support package including indication, certification, and exhibits
Draft actuarial memorandum explaining methodology and data sources
Complete state-specific filing templates (SERFF or equivalent system)
Obtain actuarial sign-off and appointed actuary certification where required
Submit rate filing to state insurance department via SERFF
Track filing status and respond to departmental objections or questions
Negotiate rate approval with regulators as needed
Receive and document regulatory approval or withdrawal decision
Coordinate with Product Management to implement approved rates in policy system
Archive approved filing documents in compliance record management system
Monitor effective dates and schedule next review cycle per state regulations

subProcesses.name: Reserve Setting & Booking
steps: Extract and reconcile claims data from claims management and financial systems
Verify data completeness, consistency, and prior-period reconciliation
Construct paid and incurred loss development triangles by line and accident year
Analyze development patterns and select volume-weighted or age-to-ultimate factors
Apply multiple actuarial methods (chain-ladder, BF, Clark, Cape Cod) to develop ultimates
Assess method credibility and select indicated reserve estimates by segment
Compare selected estimates to prior quarter and document change drivers
Calculate IBNR and total reserve requirement by line of business
Prepare reserve journal entry for Finance booking and reconcile to GL
Book reserves in financial system and flag any entries requiring CFO approval
Document analysis in reserve exhibit and actuarial work papers
Present reserve indications and key drivers to Chief Reserve Actuary

subProcesses.name: Life & Annuity Statutory Valuation (PBR)
steps: Extract in-force policy records and validate against administration system controls
Confirm credibility of company experience for assumption-setting under PBR framework
Calculate net premium reserve (NPR) for each policy using prescribed assumptions
Run deterministic and stochastic reserve calculations using actuarial projection model
Perform asset adequacy analysis and cash flow testing under prescribed scenarios
Stress test reserves under adverse mortality, lapse, and interest rate scenarios
Reconcile PBR reserve to GAAP and prior-year statutory reserve
Document PBR assumptions, methodology, and sensitivity results
Obtain Appointed Actuary review and sign-off on PBR methodology
Prepare and file Actuarial Memorandum with state domicile regulator
Complete Life and Health Actuarial Opinion Memorandum (AOM)
Archive valuation documentation in regulatory compliance repository

subProcesses.name: GAAP Long-Duration Targeted Improvements (LDTI) Reserving
steps: Define cohort groupings and measurement dates for ASC 944-40 compliance
Extract contract-level cash flow data and policyholder benefit projections from administration system
Select and lock-in discount rates at contract inception using upper-medium-grade fixed-income yields
Calculate present value of future benefits and present value of future premiums by cohort
Compute net premium ratio (NPR) and flag cohorts where NPR exceeds 100%
Apply current discount rate to remeasure liability at each reporting date and record OCI impact
Run annual assumption update unlocking process and record change through net income
Reconcile LDTI reserve to prior GAAP reserve and document transition adjustment in equity
Validate model output against manual spot-check calculations for selected cohorts
Prepare LDTI roll-forward exhibits for financial statement disclosure
Coordinate with Finance on LDTI journal entries and balance sheet presentation
Archive LDTI model runs, assumptions, and supporting documentation with version control

subProcesses.name: Unexpired Risk & Unearned Premium Reserve Analysis
steps: Extract unearned premium reserve (UPR) by line, product, and underwriting year from financial system
Calculate loss ratio required to extinguish unearned premium for each line
Compare anticipated loss and expense ratio to unearned premium reserve adequacy
Compute premium deficiency reserve (PDR) where anticipated losses exceed UPR
Identify lines or segments requiring premium deficiency recognition under ASC 944-60
Coordinate with Finance on PDR journal entry calculation and booking
Assess reinsurance recoverables attributable to unexpired risk and adjust ceded PDR
Review pro-rata vs. 24ths vs. daily earning basis and confirm appropriateness by line
Document PDR analysis, methodology, and comparison to prior period
Present unexpired risk findings to Chief Reserve Actuary and CFO
File premium deficiency disclosures in statutory annual statement as required
Archive UPR and PDR analysis work papers with financial close documentation

subProcesses.name: Reserve Adequacy Review & Actuarial Opinion
steps: Perform reserve roll-forward analysis comparing opening to closing reserve balance
Quantify favorable and adverse development by accident year and line
Review reserve adequacy ratios (paid-to-incurred, reserve-to-premium)
Conduct independent peer review of reserve selections by senior actuary
Assess whether carried reserves fall within range of reasonable estimates
Prepare draft Statement of Actuarial Opinion (SAO) or Certification
Coordinate with external actuarial firm for Appointed Actuary opinion where required
Issue final signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion and supporting memorandum
Present reserve opinion and adequacy findings to Reserve Committee
Report material reserve changes to Audit Committee with root-cause explanation
File SAO with state regulators per statutory filing deadlines
Maintain opinion documentation in compliance archive for regulatory examination

subProcesses.name: Reinsurance Recoverable & Ceded Reserve Management
steps: Identify all open claims with reinsurance treaty or facultative coverage attachments
Calculate gross and ceded reserve estimates by treaty layer and accident year
Reconcile ceded reserves to reinsurance accounts receivable in the general ledger
Notify reinsurers of claims approaching or piercing treaty attachment points
Prepare ceded loss development triangles for each active treaty
Monitor collection status of outstanding reinsurance recoverables
Assess collectability and provision for uncollectible reinsurance per statutory requirements
Coordinate with Reinsurance and Finance on commutation negotiations and reserve releases
Produce quarterly ceded reserve report for Finance and Reinsurance teams
Reconcile ceded reserve movements to reinsurance settlement statements
Support external audit of reinsurance recoverables with actuarial documentation
Archive ceded reserve analysis and treaty correspondence for regulatory examination

subProcesses.name: Actuarial Triangle Construction & Data Validation
steps: Define accident year, report year, and calendar year cut-offs for triangle construction
Extract cumulative paid and incurred loss data from claims system by line and accident year
Verify extract totals against financial general ledger for each evaluation period
Identify and isolate large losses above reporting threshold for separate analysis
Adjust triangles for portfolio mix changes, reinsurance program changes, and rate shifts
Apply development factor selection methods and document age-to-age factor patterns
Review tail factor selection and benchmark against industry development schedules
Reconcile current-quarter triangles to prior-quarter with explanation of changes
Produce final triangle exhibits with data quality certification for sign-off
Distribute validated triangle package to Reserving, Pricing, and Capital teams
Archive triangle extract files with timestamp and source system version
Maintain triangle library in version-controlled actuarial data repository

subProcesses.name: Reserve Development Monitoring & Experience Tracking
steps: Produce monthly paid and incurred loss development report by accident year
Identify accident years with development materially above or below expectation
Analyze claim count development versus loss dollar development for frequency-severity insights
Track closure rates, open claim inventory, and average open reserve per file
Assess impact of claims handling changes or process shifts on development patterns
Benchmark development factors against industry data (e.g., ISO, AM Best schedules)
Prepare calendar-year vs. accident-year loss analysis for Finance reporting
Identify potential need for reserve strengthening or release based on tracking
Distribute experience tracking report to Reserving, Pricing, and Finance teams
Update reserve monitoring dashboard and flag metrics outside control limits
Incorporate development trends into next quarter reserve indication cycle
Document significant pattern changes in assumption change log

subProcesses.name: Large Loss & Latent Exposure Management
steps: Monitor claims in excess of large-loss reporting threshold in real time
Flag claims approaching or exceeding per-occurrence or aggregate treaty attachments
Conduct actuarial review of claims with potential for adverse development (asbestos, opioids, PFAS)
Establish individual case reserves for large losses using actuarial benchmarking
Coordinate with Claims and Legal on litigation strategy for significant exposures
Model aggregate latent liability exposure using industry development patterns
Report large-loss activity and emerging trends to Chief Reserve Actuary monthly
Assess reinsurance recoverability and prepare ceded reserve estimates
Update IBNR loading for latent exposures based on emerging claim counts
Disclose large-loss and latent reserve uncertainty in financial statement footnotes
Escalate systemic exposure concerns to Executive Risk Committee
Archive large-loss reserve analysis and supporting documentation

subProcesses.name: Prior-Year Development Analysis
steps: Extract accident-year reserve positions at current and prior year-end evaluation dates
Calculate calendar-year paid and case-reserve development by accident year and line
Classify development as favorable or adverse and quantify in dollars and loss-ratio points
Attribute development to claim count changes, severity changes, and case reserve adequacy shifts
Identify accident years driving the largest absolute development amounts
Compare development magnitude to reserve margin held at prior year-end
Assess whether prior-year development signals a systemic estimation bias in reserving methods
Prepare prior-year development exhibit for annual statement Schedule P disclosure
Discuss findings with Chief Reserve Actuary and document root-cause explanations
Communicate material prior-year development to Finance and Investor Relations before earnings release
Incorporate prior-year development lessons into current-year reserve selection process
Archive prior-year development analysis in statutory filing documentation

subProcesses.name: Reserve Uncertainty & Range of Reasonable Estimates Analysis
steps: Define range of reasonable estimates framework aligned to ASOP No. 36 guidance
Select actuarial methods and parameter variations for high, central, and low scenarios
Run reserve calculations under each scenario combination to produce a distribution of outcomes
Compute coefficient of variation and interquartile range of reserve estimates by line
Assess process uncertainty (random claims fluctuation) separately from parameter uncertainty
Quantify model uncertainty by comparing results across chain-ladder, BF, and stochastic methods
Determine whether carried reserve falls within the range and document adequacy conclusion
Stress-test reserve range under adverse development scenarios for risk capital inputs
Present range analysis to Reserve Committee with narrative explanation of key drivers
Include reserve range disclosure in Statement of Actuarial Opinion Memorandum
Provide uncertainty metrics to Capital Modeling team for internal model calibration
Archive range of reasonable estimates analysis as part of reserve documentation package

subProcesses.name: Claims Closure Rate & Open Inventory Analysis
steps: Extract open and closed claim counts by accident year, line, and claim type at each evaluation
Compute closure rates by accident year and compare to historical closure pace
Identify accident years or lines with unusually slow or accelerated closure patterns
Analyze average open reserve per file by age of claim and claim type
Assess impact of litigation activity and jurisdiction mix on closure pace
Evaluate effects of claims department staffing changes or process initiatives on closure rates
Correlate closure rate changes with reserve development trends for predictive insight
Produce open inventory aging report segmented by claim status and handling unit
Flag claims open beyond expected duration for supervisory review
Coordinate findings with Claims Operations to align reserve assumptions with operational trends
Incorporate closure rate analysis into frequency-severity reserve methodology adjustments
Archive claims inventory and closure rate reports at each quarter-end evaluation

subProcesses.name: Exposure Data Preparation & Validation
steps: Extract policy-level exposure data from policy administration system for cat model input
Validate completeness of key attributes: location, construction, occupancy, year built
Geocode property addresses to highest available geographic resolution
Apply data quality scoring and flag policies with missing or imputed attributes
Resolve geocoding failures through address standardization and manual review
Classify and code construction and occupancy attributes using cat vendor data dictionaries
Reconcile total insured value (TIV) to in-force premium and underwriting reports
Produce exposure data quality report and distribute to Underwriting and Cat Modeling
Archive validated exposure extract with data quality metadata and timestamp
Coordinate data remediation plan with Underwriting for persistent data quality gaps
Rerun validation after remediation and confirm improvement against prior period
Deliver validated exposure file to cat modeling platform for analysis

subProcesses.name: Natural Catastrophe Model Execution
steps: Configure cat model run parameters (peril, region, return period, financial terms) in RMS/AIR/CoreLogic
Import validated exposure file into cat modeling platform
Execute event set simulations for applicable natural perils (hurricane, earthquake, flood, severe convective storm, wildfire)
Review model output for completeness and reasonableness against prior runs
Apply secondary uncertainty adjustments and demand surge factors
Produce per-occurrence and aggregate exceedance probability (OEP/AEP) curves
Calculate probable maximum loss (PML) at selected return periods (100, 250, 500-year)
Calculate average annual loss (AAL) by peril, region, and line of business
Validate modeled vs. actual losses for major historical events in company portfolio
Produce cat model summary report with PML, AAL, and accumulation metrics
Distribute results to Reinsurance, Capital Modeling, and Underwriting teams
Archive model run configurations, input files, and output reports for audit trail

subProcesses.name: Man-Made & Emerging Peril Modeling
steps: Identify man-made and emerging perils relevant to portfolio (cyber, terror, NBCR, pandemic)
Source third-party models or develop simplified internal models for each identified peril
Collect exposure data relevant to each man-made peril (e.g., employee count for cyber, occupancy density for terror)
Run man-made cat model scenarios and accumulation analyses
Assess concentration risk in high-density locations (CBD, critical infrastructure)
Estimate potential insured loss for defined scenarios and stress events
Overlay man-made exposure results on natural cat accumulation maps
Quantify correlation between man-made and natural cat events for aggregate modeling
Report man-made peril exposure summaries to Risk Committee and Underwriting
Incorporate man-made peril losses into capital model as stress scenario inputs
Monitor emerging peril trends and update modeling approach annually
Document model limitations and uncertainty in man-made peril modeling report

subProcesses.name: Accumulation & Concentration Risk Management
steps: Define geographic accumulation zones and risk concentration limits by zone and peril
Aggregate TIV by zone using validated exposure file and geocoded data
Compare zone accumulations to approved limits in underwriting appetite statement
Identify zones approaching or exceeding concentration limits
Calculate net and gross accumulations reflecting reinsurance treaty and per-risk coverage
Produce accumulation heat maps for Property, Marine, and Engineering portfolios
Report zone limit breaches and near-miss situations to Underwriting Leadership
Recommend underwriting action (restrict binding, increase pricing load) for over-limit zones
Monitor intra-quarter accumulation changes via real-time or weekly exposure feeds
Update concentration limits annually based on capital model and reinsurance program
Coordinate with Reinsurance to ensure treaty aggregate limits accommodate modeled PML
Archive accumulation snapshots at each month-end for regulatory and audit review

subProcesses.name: Reinsurance Structure Optimization
steps: Provide gross PML and AAL inputs to Reinsurance team for treaty renewal planning
Model alternative reinsurance structures (layer attachment, limit, reinstatements) in cat platform
Calculate net retained PML under each proposed reinsurance structure
Evaluate cost efficiency of each structure using ROL, payback period, and risk-transfer metrics
Stress-test proposed structure against multi-event and aggregate scenarios
Recommend optimal treaty structure balancing risk transfer cost and retained volatility
Coordinate with Capital Modeling team to ensure net PML reflects capital adequacy requirements
Advise Reinsurance on aggregate cover attachment points based on modeled annual aggregate loss distribution
Prepare actuarial briefing for broker and reinsurer negotiations with supporting cat data
Review bound treaty terms to confirm structure matches actuarial recommendation
Monitor mid-year net PML against treaty attachment and flag if gross PML exceeds treaty capacity
Document optimization methodology, structure selection rationale, and sensitivity results

subProcesses.name: PML Reporting & Regulatory Disclosure
steps: Compile final net and gross PML metrics at selected return periods following treaty bind
Produce PML report for rating agencies, regulators, and Board Risk Committee
Prepare catastrophe exhibit for statutory Annual Statement (e.g., NAIC cat exhibit)
Complete AM Best, S&P, and Moody's catastrophe exposure questionnaires with modeled PML data
Draft catastrophe risk narrative for ORSA report and annual filing
Coordinate with Finance on catastrophe reserve disclosures in financial statement footnotes
Respond to regulator requests for cat modeling methodology and assumption documentation
Prepare post-event regulatory notifications (state DOI, NAIC) for qualifying cat events
Support broker and reinsurer presentations with cat modeling data packages
Produce post-event actuarial report analyzing model accuracy vs. actual outcomes
Incorporate event learnings into cat model calibration and assumption update process
Archive all PML reports, regulatory submissions, and rating agency correspondence

subProcesses.name: Post-Event Loss Estimation & Response
steps: Activate post-event response protocol upon declaration of significant catastrophe event
Extract in-force exposure from policy system for affected geographic footprint
Run post-event cat model using industry-loss reports (PCS, PERILS) and event parameters
Apply event-specific vulnerability functions and secondary uncertainty to modeled losses
Produce preliminary gross and net loss estimate for Executive team within 48-72 hours
Monitor claims emergence and compare actual to modeled development weekly
Refine loss estimate at 30, 60, and 90-day intervals as claims data matures
Assess reinsurance recoverable and notify treaty reinsurers of potential loss event
Coordinate with Finance on GAAP and statutory reserve booking for cat event
Prepare regulatory notifications (state DOI, NAIC) for qualifying cat events
Produce post-event actuarial report analyzing model accuracy vs. actual outcomes
Incorporate event learnings into cat model calibration and assumption update process

subProcesses.name: Internal Economic Capital Modeling
steps: Define internal capital model scope, risk modules, and modeling period for current cycle
Collect and validate inputs: exposure, reserve, investment, and counterparty data
Calibrate risk module parameters (underwriting, market, credit, operational) to current portfolio
Run internal capital model using stochastic or deterministic simulation to compute required capital
Calculate available capital from balance sheet and reconcile to economic surplus
Compute economic capital coverage ratio and assess adequacy against internal risk appetite
Validate internal model outputs against prior period and internal benchmark scenarios
Produce ICAAP or ORSA capital assessment narrative and quantitative exhibits
Obtain sign-off from Chief Actuary and Chief Risk Officer on internal capital position
Report economic capital adequacy results to Board Risk and Capital Committee
Archive internal capital model documentation, assumptions, and audit trail
Review model calibration annually and update for portfolio changes or new risk exposures

subProcesses.name: Regulatory Capital & RBC Computation
steps: Identify applicable regulatory capital framework (NAIC RBC, Solvency II, or equivalent) for each entity
Extract risk components (underwriting, credit, market, operational) required by the regulatory formula
Apply NAIC RBC formula or equivalent regulatory calculation to compute required capital
Calculate total adjusted capital (TAC) or available capital under statutory accounting
Compute solvency coverage ratios (RBC ratio, ECR-to-SCR) under the regulatory base scenario
Reconcile RBC components to audited statutory financial statements
Coordinate with Appointed Actuary to confirm reserve inputs used in RBC calculation
Prepare RBC report schedules and exhibits for Annual Statement filing
Support Solvency II or equivalent group reporting requirements for international entities
File ORSA Summary Report sections assigned to Actuarial with domicile regulator
Respond to state regulator requests for capital clarification during examination
Track regulatory changes to capital requirements and assess impact on formula and ratio

subProcesses.name: Stress & Scenario Testing
steps: Agree annual stress-testing program with Risk Committee including scenario selection criteria
Design deterministic stress scenarios (e.g., 1-in-200 hurricane, interest rate shock, pandemic)
Design reverse-stress scenarios to identify conditions that breach solvency threshold
Collect scenario-specific inputs from underwriting, investment, and claims teams
Run stress calculations in capital model and compute post-stress capital position
Apply management actions (reinsurance, capital raise, dividend suspension) to stressed position
Analyze capital adequacy and liquidity implications under each stress scenario
Benchmark results against prior year and industry peer stress outcomes
Prepare stress testing report with executive summary and management action plan
Present stress results and conclusions to Risk Committee and Board
Incorporate stress outcomes into ORSA and ICAAP disclosures
Update scenario library and stress severity assumptions based on emerging risks

subProcesses.name: Reinsurance Capital Credit & Counterparty Assessment
steps: Identify all reinsurance recoverables and map to counterparty credit ratings
Calculate reinsurance capital credit under RBC or internal model framework
Assess counterparty default probability and recovery assumption for each reinsurer
Apply counterparty concentration limits per risk appetite framework
Compute net RBC charge for reinsurance recoverables and flag exposures above threshold
Monitor rating agency and financial strength actions on key reinsurance counterparties
Coordinate with Reinsurance team to diversify counterparty risk where concentration exists
Model impact of reinsurer default on capital position under stress scenarios
Report counterparty credit risk summary to Risk and Capital Committee quarterly
Update reinsurance counterparty register with current ratings and recoverable balances
Document counterparty assessment methodology in capital model documentation
Review and update counterparty risk policy annually with Chief Risk Officer

subProcesses.name: Capital Allocation & Internal Transfer Pricing
steps: Define capital allocation methodology (e.g., marginal, co-variance, risk-based) with Finance
Calculate divisional capital requirement using allocated capital model outputs
Produce capital allocation results by line of business, product, and geography
Compute risk-adjusted return on capital (RAROC) by business unit
Compare RAROC to cost-of-capital hurdle and identify value-creating vs. destroying segments
Facilitate capital allocation review with CFO, Business Unit Leaders, and Chief Actuary
Document capital allocation rationale and model methodology in governance register
Embed allocated capital into business unit financial plans and pricing targets
Monitor actual capital consumption against allocation plan each quarter
Provide reallocation recommendations where actual vs. plan diverges materially
Support Finance in internal transfer pricing for intercompany reinsurance arrangements
Review capital allocation methodology annually and update for portfolio changes

subProcesses.name: Dividend & Capital Distribution Analysis
steps: Model projected capital position over 3-5 year planning horizon
Calculate excess capital above regulatory and internal minimum thresholds
Assess impact of planned growth, acquisitions, and reinsurance on capital requirement
Estimate maximum distributable dividend under state insurance holding company law
Stress-test proposed dividend against adverse scenarios to confirm post-distribution adequacy
Coordinate with Treasury and Finance on dividend timing and form (cash vs. securities)
Prepare actuarial capital adequacy opinion supporting dividend declaration
Submit dividend notification or approval filing to state regulator as required
Document dividend decision rationale and capital adequacy demonstration
Monitor post-dividend capital trajectory against plan each quarter
Report actual vs. projected capital to Board on quarterly basis
Flag any post-distribution capital deterioration for immediate escalation

subProcesses.name: Actuarial Data Quality Management
steps: Define data quality standards for actuarial triangles and valuation datasets
Execute automated data validation checks at each quarter-end extract
Reconcile actuarial source data to financial general ledger and statutory exhibits
Investigate and resolve data anomalies with IT Operations and source system owners
Maintain mapping tables for lines of business, claim type, and cause-of-loss codes used in actuarial models
Document data lineage from source system to actuarial model inputs
Validate prior-period restatements and rerun prior triangles as needed
Coordinate with IT on system changes that affect actuarial data feeds
Archive validated actuarial datasets with version control and access controls
Train actuarial analysts on data governance standards and validation procedures
Produce actuarial data quality scorecard and report exceptions to Chief Actuary
Review and update actuarial data quality standards annually or after system changes

subProcesses.name: Statutory Actuarial Opinion & Certification
steps: Identify all entities requiring Appointed Actuary opinion under state law
Confirm Appointed Actuary credentials, MAAA designation, and company appointment letters
Collect reserve analyses, assumption documentation, and asset adequacy reports for all entities
Review reserve adequacy and asset adequacy conclusions across all statutory entities
Prepare draft Actuarial Opinion and, where required, Actuarial Opinion Memorandum (AOM)
Conduct quality review of draft opinion with peer actuary and General Counsel
Sign and date final Actuarial Opinion for inclusion in Annual Statement
File signed Actuarial Opinion with state insurance departments by statutory deadlines
Coordinate with external auditors on reserve-related audit procedures and sign-offs
Maintain appointment letter and credentials documentation in compliance files
Track multi-state filing deadlines and confirm receipt of filed opinions
Archive signed opinions, supporting memoranda, and regulator correspondence

subProcesses.name: Financial Reporting & Actuarial Disclosure
steps: Prepare actuarial exhibits for GAAP financial statements (ASC 944, LDTI reserve disclosures)
Produce statutory reserve and actuarial liability schedules for Annual Statement filing
Calculate and disclose Loss Development information in Schedule P (P&C) or equivalent
Prepare actuarial narrative for Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A)
Coordinate with Finance on GAAP vs. statutory reconciliation of actuarial liabilities
Support external auditors with actuarial work papers, methodology descriptions, and data
Prepare actuarial components of SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q) for publicly traded entities
Review draft financial statements for actuarial accuracy before CFO certification
Respond to auditor queries on reserve methodology, assumption selection, and adequacy
Ensure LDTI cohort definitions, measurement dates, and discount rates comply with ASC 944-40
Distribute final actuarial exhibits to Finance, Audit, and Investor Relations teams
Archive financial reporting actuarial work papers with controlled access

subProcesses.name: Actuarial Model Governance & Validation
steps: Maintain inventory of all actuarial models (pricing, reserving, capital, cat) with risk tier classification
Define model validation standards aligned to ASOP No. 56 and Model Risk Management policy
Schedule periodic independent validation reviews for Tier 1 and Tier 2 actuarial models
Execute model validation including conceptual soundness, data review, and outcome analysis
Document validation findings, model deficiencies, and remediation plans
Track model deficiency remediation to closure with target dates and responsible owners
Review and approve all model changes using formal change control process
Maintain model version control and ensure production models are locked against unauthorized changes
Produce model governance report for Chief Actuary, CRO, and Audit Committee quarterly
Coordinate with Internal Audit on actuarial model audit scope and findings
Ensure model documentation satisfies regulatory examination standards
Update model governance policy annually reflecting regulatory and ASOP guidance changes

subProcesses.name: Actuarial Standards & Professional Compliance
steps: Monitor new and revised Actuarial Standards of Practice (ASOPs) from the Actuarial Standards Board
Assess applicability and impact of new ASOPs on company actuarial practices and methods
Update internal actuarial practice standards to conform with revised ASOPs
Maintain records of Continuing Education (CE) credits for all credentialed actuarial staff
Coordinate compliance with AAA and relevant actuarial membership organization requirements
Conduct annual self-assessment of actuarial practice standards compliance
Review and approve all external actuarial communications (opinions, certifications, reports)
Maintain disciplinary and professional conduct policies for actuarial staff
Facilitate peer review program for all material actuarial analyses per ASOP guidance
Report professional compliance status to Chief Actuary and Board Risk Committee
Coordinate with Legal on disciplinary matters involving actuarial professional standards
Archive actuarial credentials, CE records, and professional compliance documentation

subProcesses.name: Actuarial Planning, Budgeting & Resource Management
steps: Develop annual actuarial work plan aligned to business planning and financial close calendar
Estimate actuarial resource requirements by function (pricing, reserving, capital, cat)
Identify capacity gaps and plan resourcing through hiring, contractor, or vendor engagement
Prepare Actuarial department budget including staff, systems, data, and consulting costs
Coordinate with HR on actuarial exam program support, study time, and progression policies
Monitor actual vs. budgeted actuarial spend quarterly and explain material variances
Prioritize actuarial project pipeline with Chief Actuary and business stakeholders
Track actuarial project delivery against agreed milestones and report status to leadership
Conduct actuarial staff performance reviews and career development planning
Maintain succession plan for key actuarial roles including Appointed Actuary
Evaluate and procure actuarial software, data, and vendor model subscriptions
Report actuarial capacity and delivery performance to Chief Actuary quarterly

subProcesses.name: Board & Executive Actuarial Reporting
steps: Prepare quarterly actuarial dashboard for Chief Actuary presentation to Board Risk Committee
Summarize reserve adequacy, capital position, and cat exposure in executive briefing format
Develop emerging risk actuarial briefing for Board covering material assumption changes
Coordinate CEO and CFO sign-off on actuarial components of Board reports
Produce annual actuarial report to Board summarizing key study results and assumption changes
Present catastrophe PML and modeled loss scenarios to Board in accessible narrative form
Report pricing adequacy and rate action summary to Board via CEO/CFO escalation
Respond to Board and Audit Committee questions on actuarial methodology and adequacy
Coordinate with Investor Relations on actuarial disclosures for earnings releases
Prepare actuarial sections of Annual Report to shareholders
Maintain archive of all actuarial Board materials with version control
Calibrate Board reporting format annually based on Board and regulator feedback

subProcesses.name: Loss Notice Receipt & Channel Management
steps: Receive loss notice via phone, web portal, mobile app, or agent channel
Authenticate caller or submitter identity against policy records
Log the initial loss notification with date, time, and channel captured
Issue an immediate claim number and provide it to the reporting party
Apply catastrophe event coding when a CAT declaration or surge alert is active
Route CAT-coded notices to the surge-handling queue and dedicated CAT adjuster pool
Confirm receipt with an automated acknowledgment containing claim number and next steps
Store raw FNOL data in the claims management system for downstream processing

subProcesses.name: Incident Detail Capture & Documentation
steps: Capture incident date, time, and location with GPS coordinates where applicable
Record a structured description of the loss cause and sequence of events
Document involved parties including claimants, witnesses, and third parties
Collect initial loss estimates and property descriptions from the reporting party
Attach photographs, video, or telematics data submitted at first notice
Record law enforcement, fire department, or emergency responder report numbers
Populate all mandatory state-specific FNOL data fields required for regulatory reporting
Confirm completeness of intake record and flag gaps for follow-up contact

subProcesses.name: Initial Severity Assessment & Claim Assignment
steps: Assess initial severity of the loss using structured triage criteria and reserve benchmarks
Classify the claim into complexity tier: fast-track, standard, complex, or large-loss
Apply catastrophe, mass-tort, or major-account flags as warranted
Determine whether emergency mitigation, board-up, or emergency housing is needed
Apply assignment rules based on line of business, territory, and complexity tier
Assign the claim to a licensed adjuster with appropriate line authority and set diary dates
Notify the insured of the assigned handler's name and contact information
Set initial reserves based on severity tier and document triage decision in the claim file

subProcesses.name: Claims Workflow Routing & Escalation
steps: Apply workflow routing rules to direct the claim to the appropriate handling track
Escalate large-loss or complex claims to senior adjusters or claim management review
Route bodily-injury claims to BI specialists and structured-settlement consultants
Flag claims meeting litigation thresholds for proactive legal unit notification
Trigger SIU referral when fraud indicators are identified during coverage or liability review
Assign catastrophe claims to CAT-team adjusters and CAT management oversight
Set escalation diary dates and ensure management review occurs within required windows
Document routing decisions and escalation rationale in the claim audit trail

subProcesses.name: Catastrophe Event Activation & Command Setup
steps: Receive and validate the CAT declaration or surge trigger from the meteorological or event source
Activate the CAT response plan and notify the CAT command team and executive leadership
Establish the CAT command center with dedicated triage queues and communication protocols
Apply regulatory extended-compliance timeframes applicable to the catastrophe declaration
Mobilize CAT-team adjusters, independent adjusters, and vendor networks for the affected region
Stand up the CAT intake hotline and digital self-service channels for the affected policyholders
Issue policyholder communications with claim-filing instructions and emergency contact information
Log the CAT event declaration and activation actions in the claims management system

subProcesses.name: CAT Field Operations & Loss Aggregation Management
steps: Deploy field adjusters and independent appraisers to the affected geography with prioritized routing
Conduct drive-by and aerial inspections to triage total-loss versus repairable properties
Establish daily CAT claim-volume, reserve, and payment-velocity reporting cadence
Coordinate with reinsurance operations on catastrophe aggregate loss reporting and threshold tracking
Monitor CAT reserve adequacy at the event aggregate level and escalate deterioration promptly
Report CAT loss estimates to actuarial, finance, and executive leadership on the defined cadence
Track open CAT claims against regulatory closure-timeline requirements for the affected states
Conduct the post-CAT event review to capture process improvements for future activations

subProcesses.name: Policy Identification & Coverage Verification
steps: Match the reported loss to the in-force policy using policy number, insured name, or VIN
Confirm policy effective and expiration dates bracket the date of loss
Retrieve the policy declarations page and applicable endorsements
Verify policy coverage types applicable to the loss against the declarations page
Identify named insureds, additional insureds, and loss payees on the policy
Confirm premium currency and absence of non-payment cancellation
Flag the policy for mid-term audit or endorsement check if coverage facts are unclear
Document the preliminary coverage confirmation in the claim file

subProcesses.name: Coverage Analysis & Position Determination
steps: Review policy documents in full, including declarations, forms, endorsements, and exclusions
Map reported loss details to policy insuring agreements to evaluate coverage applicability
Identify exclusions and conditions that may limit or bar coverage for the reported loss
Research applicable jurisdiction's coverage interpretation case law and regulatory guidance
Consult coverage counsel for ambiguous policy language or novel fact patterns
Determine coverage position as covered, potentially covered, or denied with documented basis
Draft the reservation-of-rights letter when coverage issues exist but investigation continues
Issue coverage position communication to the insured within regulatory timeframes

subProcesses.name: Reservation of Rights Administration
steps: Identify all open coverage questions that warrant a reservation-of-rights letter
Draft or update the ROR letter citing specific policy provisions and coverage questions at issue
Obtain supervisory or coverage-counsel review before issuing the ROR communication
Issue the ROR letter to the insured within state-required acknowledgment timeframes
Set a diary to reassess coverage questions as the claim investigation develops
Withdraw or supplement the ROR letter when coverage questions are resolved
Document each ROR action and revision in the claim coverage log
Track open ROR letters in the claims system for regulatory compliance reporting

subProcesses.name: Multi-Party Coverage Coordination
steps: Identify all parties asserting coverage including named insureds, additional insureds, and tenders from adverse carriers
Evaluate the scope of coverage owed to each party under the policy terms and endorsements
Coordinate with other insurers where multiple policies or contribution issues arise
Respond to tenders of defense from other carriers within required timeframes
Assess priority of coverage obligations across primary, excess, and umbrella layers
Document the coverage allocation among contributing insurers in the claim file
Negotiate coverage-sharing agreements when multiple carriers share defense or indemnity obligations
Escalate unresolved multi-carrier coverage disputes to coverage counsel for resolution

subProcesses.name: Coverage Dispute & Denial Management
steps: Draft the coverage denial letter with specific policy language and factual basis cited
Review denial for compliance with state unfair claims practices act requirements
Obtain supervisory or legal review approval before issuing the denial
Issue the denial letter within state-mandated timeframes with required disclosures
Log the denial in the claims system and set follow-up for appeal or re-inquiry
Respond to insured's dispute or appeal with supplemental analysis and documentation
Re-evaluate the denial if new evidence or legal authority is presented
Escalate unresolved coverage disputes to coverage counsel for formal opinion

subProcesses.name: Coverage Counsel Referral & Opinion Management
steps: Identify claims requiring formal coverage-counsel engagement based on complexity or exposure thresholds
Prepare the coverage-referral memorandum with a summary of facts, policy language, and coverage questions
Select and retain coverage counsel with appropriate jurisdictional and line-of-business expertise
Provide counsel with complete claim file, policy documents, and investigation materials
Track counsel's opinion timeline against the regulatory contact-and-response deadline
Review and apply the coverage opinion to the claim handling and settlement strategy
Document the coverage opinion and its application in the claim file
Close the counsel referral file and retain the opinion per document-retention requirements

subProcesses.name: Investigation Plan Development
steps: Develop investigation plan tailored to the loss type, complexity, and coverage questions
Identify all evidence sources: physical site, documents, witnesses, and electronic data
Assign field investigation tasks to field adjusters, EAs, or independent adjusters
Determine whether specialist involvement is needed (engineer, cause-and-origin, accountant)
Set investigation milestones and diary dates for evidence gathering and expert reporting
Coordinate access arrangements with the insured, claimant, and third parties
Document the investigation plan in the claim file with accountabilities and deadlines
Update the plan as new facts emerge during the investigation

subProcesses.name: Recorded Statement & Witness Interview Management
steps: Identify all parties from whom recorded statements are needed including insured, claimant, and witnesses
Schedule recorded statement sessions and provide required advance notice per state statute
Conduct recorded statements using structured questioning to develop all material loss facts
Obtain written statements or sworn examinations under oath when policy provisions require
Authenticate recorded statement media and create verbatim transcripts for the claim file
Document witness contact details, availability, and relevance in the investigation log
Assess statement consistency against physical evidence and other collected accounts
Archive all recorded statements and transcripts in the claim file per retention requirements

subProcesses.name: Expert Assignment & Field Inspection Coordination
steps: Identify expert disciplines needed based on loss type: engineer, appraiser, cause-and-origin, or reconstructionist
Select and retain qualified experts through the approved vendor panel with appropriate credentials
Provide expert with loss facts, site-access authorization, and inspection scope instructions
Coordinate inspection access with the insured, public authorities, and opposing experts where applicable
Review expert preliminary findings and direct supplemental investigation when scope gaps exist
Obtain the final expert report and assess its conclusions against the claim facts
Brief defense counsel or coverage counsel on expert opinions when litigation is anticipated
File the expert report and assignment correspondence in the claim file

subProcesses.name: Liability Evaluation & Fault Determination
steps: Gather evidence including police reports, photos, statements, and scene documentation
Obtain expert assessments from engineers, appraisers, or reconstructionists as appropriate
Evaluate liability by mapping duty, breach, causation, and damages elements
Research jurisdictional negligence rules including comparative and contributory fault standards
Apportion fault across all involved parties based on evidence and legal standards
Assess defenses available to the insured and evaluate their viability
Document the liability determination with supporting rationale and evidence citations
Communicate the preliminary liability assessment to the insured and claimant as appropriate

subProcesses.name: Bodily Injury Evaluation & Medical Management
steps: Identify all bodily injury claimants and obtain HIPAA-compliant medical authorizations
Order and review medical records to establish injury causation, diagnosis, and treatment course
Assess permanency and future medical cost projections using evidence-based medical guidelines
Engage an independent medical examination or peer review when treating-provider opinions are disputed
Evaluate wage-loss and loss-of-earning-capacity claims against employment and vocational records
Assess non-economic damages including pain and suffering against jurisdictional jury-verdict data
Apply comparative-fault reductions to bodily injury damages where contributory negligence is established
Document the bodily injury evaluation summary and reserve recommendation in the claim file

subProcesses.name: Damage Assessment & Valuation
steps: Conduct or commission a physical inspection of damaged property or vehicle
Obtain repair estimates from licensed contractors, body shops, or preferred vendors
Assess damages using industry pricing tools, cost databases, and comparable sales data
Engage independent appraisers when estimates are disputed or property is complex
Determine actual cash value versus replacement cost value based on policy provisions
Calculate depreciation, betterment, and deductible to arrive at net payable amount
Review damage assessment for consistency with the reported cause of loss
Finalize the damage valuation and document in the claim file with supporting exhibits

subProcesses.name: Fraud Indicator Screening & SIU Referral
steps: Screen claim for fraud indicators using structured red-flag checklist and predictive model scores
Run automated link and network analysis to identify connections to known fraud rings
Flag fraud indicators for SIU screening before claim advancement
Review the flagged claim against SIU referral criteria and mandatory reporting thresholds
Complete the SIU referral form with supporting loss facts, policy history, and red-flag rationale
Obtain supervisor approval and submit the referral to the SIU intake queue
Confirm SIU receipt and log the referral date in the claim file
Set adjuster diary for SIU status updates and claim-hold coordination

subProcesses.name: SIU Investigation Planning & Assignment
steps: Receive SIU referral and acknowledge intake within the unit's service standard
Conduct initial file review to assess referral validity and investigation scope
Plan investigation by identifying evidence targets, subjects, and investigation methods
Assign the investigation to a licensed SIU investigator based on geography and specialty
Determine whether law enforcement notification or public agency coordination is required
Set investigation milestones, diary dates, and expected completion timeline
Coordinate with the handling adjuster on claim-hold status and communication strategy
Document the investigation plan and assignment in the SIU case management system

subProcesses.name: Field Investigation & Evidence Collection
steps: Conduct investigation through recorded statements, scene visits, and surveillance as authorized
Analyze evidence including documents, digital records, medical records, and financial data
Conduct network and link analysis on involved parties, providers, and claimants
Interview insured, claimants, witnesses, and third parties under appropriate legal authority
Obtain and authenticate documentary evidence including titles, receipts, and records
Engage forensic specialists for cause-and-origin, digital forensics, or handwriting analysis
Coordinate with law enforcement for criminal referrals and evidence preservation
Maintain chain-of-custody documentation for all physical and digital evidence collected

subProcesses.name: SIU Findings Analysis & Recommendation
steps: Analyze evidence gathered to assess the probability and nature of fraud or misrepresentation
Quantify recoverable amounts tied to proven fraud or inflated claims
Assess legal sufficiency of the evidence for a coverage denial or rescission action
Recommend action from the options: pay, deny, rescind, partial pay, or refer to prosecution
Draft the SIU investigation report with findings, evidence summary, and recommendation
Present findings to the handling adjuster, supervisor, and legal counsel as warranted
Coordinate restitution and recovery pathways with the subrogation team where applicable
File the investigation report and evidence package in the claim file for audit

subProcesses.name: Regulatory Fraud Reporting & Law Enforcement Coordination
steps: Compile the fraud-recovery referral dossier for state insurance department submission
Determine mandatory versus voluntary reporting obligations under the applicable state statute
Complete and submit the state fraud referral form within the required reporting window
Coordinate with law enforcement agencies on criminal referrals and prosecution support
Respond to law enforcement requests for records, statements, and expert witnesses
Track the status of criminal proceedings and update the claim file with case developments
Log all fraud reporting actions in the regulatory compliance tracking system
Close the SIU case and report outcomes to the fraud analytics and prevention team

subProcesses.name: SIU Case Closure & Fraud Analytics Reporting
steps: Close and report SIU findings to the handling adjuster with a final action recommendation
Update the claim file with the SIU disposition code and outcome classification
Document lessons learned and red-flag patterns identified during the investigation
Submit closed-case data to fraud analytics for model tuning and red-flag refinement
Notify the handling adjuster of claim-hold release or continued hold based on findings
Compile the SIU case metrics for the unit performance scorecard
Archive the SIU case file and all associated evidence per retention policy
Identify systemic fraud patterns and escalate to the fraud strategy and prevention team

subProcesses.name: Initial Reserve Establishment
steps: Set initial reserves based on triage severity tier, coverage facts, and initial damage assessment
Apply reserving guidelines for the applicable line of business and claim type
Establish separate reserve components for indemnity, expense, and litigation as warranted
Obtain required supervisory approval for reserves exceeding individual authority limits
Post the initial reserve to the claims financial system with effective date and handler ID
Document the reserving rationale and assumptions in the claim file
Set a diary date for the first reserve adequacy review per reserving guidelines
Notify actuarial of large-loss reserves exceeding the unit's large-loss threshold

subProcesses.name: Reserve Adequacy Review & Adjustment
steps: Review reserve adequacy at each significant claim development event
Update reserves and action plan when new facts materially change the exposure estimate
Reconcile the updated reserve against coverage limits, deductibles, and reinsurance thresholds
Obtain approval for reserve increases that exceed delegated authority
Document the basis for each reserve change with supporting evidence and analysis
Flag claims with deteriorating reserve trends for management review and casualty monitoring
Track reserve development history to support actuarial loss development analysis
Submit large-loss reserve updates to the excess and reinsurance notification queue

subProcesses.name: Ceded-Loss Notification to Reinsurance
steps: Identify claims exceeding treaty or facultative retention and reinsurance attachment points
Issue timely reinsurance loss notice per treaty reporting requirements and deadlines
Calculate the reinsurer's proportional share of indemnity, expense, and reserve
Maintain the reinsurance correspondence file and track reinsurer acknowledgments
Respond to reinsurer queries on covered losses, reserves, and claim development
Diary the reinsurer notification and confirmation deadlines to prevent lapsing of recoveries
Reconcile ceded-loss notification records against the claims financial ledger quarterly
Escalate disputed reinsurer positions to the Reinsurance division for treaty-level resolution

subProcesses.name: Expense Monitoring & Allocated Loss Adjustment
steps: Track allocated loss adjustment expenses (ALAE) incurred on the claim including legal, expert, and IA fees
Review vendor invoices for accuracy, reasonableness, and compliance with fee schedules
Approve and post ALAE payments within delegated authority limits
Monitor total ALAE-to-indemnity ratio against line-of-business benchmarks
Flag claims with disproportionate ALAE for management review and expense controls
Accrue estimated future ALAE in the claim reserve alongside indemnity reserves
Report ALAE by claim, line, and cost category for financial close and reporting purposes
Close ALAE tracking when the claim is closed and reconcile actuals against accruals

subProcesses.name: Medicare & Lien Obligation Management
steps: Identify claimants who may be Medicare beneficiaries and register with the MMSEA Section 111 system
Submit mandatory insurer reporting to the CMS coordination of benefits contractor
Obtain a conditional payment letter from CMS and verify the itemized Medicare lien amount
Negotiate Medicare conditional payment reduction where appropriate with CMS or a lien resolution vendor
Resolve Medicare and lien obligations including Section 111 and MSP compliance before settlement
Identify and address Medicaid, ERISA, and workers' compensation liens in the settlement
Document lien resolution amounts and obtain necessary releases before disbursement
Retain Medicare lien compliance records per CMS documentation requirements

subProcesses.name: Financial Leakage Identification & Control
steps: Conduct periodic leakage audits on closed and open claims using severity and reserve benchmarks
Identify overpayment patterns in indemnity, ALAE, and vendor expense categories
Flag reserve-to-payment variance outliers for supervisory review and correction
Analyze deductible collection shortfalls and ensure deductible receivables are billed promptly
Review authority-limit compliance to confirm all approvals were obtained before payment
Report leakage findings to claims management and quality assurance teams
Recommend process or authority controls to prevent identified leakage categories
Track remediation actions and re-audit targeted handlers to confirm improvement

subProcesses.name: Emergency Mitigation & Property Preservation
steps: Assess the need for emergency mitigation including water extraction, board-up, or tarping
Authorize emergency services to prevent further damage within authority limits
Coordinate access between the insured and the emergency mitigation contractor
Monitor and approve emergency mitigation scope and billing against policy provisions
Obtain documentation of pre-mitigation and post-mitigation conditions with photos
Confirm that emergency services scope does not include unauthorized betterment
Review and approve the emergency services invoice before payment processing
Update reserves to reflect emergency mitigation costs and revised repair estimate

subProcesses.name: Preferred Vendor Network Dispatch & Assignment
steps: Identify the applicable preferred vendor network for the loss type, line, and geography
Dispatch the assignment to a network contractor, body shop, or restoration company
Confirm vendor acceptance of the assignment with expected inspection date
Provide the insured or claimant with the vendor contact and expected service timeline
Log vendor assignment details in the claims management system with accountability tracking
Monitor vendor performance against the agreed service-level agreement response times
Escalate to an alternate vendor when primary vendor cannot meet the service timeline
Update the claim file with vendor assignment and initial contact confirmation

subProcesses.name: Repair Estimate Review & Supplement Management
steps: Receive and review the initial repair estimate from the assigned contractor or appraiser
Compare the estimate against the adjuster's damage assessment and coverage provisions
Negotiate scope and pricing differences with the contractor within approved fee schedules
Approve the estimate and issue authority to repair or total-loss determination
Process and review supplement requests submitted during the repair process
Authorize legitimate supplements with documentation of additional damage discovered
Deny or partially approve supplements lacking adequate documentation or coverage support
Reconcile final repair costs against the reserve and adjust the reserve accordingly

subProcesses.name: Total Loss Processing & Vehicle Title Management
steps: Determine total-loss status when repair cost exceeds the applicable total-loss threshold
Obtain a market-value appraisal using an approved valuation tool and comparable sales
Present the total-loss offer to the claimant or insured with supporting valuation data
Negotiate the total-loss settlement within market-value parameters and policy limits
Obtain a signed total-loss settlement agreement and title or lien-release documents
Identify total-loss assets eligible for salvage and initiate salvage disposition
Process the total-loss payment after title transfer and all lien satisfactions are confirmed
Close the vehicle claim file and post the total-loss finalization to the claims system

subProcesses.name: Rental & Additional Living Expense Authorization
steps: Confirm rental reimbursement or additional living expense coverage under the policy
Authorize rental vehicle reservation or ALE housing placement within policy limits
Set the expected repair completion date as the rental duration benchmark
Monitor rental duration against repair progress and extend only with documented justification
Review and approve rental invoices against the policy per-day and per-occurrence limits
Notify the insured of rental expiration as the repair completion date approaches
Terminate rental authorization upon confirmed repair completion or total-loss settlement
Reconcile rental charges against the policy limit and post to the claim financial record

subProcesses.name: Salvage Management & Disposal
steps: Identify total-loss and damaged assets eligible for salvage from closed claims
Secure title, possession, and storage of the salvage asset and confirm lien releases
Obtain salvage valuations and reserve estimates from the assigned salvage pool or vendor
Assign the asset to a salvage pool or disposal channel (auction, direct sale, or parts)
Reconcile bid proceeds against the reserve estimate and approve the salvage disposition
Net salvage proceeds against the recoverable balance and update the claim financials
Post the settled salvage disposition to the claim file and recovery ledger
Report salvage proceeds to reinsurance when applicable to the ceded treaty

subProcesses.name: Vendor Performance Monitoring & Network Management
steps: Score salvage, contractor, and expert vendor performance against SLA metrics quarterly
Review customer satisfaction scores for insured-facing repair and mitigation vendors
Identify underperforming vendors and initiate remediation or network removal process
Negotiate fee schedule renewals with preferred vendors based on volume and performance data
Add new vendors to the network following credentialing, licensing, and insurance verification
Monitor vendor invoice accuracy and billing-compliance rates against approved fee schedules
Compile the vendor performance scorecard for claims management and procurement review
Update the preferred vendor network directory and routing rules in the claims system

subProcesses.name: Settlement Strategy Development
steps: Develop settlement strategy based on liability, damages, coverage, and exposure analysis
Evaluate bodily-injury severity, future medical costs, and wage-loss elements
Assess the claimant's demand and supporting documentation for reasonableness
Determine the settlement authority needed and request approval from the appropriate level
Identify structured-settlement opportunities for significant injury or long-tail claims
Consult with defense counsel on litigation risk and settlement value where suit is pending
Set the negotiation range with a reserve adequacy check before initiating discussions
Document the settlement strategy and authority level in the claim file

subProcesses.name: Negotiation & Settlement Execution
steps: Initiate settlement discussions with the claimant, attorney, or adverse carrier
Negotiate settlement within delegated authority limits and documented settlement parameters
Counter low-ball demands or unreasonable positions with evidence-based analysis
Escalate negotiation to supervisor or senior adjuster when impasse is reached
Obtain settlement authority approval before accepting or extending a final offer
Document the settlement agreement, release terms, and agreed amount in the claim file
Confirm Medicare, lien, and fee-interest obligations are addressed in the settlement
Communicate the settlement confirmation to the insured, claimant, and counsel

subProcesses.name: Release & Settlement Agreement Management
steps: Draft the general release or partial release consistent with the settlement terms
Obtain legal review of release language for complex or high-exposure settlements
Issue the release to the claimant or counsel for execution with a signature deadline
Track outstanding releases and follow up on unsigned documents
Authenticate executed release signatures and notarization where required
File the executed release in the claim file and update the claim status
Confirm that all lien-holder and Medicare consent obligations are satisfied before closing
Archive the final release as the authoritative settlement-closure document

subProcesses.name: Sanctions Screening & Payment Authorization
steps: Submit claim payees to sanctions screening and clear any OFAC SDN or state exclusion hits per the compliance control point
Verify payee bank account or mailing address against the claim and settlement file
Confirm the payment amount, payee, and claim reference in the payment authorization request
Obtain required dual-approval for payments exceeding the single-approval authority limit
Submit the authorized payment instruction to the accounts payable or claims payment system
Log the payment authorization with approver identities and timestamps for audit purposes
Retain the sanctions-screening results and clearance documentation in the claim file
Confirm the payment instruction is transmitted without exceptions before closing the authorization

subProcesses.name: Payment Processing & Disbursement
steps: Process claim payment via check, EFT, or structured settlement funding as elected
Apply the deductible offset before calculating the net payment due to the claimant
Confirm payment amount against the settlement authority and approved claim financials
Generate the payment instrument and transmit to the disbursement queue
Apply tax withholding where required and generate the applicable tax reporting document
Confirm payment delivery and obtain acknowledgment from the payee where required
Post the payment to the claim financial ledger and reduce reserves by the indemnity paid
Retain payment confirmation and disbursement records per document retention policy

subProcesses.name: Structured Settlement Placement & Annuity Administration
steps: Identify claims appropriate for structured settlement based on injury type and exposure amount
Engage a structured settlement consultant to develop annuity funding proposals
Present structured settlement options and tax-advantage disclosures to the claimant
Obtain court approval for structured settlements involving minors or incapacitated claimants
Execute the assignment and qualified assignment agreement with the annuity issuer
Fund the annuity purchase and confirm placement with the life insurance company
Document the structured settlement terms and annuity contract in the claim file
Close the indemnity reserve and confirm ongoing annuity payment responsibility with the issuer

subProcesses.name: Recovery Opportunity Detection & Triage
steps: Run automated subrogation-trigger rules across newly paid claims to identify candidates
Score candidate claims for recovery likelihood and net value using recovery analytics
Review loss facts to confirm a recoverable third party exists with applicable liability
Verify policy coverage and right-of-recovery language supports the subrogation claim
Flag fraud indicators for SIU screening before referral to the recovery unit
Reject non-viable candidates with documented rationale and close the recovery file
Compile the triaged worklist for referral routing to the subrogation specialist team
Report detection metrics and missed-recovery patterns for referral process improvement

subProcesses.name: Referral Intake, File Setup & Evidence Capture
steps: Receive and acknowledge the adjuster subrogation referral within the unit's service standard
Validate referral completeness against intake standards and return deficient referrals for cure
Open the recovery file and assign a specialist owner with appropriate authority level
Calculate the gross recoverable including the insured deductible and net paid loss
Build the evidence and document checklist and order police, fire, or incident reports
Set statute-of-limitations and diary tickler dates to protect the right of recovery
Flag claims exceeding treaty attachment points for ceded-loss notification to Reinsurance
Assemble the indexed evidence package including photos, witness statements, and expert reports

subProcesses.name: Subrogation Liability Assessment & Fault Apportionment
steps: Map the duty, breach, and causation chain for the loss event
Research jurisdictional negligence and comparative-fault rules applicable to the venue
Apportion fault across the involved parties based on evidence and legal standards
Assess defenses and recovery-barring exposures including contributory negligence
Quantify the net recoverable after fault apportionment and deductible inclusion
Draft the liability assessment memo and recovery recommendation
Inspect the damaged property or vehicle at the scene and preserve physical evidence
Engage a forensic or cause-and-origin expert when warranted by the loss complexity

subProcesses.name: Demand Preparation & Direct Negotiation
steps: Draft the recovery demand package with supporting exhibits including proof of payment
Identify and serve the adverse carrier or responsible party with the demand
Log the adverse party's response and counter-position in the recovery file
