Negotiate settlement within delegated authority limits and documented recovery parameters
Evaluate offers against the net recoverable and the cost-to-pursue threshold
Execute the settlement agreement and release upon reaching an acceptable resolution
Issue the deductible reimbursement to the insured upon receipt of the recovery
Post the recovery receipt to the claims financial ledger and close the demand file

subProcesses.name: Intercompany Arbitration Filing
steps: Confirm arbitration eligibility and the applicable forum rules (AAA, NASAR, or state forum)
Send the intercompany reimbursement notification to the adverse carrier
Assemble the arbitration contention and evidence exhibits per forum requirements
Verify the damage claim excludes double-counted deductible and salvage amounts
File the contention with the arbitration forum and pay the required filing fee
Submit rebuttal to the adverse carrier's counter-contention within the forum deadline
Attend the arbitration hearing or submit written submissions as required
Record the arbitration decision and recovery award in the recovery management system

subProcesses.name: Deductible Recovery & Insured Reimbursement
steps: Identify the insured deductible included in the recoverable demand amount
Track the made-whole rule compliance to confirm the insured is fully indemnified before recovery
Apply the insured's deductible share to the recovery demand proportionally
Calculate the pro-rata deductible share when only a partial recovery is received
Issue the deductible reimbursement check or EFT to the insured upon recovery receipt
Notify the insured of the reimbursement amount and the recovery outcome
Update the recovery file to reflect the deductible obligation as closed
Retain deductible reimbursement documentation for audit and regulatory purposes

subProcesses.name: Recovery Posting, Collections & Ageing Management
steps: Receive and identify incoming recovery payments from adverse carriers or parties
Apply the receipt to the correct claim and recovery file with accurate allocation
Allocate proceeds across deductible, salvage, and reinsurance shares per the recovery formula
Post recovery entries and reverse related reserves in the claims financial system
Reconcile recovery postings against the claim payment ledger for financial close accuracy
Age open recovery receivables by days outstanding and generate the ageing report
Issue follow-up and dunning notices on overdue balances per the collection schedule
Refer uncollectible balances to external collections or write off with documented rationale

subProcesses.name: Recovery Analytics & Performance Management
steps: Extract recovery, leakage, and cycle-time metrics from the recovery management system
Measure recovery rate against paid losses and benchmark against industry targets
Tune the subrogation-detection model with closed-file outcomes and missed-recovery data
Score salvage, collections, and legal vendor performance against contracted SLA metrics
Identify missed-recovery patterns and feed findings back to the referral and triage process
Compile the recovery performance and vendor scorecard for management reporting
Report net recovery results to actuarial for loss development and reserve credit purposes
Present recovery improvement recommendations to claims leadership for action

subProcesses.name: Suit Notice Receipt & Litigation Intake
steps: Receive suit notice from the insured, agent, or process server and log the receipt date
Open a litigation sub-file and assign a litigation handler or senior adjuster
Notify defense counsel of record or initiate a defense counsel selection process
Confirm the insured's duty to cooperate obligations and gather the tendered suit papers
Evaluate exposure including policy limits, coverage issues, and potential excess judgment risk
Set initial litigation reserves based on the complaint allegations and demand level
Log the answer deadline and all initial litigation diary dates in the claims system
Notify the insured in writing of the litigation assignment and defense arrangement

subProcesses.name: Defense Strategy Development
steps: Develop defense strategy collaboratively with assigned defense counsel
Review the complaint, prior claim history, investigation file, and coverage analysis
Identify affirmative defenses, cross-claims, and third-party contribution opportunities
Establish the litigation budget and litigation management guidelines for defense counsel
Determine whether a coverage disclaimer or defense under reservation of rights is appropriate
Set case objectives including resolution target, litigation timeline, and authority parameters
Obtain excess carrier or reinsurer notification when exposure approaches retention limits
Document the defense strategy and case plan in the litigation file

subProcesses.name: Discovery Management & Insured Cooperation
steps: Manage discovery by coordinating document production with the insured and defense counsel
Identify and preserve electronically stored information (ESI) relevant to the litigation
Review document production for privilege, work-product protection, and confidentiality
Prepare the insured, witnesses, and internal experts for fact and expert depositions
Review and approve defense counsel's discovery strategy and interrogatory responses
Monitor discovery compliance deadlines and escalate missed deadlines to claims management
Evaluate and respond to plaintiff's discovery requests for insurer claim records
Update litigation reserves as discovery reveals new information about exposure

subProcesses.name: Expert Witness & Damages Analysis
steps: Identify expert witness needs for liability, damages, causation, and industry-standard opinions
Retain qualified expert witnesses through defense counsel with appropriate credentials
Review expert reports and opinions for sufficiency before filing or disclosure
Challenge plaintiff expert opinions through Daubert motions or voir dire strategy
Analyze plaintiff's damages model for mathematical accuracy and legal supportability
Obtain independent damages analysis to counter inflated or unsupported claims
Coordinate expert testimony scheduling and preparation with defense counsel
Monitor expert witness fees against the litigation budget and approve invoices

subProcesses.name: Pre-Trial Settlement Negotiation
steps: Evaluate settlement value periodically throughout the litigation lifecycle
Negotiate pre-trial resolution through mediation, structured negotiation, or direct discussions
Obtain updated settlement authority as case value evolves during discovery and motion practice
Evaluate mediation proposals against litigation cost, trial risk, and excess exposure
Confirm satisfaction of Medicare, liens, and fee interests in any settlement structure
Execute the settlement agreement and stipulation of dismissal with prejudice
Confirm funding of the settlement and obtain signed releases from all plaintiffs
Update reserves to zero and close the litigation file upon confirmed settlement

subProcesses.name: Trial Management & Verdict Response
steps: Monitor trial proceedings and provide real-time authority adjustments to defense counsel
Coordinate daily trial status updates with defense counsel and claims management
Evaluate mid-trial settlement opportunities as verdict risk becomes clearer
Assess jury selection, opening statements, and witness testimony for exposure impact
Authorize last-minute settlement within authority if warranted by trial developments
Document the trial outcome including verdict amount and any special damages awarded
Evaluate post-trial motions and appeal options with defense counsel after an adverse verdict
Adjust reserves to reflect the verdict, judgment interest, and costs of collection

subProcesses.name: Bad Faith Prevention & Excess Exposure Management
steps: Monitor the claim for conditions that create excess judgment or bad-faith exposure
Notify the insured when demands approach or exceed policy limits and document the notification
Evaluate the Stowers or similar tender-of-limits demand and respond within required timeframes
Obtain excess carrier participation and consent before rejecting a limits demand
Conduct a bad-faith audit of the claim handling record at the litigation team level
Engage coverage counsel to assess and document the reasonableness of settlement decisions
Pursue recoveries where excess judgment creates a reimbursement right against a responsible party
Report excess-judgment events to senior leadership and actuarial for reserve and IBNR impact

subProcesses.name: Claim File Audit & Quality Review
steps: Select claims for quality audit using random sampling and targeted-trigger criteria
Evaluate file documentation completeness against the claims-handling standards checklist
Assess coverage analysis quality, liability determination accuracy, and reserve adequacy
Review compliance with regulatory contact and acknowledgment timelines
Score the claim file on a standardized quality scorecard and identify deficiency categories
Debrief the handling adjuster on audit findings and required corrective actions
Escalate systemic quality issues to claims management for process or training intervention
Document audit results in the quality management system and track remediation completion

subProcesses.name: Claims Compliance Monitoring & Regulatory Reporting
steps: Monitor claim-handling timelines against state fair-claims-practices act requirements
Track and report compliance rates for acknowledgment, investigation, and denial deadlines
Prepare and submit state-required statistical reports including loss-run and bordereaux data
Respond to state regulatory market-conduct examinations and document production requests
Track department-of-insurance complaint filings and ensure timely, compliant responses
Monitor changes in state claims-handling regulations and update handling guidelines accordingly
Report compliance metrics to the Chief Claims Officer and legal/compliance leadership
Maintain the regulatory compliance calendar with all state reporting deadlines and exam schedules

subProcesses.name: Claims Closure Standards & File Finalization
steps: Confirm all indemnity payments, expense payments, and recoveries are finalized before closure
Verify that executed releases, closing documents, and lien satisfactions are in the file
Confirm reinsurance notification and recovery billings are complete for eligible claims
Review the final reserve to zero and confirm no outstanding financial obligations remain
Apply the correct closure code, outcome classification, and closure date in the claims system
Complete the post-closure review checklist and obtain supervisor sign-off
Archive the claim file in accordance with state document-retention and e-discovery requirements
Confirm closure metrics are captured for cycle-time, reserve accuracy, and payment timeliness reporting

subProcesses.name: Reopened Claim Management
steps: Receive and evaluate a request to reopen a closed claim with documented justification
Confirm that the statute of limitations or contractual claim-filing period remains open
Reopen the claim in the claims system and restore or establish reserves as warranted
Assign the reopened claim to a handler and set investigation and contact diaries
Conduct a supplemental investigation to assess the basis for the reopened loss
Adjudicate the reopened claim and communicate a coverage position within regulatory deadlines
Process any additional payments or denials arising from the supplemental investigation
Re-close the claim with updated closure documentation and lessons-learned notation

subProcesses.name: Claims Performance Analytics & Reporting
steps: Extract key performance indicators including cycle time, severity, frequency, and recovery rate
Benchmark claims performance against prior periods, peer carriers, and industry data
Analyze loss-development trends by line of business, territory, and cause of loss
Report emerging claim trends and large-loss patterns to actuarial and underwriting
Compile the monthly claims dashboard for executive and board-level reporting
Monitor adjuster caseload, authority utilization, and productivity metrics
Identify performance outliers at the adjuster, team, and regional level for management action
Present claims analytics findings to the Claims Leadership Team at the quarterly review

subProcesses.name: Claims Training, Calibration & Capability Development
steps: Identify training needs from quality audit results, compliance findings, and performance data
Develop and deliver line-specific technical training on coverage, liability, and reserving
Conduct claims-calibration sessions to align adjuster judgment on severity and settlement value
Facilitate mock negotiations and settlement simulations for junior adjusters
Deliver regulatory and compliance training on new or amended state claims-handling requirements
Track training completion rates and competency assessments for each adjuster
Measure post-training quality improvement by re-auditing the trained cohort
Report training effectiveness and curriculum updates to the Chief Claims Officer

subProcesses.name: STD/LTD Claim Intake & Eligibility Verification
steps: Receive and register disability claim through employer, claimant, or treating-provider channel
Verify coverage, eligibility, and elimination period against the group policy and census data
Obtain authorizations and medical evidence including HIPAA authorizations and attending physician statements
Confirm pre-disability earnings and occupation definition from the employer and policy records
Render initial liability decision within ERISA timeline per the applicable ERISA clock
Issue the initial claim determination notice with appeal rights disclosure to the claimant
Notify the employer of the claim status and expected benefit payment timeline
Document intake actions and eligibility determination in the disability claim system

subProcesses.name: Medical Review & Functional Capacity Assessment
steps: Triage claim by severity and expected duration using diagnosis, treatment, and occupational data
Conduct clinical review of medical evidence by an in-house nurse or clinical consultant
Order independent medical exam or functional capacity evaluation when clinical evidence is insufficient
Assess functional capacity against disability definition (own-occupation or any-occupation standard)
Obtain peer review or specialist consultation for complex diagnoses or disputed impairments
Document clinical rationale and update claim plan with evidence-based functional restrictions
Communicate the medical review outcome to the claimant and treating provider
Set diary for ongoing medical update collection and the any-occupation transition review date

subProcesses.name: Benefit Calculation & Offset Administration
steps: Establish gross benefit from covered earnings using the policy benefit formula
Identify and apply other-income offsets including SSDI, workers' compensation, and pension benefits
Initiate SSDI application support and reimbursement agreement with the claimant
Set up tax withholding and sick-pay reporting under applicable IRS requirements
Authorize and release recurring benefit payments on the scheduled payment cycle
Reconcile SSDI awards and recover overpayments when SSDI is awarded retroactively
Adjust the benefit calculation when offset sources change or claimant reports new income
Document the benefit calculation worksheet and offset schedule in the claim file

subProcesses.name: Ongoing Claim Management & Recertification
steps: Develop claim management and contact plan with defined touchpoint schedule for the claimant
Collect periodic proof of continuing disability through medical updates and attending-physician statements
Review and update the offset schedule when claimant reports changes in other-income sources
Conduct any-occupation transition review at the policy-defined transition point
Evaluate vocational capacity and labor market surveys for the any-occupation standard
Continue, terminate, or settle benefits and communicate decision within ERISA timelines
Provide adverse benefit determination notice with appeal rights when benefits are terminated
Archive the ongoing-management activity log for ERISA compliance and audit purposes

subProcesses.name: Return-to-Work & Vocational Rehabilitation
steps: Screen claim for return-to-work potential using functional capacity and employer feedback
Develop return-to-work and rehabilitation plan with the claimant, employer, and treating provider
Coordinate workplace accommodations with employer under ADA interactive process guidelines
Monitor transitional work and apply partial benefit offsets during the transitional work period
Engage a vocational rehabilitation counselor for retraining or job placement assistance
Track rehabilitation participation and progress against the approved vocational plan milestones
Authorize rehabilitation expenses within the policy's vocational benefit provisions
Close rehabilitation case and record outcomes and report return-to-work results to the employer

subProcesses.name: ERISA Appeals & Adverse Determination Review
steps: Register appeal and acknowledge within ERISA window upon receipt of the appeal request
Assemble appeal file and assign independent reviewer with no prior involvement in the claim
Obtain independent clinical and vocational opinions to support the appeal review
Render appeal determination within regulatory timeline with full ERISA compliance
Issue the final adverse benefit determination letter with the right-to-sue disclosure
Refer exhausted appeals to litigation counsel with the complete administrative record
Track appeal outcomes and identify systemic denial patterns for claims leadership review
Report ERISA appeal compliance metrics to the regulatory affairs and legal teams

subProcesses.name: Death Claim Notification & Intake
steps: Receive death notification and open claim from beneficiary, agent, or estate representative
Identify in-force policies and contracts across lines including life, annuity, and rider products
Validate death certificate authenticity and confirm the insured identity match
Verify beneficiary designations on file and assess whether a beneficiary update occurred near death
Assign claim and issue acknowledgment packet with required documentation list and instructions
Conduct a Death Master File cross-check to confirm the insured's reported date of death
Open the claim record in the life claims administration system and set intake diary dates
Notify the insured's agent of record and employer group sponsor if applicable

subProcesses.name: Claim Requirements Gathering & Good-Order Management
steps: Determine claim requirements by product and jurisdiction for each in-force policy or contract
Issue claimant statements and claim kits with instructions and applicable form packages
Track outstanding requirements and follow up within regulatory timeframes per state statute
Review submissions for good order and authenticate claimants through identity verification
Request additional documentation when submissions are incomplete or contain discrepancies
Confirm all required jurisdictional forms are signed, witnessed, and notarized as required
Log all follow-up contacts and submission status in the claim tracking system
Advance the claim to adjudication queue only when the file is in complete good order

subProcesses.name: Contestability & Interpleader Review
steps: Screen claims for contestability and investigation triggers based on the contestability period and cause of death
Conduct contestable claim investigation including ordering medical records and attending-physician statements
Research the applicant's representations on the original application for material misrepresentation
Determine rescission, adjustment, or payment decision with documented coverage rationale
Identify competing claimant and beneficiary disputes arising from multiple or conflicting designations
Obtain legal counsel opinion on contested beneficiary designation or community property rights
File interpleader and deposit proceeds with court when the dispute cannot be resolved without judicial intervention
Resolve dispute and release proceeds per court order and close the interpleader file

subProcesses.name: Death Benefit & Statutory Interest Calculation
steps: Retrieve policy values and adjustments including outstanding loans, premium arrears, and dividend credits
Calculate gross death benefit and deductions applying all contractual policy provisions
Determine the applicable accidental death benefit or double-indemnity rider payment
Calculate statutory claim interest by state from the date of death to the payment date
Confirm the net benefit payable after loan offsets, deductions, and tax withholding
Obtain settlement authority approval for benefits exceeding the unit's delegated limit
Document the benefit calculation worksheet in the claim file with actuarial formula reference
Prepare the payment instruction with the final net amount and payee instructions

subProcesses.name: Accelerated Death Benefit & Rider Claims
steps: Receive accelerated benefit or waiver-of-premium claim from the policyowner or insured
Evaluate medical certification of qualifying condition including terminal illness or chronic illness documentation
Confirm eligibility under the applicable rider provisions and policy contract terms
Approve benefit and calculate acceleration or waiver of future premium obligations
Disburse accelerated benefit and confirm tax treatment with the appropriate IRS exclusion disclosure
Issue the benefit payment and update the remaining death benefit and cash value records
Set recertification diary for continuing disability waiver-of-premium cases
Recertify continuing disability and terminate waiver on recovery per rider provisions

subProcesses.name: Settlement Option Election & Payout
steps: Present settlement options and disclosures to beneficiaries including lump sum, annuity, and installment options
Record settlement election and verify payee instructions with identity verification
Screen beneficiary payees against sanctions lists including OFAC SDN and state exclusion databases
Obtain required guardian or court approval for minor or incapacitated beneficiaries
Disburse proceeds and apply tax withholding with the correct federal and state withholding calculations
Issue settlement confirmation and tax reporting including Form 1099-R or 1099-MISC as applicable
Close claim and update policy status in the policy administration and claims systems
Retain settlement election documentation and tax-reporting records per retention policy

subProcesses.name: Annuity Death Benefit & Maturity Processing
steps: Receive annuity death claim and confirm contract status and beneficiary designation
Determine death benefit under contract provisions including GMDB, GMIB, or standard account value
Capture beneficiary distribution election including 5-year rule, stretch, or lump-sum options
Process qualified contract and IRA beneficiary distributions per IRS required-minimum-distribution rules
Identify maturing and endowing policies and notify policyowners of available settlement elections
Calculate maturity or endowment value with applicable interest and bonus credits
Disburse annuity death proceeds or maturity payment and issue tax reporting with Form 1099-R
Refer unresponsive maturities to unclaimed property after required outreach attempts are exhausted

subProcesses.name: Retained Asset Account & Unclaimed Property Administration
steps: Establish and fund retained asset account for eligible beneficiaries electing the RAA option
Deliver RAA disclosures and welcome kit with account terms, interest rate, and withdrawal instructions
Service RAA drafts, withdrawals, and statements in compliance with state interest-crediting requirements
Monitor RAA dormancy and refer to escheatment after required dormancy period per state statute
Receive DMF match referrals and open insurer-initiated claims for life and annuity policies
Conduct beneficiary location and documented outreach per RSA settlement agreement standards
Adjudicate located-beneficiary claims and pay with interest as required by the RSA or state statute
Track RSA compliance and report to regulators on the required reporting schedule

subProcesses.name: Policy Issuance & Record Creation
steps: Receive bound risk package from underwriting and log transaction in policy administration system
Validate issuance data against bound quote — coverage terms, limits, deductibles, and effective dates
Confirm state form filing approval and retrieve applicable approved policy forms and endorsements
Assemble policy document package including declarations page, coverage forms, exclusions, and mandatory notices
Apply rating output and premium schedule to the policy record
Generate policy documents via document composition engine and apply digital signatures where permitted
Perform quality review of assembled policy package against underwriting bind authority and state requirements
Assign policy number and activate the in-force policy record in the administration system
Distribute policy package to insured, agent/broker via preferred delivery channel
Trigger producer commission calculation and transmit compensation feed
Log audit trail of issuance event and file proof of delivery
Confirm receipt acknowledgment and close issuance work item

subProcesses.name: Endorsements & Mid-Term Changes
steps: Receive change request from insured, broker, or underwriter and log in service queue
Validate request against policy record — identify coverage area, effective date, and binding authority required
Route to appropriate authority level based on change type and underwriting guidelines
Calculate premium impact of requested change including pro-rata or short-rate adjustment
Apply required underwriting review for coverage increases, new locations, or exposure additions
Process change in policy administration system and update all affected coverage fields
Generate endorsement document and attach to master policy record
Distribute endorsement to insured and broker and post to online portal
Update billing record to reflect premium change effective date
Log audit entry for change including requestor, authority, and premium impact
Notify downstream systems — claims, reinsurance, regulatory reporting — of material coverage changes
Close change request and confirm completion to requestor

subProcesses.name: Renewals Processing
steps: Identify policies entering renewal evaluation window and generate renewal candidate report
Pull prior-term loss data, exposure changes, and rate revision factors from rating engine
Apply renewal rating including any carrier-filed rate changes and tier re-evaluation
Generate renewal offer with updated premium, coverage terms, and any underwriting conditions
Distribute renewal offer to insured and broker within statutory advance-notice period
Receive broker or insured response — acceptance, declination, or counter-request
Process any coverage modifications requested at renewal through endorsement workflow
Bind renewal policy and generate renewal declarations and updated policy documents
Transition billing to renewal term and issue first-term invoice or EFT draft notice
Update in-force records for new policy period and archive prior-term documents
Report renewal retention metrics and declination reasons to underwriting management
Close renewal work item and confirm new policy period is active

subProcesses.name: Cancellations & Non-Renewal Processing
steps: Receive cancellation request or identify non-renewal trigger — non-payment, underwriting action, or insured request
Validate cancellation authority and classify as flat, pro-rata, or short-rate cancellation
Confirm statutory advance-notice requirements by state and line of business
Generate and distribute cancellation or non-renewal notice to insured and lienholder within required timeframes
Calculate return premium and transmit adjustment to billing and collections
Process mortgage and lienholder notifications and evidence of cancellation certificates
Update policy status to cancelled or non-renewed in policy administration system
Stop automated billing and cancel outstanding premium notices
Issue return premium payment or apply credit to outstanding balance
Notify claims of mid-term cancellation for any open claims adjustment
Log cancellation with reason code and effective date for regulatory reporting
Archive policy record and confirm cancellation is complete

subProcesses.name: Reinstatements Processing
steps: Receive reinstatement request and verify prior policy is within reinstatement eligibility window
Confirm reason for lapse — non-payment, underwriting failure, or insured request
Assess underwriting acceptability of risk for reinstatement based on loss activity during lapse gap
Calculate back premium owed including any reinstatement fees or interest
Require evidence of insurability if required by line and state regulations
Issue conditional reinstatement offer specifying terms, payment required, and effective date
Collect payment and validate funds clearance before reinstating coverage
Reinstate policy record with correct effective date and note lapse period in history
Generate reinstatement confirmation and updated policy documents
Notify claims of lapse gap dates for any claims adjudication purposes
Reset grace-period tracking and update billing schedule
Log reinstatement audit trail and close request

subProcesses.name: Grace Period, Lapse & Nonforfeiture Processing
steps: Identify premium default and calculate grace period start date per state statute and policy terms
Generate and distribute grace period notice to policyowner with amount due and deadline
Monitor for payment receipt during grace period and halt lapse if premium received
Issue pending lapse notice if premium remains unpaid approaching grace period expiry
Evaluate nonforfeiture options available — extended term, reduced paid-up, or surrender value
Apply automatic nonforfeiture option per policy default election at grace period expiry
Update policy status to lapsed or paid-up per nonforfeiture election
Notify policyowner and beneficiary of lapsed status and reinstatement eligibility window
Halt claim payment on lapsed coverage and notify claims accordingly
Apply waiver-of-premium benefit for approved disability claims to halt lapse processing
Record lapse event with reason code and report conservation metrics to product management
Archive lapse record and close processing work item

subProcesses.name: Term Conversions & 1035 Exchanges
steps: Receive conversion or exchange election from policyowner or producer
Verify conversion eligibility — term within conversion period, attained age, and product availability
Confirm conversion credits and transferred values applicable to new product
Validate 1035 exchange paperwork and replacement disclosures per NAIC Model Replacement Regulation
Coordinate funds transfer request to ceding carrier and track incoming funds timeline
Apply received funds and record carryover cost basis for tax purposes
Apply best-interest review for annuity conversion cases per applicable state requirements
Issue converted or exchanged contract with new policy number and effective date
Confirm producer appointment and compensation for new contract
Terminate prior coverage and reconcile any outstanding premium balances
Distribute new contract documents and deliver required disclosures to owner
Log conversion or exchange event in policy history and report to compliance

subProcesses.name: Beneficiary Designation Management
steps: Receive and authenticate beneficiary change request from policyowner or authorized representative
Validate requestor authority to modify beneficiary under current policy ownership and assignment records
Confirm consent requirements — irrevocable beneficiary release or collateral assignment holder approval — before processing
Assess designation requirements for compliance with policy terms — per stirpes, class, or specific beneficiary
Review designation for completeness — full legal name, relationship, date of birth, and percentage allocations
Obtain required spousal consent documentation for community property state or ERISA-qualified contracts
Update beneficiary designations in policy record and endorse contract if required by state or product
Confirm change with written acknowledgment to policyowner and new designee where applicable
Notify collateral assignment holders of changes affecting their security interest
Distribute updated policy documents or endorsement reflecting the beneficiary change
Log change event in policy audit history with authentication and approval records
File required state notifications for designations involving minors or special designations

subProcesses.name: Policy Ownership & Assignment Changes
steps: Receive ownership change or assignment request with supporting legal documentation
Validate requestor authority and confirm current owner identity before processing any transfer
Review supporting documentation — trust agreement, corporate resolution, or UTMA custodial documents — for legal sufficiency
Process absolute assignment transferring all ownership rights with required acknowledgment from assignee
Process collateral assignment for lender security interest and confirm lender notification requirements
Update ownership record — individual, trust, corporate, or UTMA — in policy administration system
Confirm tax implications of ownership transfer and generate required disclosure to new owner
Notify collateral assignment holders of new ownership structure affecting their security interest
Update billing and premium payor records to reflect new ownership and payment responsibility
Distribute ownership change confirmation and updated policy documents to new owner
Log ownership change event in policy audit history with all supporting documentation references
Close ownership change request and confirm all downstream records are updated

subProcesses.name: Policy Loans & Partial Surrenders
steps: Receive and validate in-force transaction request — policy loan or partial surrender — and confirm owner identity
Review replacement and suitability implications for transactions involving coverage reduction
Calculate available loan value or surrender value for the requested transaction amount
Apply state and policy-specific waiting periods and processing requirements for financial transactions
Screen payee against OFAC and sanctions watchlists before approving disbursement
Obtain required supervisor approval for transactions above defined financial authority limits
Process disbursement via owner-specified method and apply appropriate tax withholding
Apply loan interest accrual from disbursement date and update policy loan balance
Update policy values — cash value, death benefit, and outstanding loan balance — post-transaction
Issue transaction confirmation and updated policy value statement to policyowner
Reconcile disbursement to accounting ledger and confirm funds cleared
Log transaction in policy audit history and close service request

subProcesses.name: Life Premium Billing Handoff & Premium Application
steps: Establish billing mode and premium schedule in billing system at policy issue per insured election
Transmit premium due feed to billing system for each billing cycle with modal premium and policy identifier
Receive premium payment confirmation from billing and apply to policy values — reserve, cash value, or face amount
Resolve policy-side premium application exceptions — unallocated payments, returned items, and modal timing mismatches
Process extra premium payments for additional coverage, rider reinstatement, or policy loan repayment
Apply waiver-of-premium credit to policy record upon disability claim approval
Trigger automatic premium loan processing when policy is in grace period and loan value is available
Update premium payment history and next-due-date in policy record
Confirm premium application to dividend calculation base for participating policies
Reconcile premium receipts applied to policy record against billing system payment confirmations
Report premium payment status and automatic premium loan activity to policy administration management
Archive premium payment records per record-retention schedule

subProcesses.name: Policy Values, Illustrations & Annual Statements
steps: Run monthly valuation cycle and apply credited interest, cost-of-insurance charges, and rider charges to universal life contracts
Run annual dividend calculation for participating life contracts using divisible surplus allocation
Update accumulated value, loan balance, and net surrender value in policy administration system
Apply dividend option per policyholder election — paid in cash, reduce premium, purchase paid-up additions, or deposit at interest
Produce in-force illustrations upon request using current non-guaranteed elements per NAIC Illustration Model Regulation
Validate illustration compliance with actuarial certification requirements and state filing
Generate annual policy statements with premium history, values, loans, and transaction summary
Distribute statements via customer preferred channel and post to online portal
Produce policy anniversary notices and dividend notices with values and election options
Process statement corrections and reissue updated statements for calculation or data errors
Resolve policyholder inquiries regarding illustrated values, dividend amounts, and loan impact on values
Archive annual statements in document management system per retention schedule

subProcesses.name: Retirement Plan Recordkeeping & ERISA Servicing
steps: Process payroll contribution and allocation instructions from plan sponsor on each contribution cycle
Maintain participant records — eligibility, enrollment date, investment elections, and vesting schedule
Apply vesting schedule calculations on anniversary date or termination event per plan document
Process in-service distributions, hardship withdrawals, and plan loans per plan document and IRS requirements
Process termination distributions and rollovers with required 402(f) special tax notice and withholding
Qualify and administer domestic relations orders — review QDRO compliance and segregate alternate payee account
Process plan death benefit claims including spousal consent verification and beneficiary distribution
Prepare ERISA participant disclosure support — 404(a)(5) fee disclosures and benefit statements
Prepare 408(b)(2) service provider disclosure information for plan sponsor filing
Reconcile plan assets and participant accounts to custodian and investment records
Support Form 5500 preparation with plan-year financial data and participant counts
Resolve plan compliance issues and support EPCRS voluntary correction filings

subProcesses.name: Life Policy Reinstatement & Conservation
steps: Receive reinstatement application from lapsed policyowner within reinstatement eligibility window
Verify lapsed policy is within reinstatement period per policy terms and state statute
Order evidence of insurability — medical exam, attending physician statement, or non-medical questionnaire
Underwrite evidence of insurability and determine reinstatement acceptability
Calculate back premiums, loan interest, and reinstatement fees owed from lapse date
Issue conditional reinstatement offer with terms, payment required, and effective date
Collect funds and validate clearance before reinstating policy coverage
Restore policy to in-force status with correct reinstatement effective date in policy record
Reset contestability period clock from reinstatement date per policy terms
Notify claims of contestability reset for any claims adjudication
Generate reinstatement confirmation and updated policy documents
Report conservation success rates and reinstatement metrics to product management

subProcesses.name: Death Master File Matching & Escheatment
steps: Run periodic batch matching of in-force policy records against Social Security Administration Death Master File
Identify potential matches and apply match confidence scoring to filter false positives
Investigate potential DMF matches — request death certificate or probate records to confirm insured death
Attempt contact with beneficiaries and policyowners to prompt claim filing on confirmed deaths
Initiate proactive claim payout for confirmed unclaimed life insurance benefits per state settlement agreements
Calculate and disburse unclaimed death benefits with accumulated interest per state unclaimed property law
Identify dormant life and annuity accounts with no owner contact and initiate due-diligence outreach
Report unclaimed property to state unclaimed property administrators on annual statutory filing deadline
Maintain DMF matching run log with match volumes, confirmation rates, and payout amounts
Support state and regulatory audits of unclaimed property compliance
Track proactive claims payout activity against settlement agreement targets
Report DMF matching program results and escheatment amounts to compliance and finance annually

subProcesses.name: Annuity Application Intake & Good-Order Review
steps: Receive and index annuity application with all required supporting forms and disclosures
Verify producer license, appointment, and required product training certification
Confirm anti-money-laundering identification documentation meets BSA requirements
Perform good-order review — check all required fields, signatures, dates, and required disclosure acknowledgments
Identify and log not-in-good-order deficiencies with specific cure requirements
Contact producer or applicant to resolve not-in-good-order items within defined correction window
Confirm initial premium receipt and apply rate lock or interest crediting start date per product terms
Review replacement disclosures for completeness and confirm replacement paperwork is filed with state if required
Screen applicant and payee against OFAC and sanctions watchlists
Validate that application is received within any applicable offer period or rate lock window
Log completed good-order review result and advance application to suitability review
Notify producer of application receipt and good-order status

subProcesses.name: Suitability & Best-Interest Review
steps: Compile consumer profile and financial information from application — age, income, assets, liquid net worth, and objectives
Evaluate the recommendation against best-interest obligations under NAIC Model 275 and applicable state rules
Assess consumer need for liquidity relative to surrender charge period and contract terms
Review replacement activity and confirm replacement disclosures are complete and regulator-filed
Evaluate whether the recommended product and benefit riders are in the consumer best interest
Escalate cases with suitability concerns to supervisory review queue for additional scrutiny
Request additional consumer financial information if initial profile is insufficient for evaluation
Decline or pend unsuitable cases and notify producer of reason for non-acceptance
Record supervisory review determination and supporting rationale in suitability audit trail
File required suitability review documentation per state and company record-retention standards
Report suitability review outcomes and decline rates to compliance for trend monitoring
Advance approved applications to contract issue processing

subProcesses.name: 1035 Exchange & Transfer Funding
steps: Validate 1035 exchange and transfer paperwork — Form 1035, transfer authorization, and ceding carrier information
Confirm replacement compliance before initiating funds request — NAIC replacement forms complete and filed
Confirm cost-basis and adjusted basis information is provided by ceding carrier or owner
Initiate funds request to ceding carrier via required transfer instructions within defined timeline
Track incoming funds and monitor aging transfers against expected receipt dates
Follow up on delayed transfers with ceding carrier using standardized escalation timeline
Receive incoming transfer funds and confirm amount matches expected surrender value
Apply received funds to new annuity contract and record carryover cost basis for tax purposes
Issue contract confirmation with opening account value reflecting transferred funds
Report any tax-year contribution coding required for IRA rollovers
Notify producer of successful funding and contract activation
Log all exchange correspondence, funds receipt, and cost-basis records in contract history

subProcesses.name: Contract Issue, Delivery & Free-Look Administration
steps: Generate annuity contract and complete issue package including all state-required annexes and disclosures
Perform pre-issue quality review of contract variables — owner, annuitant, beneficiary, premium, and benefit elections
Deliver contract via insured preferred channel and capture delivery receipt or e-consent acknowledgment
Start free-look period clock from date of contract delivery per state-specific free-look statute
Monitor free-look period expiration dates and confirm contracts that have exited free-look
Process free-look cancellations — return premium with applicable interest per state requirement
Confirm issue and trigger producer compensation event to commission accounting system
Finalize in-force contract record and activate owner online account
Distribute required periodic statement and owner notification schedules from issue date
Record delivery confirmation in contract history with date, channel, and signature or acknowledgment reference
Report free-look cancellation rates by product and state to product management
Confirm contract is fully in force and advance to ongoing servicing

subProcesses.name: Subaccount Allocation & Portfolio Rebalancing
steps: Receive and validate allocation change or rebalancing request from owner or authorized agent
Authenticate owner identity using knowledge-based or multi-factor authentication
Process fund allocation changes and future-premium redirection per owner election
Execute portfolio rebalancing to target allocation percentages on scheduled or requested basis
Update systematic program instructions — automatic rebalancing and dollar-cost averaging — per owner election
Validate allocation elections against available investment options and confirm no restricted funds are selected
Apply allocation changes to existing contract value and confirm transaction effective date and price
Generate allocation confirmation showing new percentage elections and updated subaccount values
Post allocation change to contract record and update online account view
Issue confirmation of allocation change to owner and producer
Log all allocation and rebalancing actions with requestor authentication record and change detail
Report subaccount allocation change volumes and systematic program enrollment to product management

subProcesses.name: Contract Owner & Beneficiary Maintenance
steps: Receive and validate non-financial service request from owner or authorized agent
Authenticate owner identity using knowledge-based or multi-factor authentication
Process beneficiary designation changes with required signature and consent documentation
Process ownership changes — absolute assignment, UTMA, trust, or entity changes — with legal review where needed
Update banking information for systematic withdrawals or income payments with pre-note verification
Maintain address, phone, and communication preference updates in contract record
Confirm tax implications of ownership transfer and generate required disclosure to new owner
Notify collateral assignment holders of ownership or beneficiary changes affecting their security interest
Generate updated contract statement reflecting account maintenance changes
Issue confirmation of all account changes to owner and producer
Log all service actions with requestor authentication record and change detail in contract history
Report maintenance request volumes and pending items to servicing operations management

subProcesses.name: Withdrawals & Surrender Processing
steps: Receive and validate withdrawal or surrender request — verify owner identity and confirm authority
Calculate withdrawal amount and applicable surrender charges, market value adjustments, and tax withholding
Perform conservation outreach for full surrender cases above defined value threshold
Apply best-interest review triggers for surrender or large withdrawal requests per applicable rules
Evaluate free-withdrawal provision availability before applying surrender charges
Screen payee against OFAC and sanctions watchlists before disbursement approval
Obtain supervisory approval for large disbursements above defined authority thresholds
Process disbursement via owner-specified method — check, wire, EFT, or 1035 transfer
Apply required federal and state tax withholding per owner election and calculate withholding amount; forward to tax remittance via Document & Correspondence Management
Issue IRS Form 1099-R tax document for reportable distributions
Terminate contract record upon full surrender and archive final statement
Log all withdrawal and surrender actions with approval record and disbursement confirmation in contract history

subProcesses.name: Annuity RMD Processing
steps: Identify RMD-eligible annuity contract holders — IRA and qualified annuities, age 73 or older per SECURE 2.0 rules
Calculate annual RMD amounts using IRS Uniform Lifetime Table or Beneficiary Table as applicable to the contract
Notify contract owners of RMD obligation and capture payment frequency and withholding elections
Process RMD payments by December 31 statutory deadline and April 1 for initial year of eligibility
Track cumulative RMD payments against calculated annual requirement throughout the year
Identify missed or insufficient annuity RMDs and initiate correction process
Support contract owner submission of IRS Form 5329 for excise tax abatement on missed RMDs
Process beneficiary RMDs for inherited annuity accounts under applicable distribution rules
Apply 10-year rule for non-eligible designated beneficiaries per SECURE Act requirements
Issue 1099-R for all RMD distributions with correct distribution code
Report RMD compliance statistics and correction activity to tax reporting and compliance team
Archive RMD calculation records and payment confirmation per IRS retention requirements

subProcesses.name: Annuitization & Payout Election Administration
steps: Notify owner approaching annuity date of available payout options and required election deadline
Present payout option illustrations — life only, period certain, joint and survivor, and lump sum
Quote annuity income amounts based on current annuity purchase rates and applicable mortality tables
Capture and validate payout election from owner — including joint annuitant and period-certain term
Calculate income payment amount and exclusion ratio for tax-free return of cost-basis portion
Establish payout records in annuity payment administration system
Process first annuity income payment and confirm receipt by owner
Set up recurring payment schedule — monthly, quarterly, or annual — per owner election
Administer proof-of-life and survivorship verification requirements for life-contingent payout options
Process death benefit upon annuitant death during payout phase per benefit option terms
Issue annual 1099-R for payout-phase distributions with correct taxable and exclusion breakdown
Monitor ongoing payment accuracy and process payment amount adjustments for COLA-linked products

subProcesses.name: Plan Installation & Conversion Onboarding
steps: Gather plan documents, adoption agreement, and service requirements from new plan sponsor
Review plan document for recordkeeping-system compatibility and identify any custom plan provisions
Configure plan rules on recordkeeping platform — eligibility, entry dates, vesting, match formula, and loan provisions
Establish investment lineup on platform and confirm fund availability and share class selection
Coordinate transition asset transfer with prior recordkeeper and establish transition timeline
Distribute blackout notice to participants within required 30-day advance-notice window
Receive and reconcile conversion records — participant balances, loans, and investment allocations
Validate go-live data completeness and accuracy against prior recordkeeper final records
Lift blackout period and confirm participant access to accounts and transaction capabilities
Conduct sponsor orientation on plan administration portal and reporting tools
Confirm all required ERISA plan notices are distributed to participants at plan launch
Report plan installation completion to relationship management and compliance

subProcesses.name: Participant Enrollment & Account Maintenance
steps: Process eligibility and enrollment files from plan sponsor on each payroll cycle
Establish participant accounts with elected investment allocations and deferral rates
Maintain indicative data — name, address, Social Security number, date of birth, and hire date
Process beneficiary designation changes with required spousal consent documentation
Apply vesting schedule to participant accounts at anniversary, termination, and distribution events
Reconcile payroll data discrepancies with plan sponsor and resolve eligibility classification issues
Process deferral rate changes and investment re-election on participant request
Locate missing participants using SSA, USPS, and commercial search resources
Resolve stale payment checks — stop payment and reissue or initiate rollover to IRA
Generate and distribute participant benefit statements on quarterly and annual cycle
Maintain auto-enrollment and auto-escalation program elections per plan document
Report participant account and enrollment data accuracy metrics to plan sponsor

subProcesses.name: Contribution Remittance & Allocation Processing
steps: Receive and validate payroll contribution files from plan sponsor on each contribution cycle
Confirm contribution file format, participant identifiers, and contribution source codes
Collect contribution funding via wire transfer and confirm bank receipt
Monitor deposit timeliness against DOL deposit rules and flag late remittances for fiduciary reporting
Validate contributions against IRS 402(g) elective deferral limits and 415 annual additions limits
Allocate participant contributions to elected investment options at daily NAV
Apply employer match formula per plan document including true-up provisions
Allocate profit-sharing and employer non-elective contributions on plan-document-defined allocation method
Resolve suspense and allocation exceptions — unmatched participants and incomplete census entries
Reconcile plan remittances and investment allocations to custodian and fund confirmations
Generate contribution confirmation report for plan sponsor acknowledgment
Report late remittances, prohibited transactions, and annual limit exceedances to compliance

subProcesses.name: Omnibus Trade Settlement & Trust Reconciliation
steps: Aggregate participant-level investment transactions and generate daily omnibus trade file for each fund
Transmit trade files to fund companies or custodian within cut-off time for same-day NAV
Receive trade confirmation and daily NAV data from fund companies and custodian
Post trade settlements and daily valuations to participant account records
Reconcile participant unit positions to omnibus account holdings at custodian
Reconcile cash positions and sweep account balances to custodian and bank records
Identify and resolve trade settlement breaks — quantity mismatches, failed trades, and pricing errors
Process make-whole adjustments to participant accounts for pricing errors per DOL guidance
Maintain investment lineup and process fund substitution changes per plan sponsor direction
Coordinate fund closure or restriction changes with participants and update election options
Generate trust reconciliation report and confirm agreement with custodian monthly
Report unresolved settlement breaks and aged reconciliation items to operations management

subProcesses.name: Distribution, Rollover & Termination Processing
steps: Receive distribution request from terminating or retired participant and verify eligibility and vesting
Deliver IRS 402(f) special tax notice and capture participant signed election within required notice period
Confirm rollover destination eligibility — IRA, qualified plan, or annuity
Document rollover best-interest review for IRA rollover recommendations per DOL fiduciary standards
Screen distribution payees against OFAC and sanctions watchlists
Calculate net distribution amount after applicable income tax withholding
Process mandatory 20% federal income tax withholding for eligible rollover distributions paid to participant
Disburse funds via check, wire, or direct rollover transfer to receiving institution
Process force-out cash-outs for account balances below plan-defined threshold
Process automatic rollover to IRA for force-outs between $1,000 and $7,000 per plan document
Issue 1099-R for taxable distributions by January 31 following distribution year
Terminate participant account upon full distribution and archive records

subProcesses.name: Plan Loan & Hardship Withdrawal Administration
steps: Validate participant loan eligibility — vested balance, outstanding loan count, and plan loan policy limits
Calculate maximum loan amount per IRS Section 72(p) — lesser of 50% of vested benefit or $50,000
Process loan origination and establish amortization schedule with payroll deduction instructions
Confirm loan promissory note execution and transmit repayment instructions to plan sponsor payroll
Monitor loan repayments and identify missed payments approaching cure period expiration
Issue cure period notices and process deemed distributions for loans in default beyond cure period
Review hardship withdrawal request against IRS safe-harbor criteria and plan-document hardship definition
Verify participant has exhausted other plan resources available before approving hardship withdrawal
Obtain required documentation for non-safe-harbor hardship withdrawals
Process hardship withdrawal disbursement with mandatory income tax withholding
Apply tax reporting for hardship distributions — 1099-R with distribution code for early withdrawal
Report plan loan portfolio — outstanding balances, delinquency rates, and deemed distributions — to compliance

subProcesses.name: Plan Required Minimum Distribution Administration
steps: Identify RMD-eligible participants — age 73 or older per SECURE 2.0 rules — and beneficiary distributions
Calculate annual RMD amounts using IRS Uniform Lifetime Table or Beneficiary Table as applicable
Notify participants of RMD obligation and capture payment frequency and withholding elections
Process RMD payments by December 31 statutory deadline and April 1 for initial year of eligibility
Track cumulative RMD payments against calculated annual requirement throughout the year
Identify missed or insufficient RMDs and initiate correction process
Support participant submission of IRS Form 5329 for excise tax abatement on missed RMDs
Process beneficiary RMDs for inherited accounts under applicable distribution rules
Apply 10-year rule or stretch IRA rules for beneficiary distributions per SECURE Act requirements
Issue 1099-R for all RMD distributions with correct distribution code
Report RMD compliance statistics and correction activity to ERISA compliance team
Archive RMD calculation records and payment confirmation per IRS retention requirements

subProcesses.name: Nondiscrimination Testing & Limit Compliance
steps: Collect and scrub annual census data from plan sponsor — compensation, hours, eligibility, and HCE/NHCE classification
Validate census data completeness and resolve discrepancies with plan sponsor before running tests
Run ADP test — compare average deferral percentages of HCEs to NHCEs and determine pass or fail
Run ACP test — compare average contribution percentages including employer match for HCEs vs. NHCEs
Run top-heavy test and calculate minimum contribution requirements if plan is top-heavy
Run coverage test under IRC Section 410(b) to confirm sufficient NHCE coverage
Monitor 402(g) elective deferral limits and 415 annual additions limits for each participant throughout the year
Process corrective distributions and refunds to HCEs for failed ADP/ACP tests within 2.5-month deadline
Apply 10% excise tax on late corrective distributions and report to finance
Support EPCRS self-correction and VCP filings for plan document and operational failures
Distribute corrective distribution notices to affected participants with required explanations
Report nondiscrimination test results and corrective actions to plan sponsor and compliance

subProcesses.name: Form 5500 Filing & Plan Audit Support
steps: Compile plan-year financial data — beginning and ending assets, contributions, distributions, and expenses
Compile participant count data — active, terminated vested, retired, and deceased participants
Prepare Form 5500 annual return and all applicable schedules — Schedule A, C, D, G, H, or I
Coordinate independent plan auditor engagement for large-plan filers
Provide auditor access to participant records, transaction data, trust records, and plan documents
Respond to auditor requests and findings and process plan audit adjustments
Obtain plan sponsor and trustee signatures on Form 5500 and audit report
Submit Form 5500 filing via EFAST2 by deadline — July 31 or extended deadline with Form 5558
Track IRS and DOL acceptance confirmation and respond to correspondence on filing issues
Prepare and distribute Summary Annual Report to participants within two months of filing
Archive Form 5500 filings and audit reports per ERISA record-retention requirements
Report filing status and audit findings to plan sponsor and operations compliance team

subProcesses.name: Fee Disclosure & Participant Notice Administration
steps: Compile plan and investment fee data — plan administration fees, investment management expenses, and transaction fees
Calculate per-participant fee allocation for plan-level administrative charges
Produce 404(a)(5) participant fee disclosure with all required investment and plan fee information
Distribute 404(a)(5) disclosures to participants annually and within 90 days of plan entry for new participants
Produce 408(b)(2) service-provider fee disclosures for plan sponsor review and retention
Distribute annual plan notices — safe-harbor notice, QDIA notice, auto-enrollment notice, and fee notice
Distribute blackout period notices at least 30 days in advance of any investment blackout
Track delivery evidence for all required notices and maintain documentation for DOL audit readiness
Remediate disclosure failures — identify missed recipients and re-issue notices with documentation of remediation
Update disclosure content when plan fees, investment options, or regulatory requirements change
Monitor regulatory changes to ERISA disclosure rules and update notice templates and timelines
Report notice distribution completion and any remediation activity to ERISA compliance team

subProcesses.name: Billing Mode Setup & Premium Notice Generation
steps: Establish billing account at policy inception with modal premium schedule and billing mode election
Set up EFT draft authorization and collect bank account or card information per NACHA requirements
Configure list bill and payroll deduction arrangements for employer-sponsored or group policies
Assign billing cycle and generate first-bill data record for premium notice production
Generate and distribute premium notices via mail, email, or portal per customer preference
Apply statutory advance-notice requirements for premium due dates by state and line
Process billing mode changes — annual to monthly, direct to list bill — upon insured request
Update payor information and redirect billing for lienholder-pay or third-party-pay arrangements
Validate that billing account is synchronized with policy administration system premium amounts
Reconcile billing records to policy in-force file to identify billing and policy mismatches
Log billing setup actions in audit trail and confirm billing activation with policy team
Report billing setup completion for new business cohort to finance and operations

subProcesses.name: Premium Collection & Payment Processing
steps: Execute scheduled EFT drafts and receive remittance files from list bill sponsors on billing cycle date
Process inbound payments received via lockbox, web portal, IVR, and agency sweep
Apply payments to correct policy or contract records using policy number and billing account matching
Reconcile list bill remittances to billed census and identify overpayments, underpayments, and missing remitters
Process flexible premium payments for universal life and annuity products and test tax qualification limits
Handle returned payments and NSF reversals — reverse applied payment and trigger return-payment notice
Apply partial payments per contract terms and calculate remaining balance
Verify qualified contribution limits and tax year coding for IRA and qualified annuity payments
Log all payment transactions in payment ledger with date, amount, source, and policy reference
Reconcile daily payment receipts to bank clearing account and resolve bank reconciliation breaks
Report daily collection totals and outstanding receivables balance to treasury and finance
Escalate aged receivables and non-pay cancellation candidates to collections management

subProcesses.name: Cash-with-Application & Premium Suspense Management
steps: Log cash received with application and unallocated receipts to suspense account immediately upon receipt
Record suspense item with source, amount, date, and available identifying information
Research and match suspense items to pending applications or existing policy records
Contact agent or applicant for clarification on unidentifiable suspense items within aging threshold
Age suspense register and escalate items exceeding 30-day hold limit to supervisory review
Return unresolvable funds to remitter with written explanation within state-mandated timeframe
Refer aged unresolvable items to unclaimed property and escheatment process where required by state law
Apply matched suspense items to correct policy and reverse original suspense entry
Reconcile suspense account balance daily and confirm zero unresolved items beyond aging threshold
Log all suspense research and resolution actions with supporting documentation
Report suspense aging summary to finance and compliance monthly
Close resolved suspense records and archive documentation per record-retention policy

subProcesses.name: Grace Period & Lapse Billing Administration
steps: Identify past-due premiums by scanning billing records against expected payment dates
Start grace period counter per state statute and policy-type requirements
Generate and distribute grace period notice with amount due, due date, and lapse consequences
Issue statutory pending-lapse notice if premium remains unpaid at statutory advance-notice point
Monitor for payment receipt during grace period and halt lapse notification if premium received
Apply waiver-of-premium credit for policyowners with approved disability claims
Process automatic premium loan election at grace period expiry for eligible life policies
Apply nonforfeiture option per default policy election when premium loan is unavailable
Trigger lapse notification to policy administration and stop future billing runs
Calculate return premium for cancelled policies and transmit to premium refund processing
Quote reinstatement requirements — back premium, fees, and evidence of insurability — upon request
Report lapse activity and grace period conversion rates to product and finance management

subProcesses.name: Annuity Purchase Payment Processing
steps: Receive and validate purchase payment instructions against annuity contract terms and investment elections
Apply best-interest review trigger for additional purchase payments per NAIC Model 275 compliance rules
Verify qualified contribution limits and tax year coding for IRA and qualified annuity purchase payments
Check maximum premium limits and anti-money-laundering large-payment review thresholds
Allocate purchase payment to designated subaccounts and indexed crediting options per owner election
Apply purchase payment to fixed account or general account with guaranteed crediting rate
Calculate and accrue applicable state premium tax on purchase payment
Issue payment confirmation to owner and producer showing allocation and updated contract values
Update contract record with new accumulation value and cost-basis information
Transmit purchase payment allocation data to investment operations and general ledger
Log all purchase payment transactions in contract history with tax year and contribution type codes
Report purchase payment volumes and qualified contribution totals to tax reporting and finance

subProcesses.name: Premium Refunds & Overpayment Processing
steps: Identify refund triggers — policy cancellation, short-rate calculation, overpayment, or duplicate payment
Calculate refund amount using applicable pro-rata, short-rate, or return-of-overpayment method
Validate payee entitlement — confirm refund goes to insured, premium payor, or lienholder per policy terms
Obtain required approval for refunds above designated authority thresholds
Screen refund payee against OFAC and sanctions watchlists before disbursement
Transmit approved refund for disbursement via check, EFT reversal, or credit to card
Apply refund adjustments to policy record and update premium accounting ledger
Issue 1099 or tax adjustment documentation for refunds with tax implications
Confirm refund payment cleared and matches expected amount
Resolve payee inquiries regarding refund status and delivery
Log refund transaction with calculation detail, approval, and disbursement confirmation
Report refund volumes and amounts to finance for expense and loss accounting

subProcesses.name: Contact Intake & Case Routing
steps: Receive inbound customer contact via phone, email, chat, portal, or written correspondence
Authenticate caller identity using knowledge-based or multi-factor authentication protocols
Capture contact reason and classify into service category — billing, policy, claims inquiry, complaint, or general
Search customer record and retrieve policy, account, or claim information relevant to inquiry
Log interaction in CRM — channel, contact reason, customer identifier, and timestamp
Apply IVR or digital self-service deflection for routine inquiries eligible for automation
Route complex or escalated contacts to appropriate service queue or specialist team
Set customer expectation for resolution timeframe and provide case reference number
Flag priority contacts — vulnerable customers, regulatory complaints, or high-value accounts — for expedited handling
Distribute work item to assigned representative with full context from intake
Monitor queue volumes and trigger overflow routing protocols when thresholds are exceeded
Record intake outcome and advance case to resolution stage

subProcesses.name: Service Inquiry Resolution
steps: Review routed case and confirm scope of customer inquiry against policy or claim record
Authenticate customer identity at point of resolution if not completed at intake
Research policy terms, coverage details, billing history, or claim status using relevant systems
Access claims system to provide status updates, payment details, or adjuster contact information
Answer coverage interpretation questions within service authority and escalate to underwriting when beyond authority
Process routine in-scope service actions — address change, payment method update, document requests
Escalate inquiry to specialist, supervisor, or external team if resolution requires elevated authority
Communicate resolution clearly to customer and confirm understanding
Document interaction outcome, resolution actions taken, and any commitments made
Issue follow-up correspondence or confirmation documents where required
Schedule callback or follow-up contact if full resolution cannot be achieved in first contact
Close case in CRM and capture first-contact resolution indicator for quality reporting

subProcesses.name: Self-Service Portal & Digital Channel Operations
steps: Monitor portal availability, uptime, and authentication success rates against SLA targets
Review digital self-service utilization metrics — transactions completed, abandonment rates, and error events
Identify transactions failing in digital channels and triggering agent-assisted fallback contacts
Configure portal content updates — FAQs, document templates, coverage summaries, and claim instructions
Coordinate with IT to resolve portal defects and prioritize customer-facing fixes
Administer digital document delivery preferences and consent records per e-delivery regulations
Support customer onboarding to portal — enrollment, credential recovery, and access troubleshooting
Manage digital identity verification for sensitive self-service transactions — beneficiary change and bank update
Review accessibility compliance for digital channels per ADA and state digital-equity requirements
Produce monthly digital channel utilization report and deflection rate analysis
Evaluate enhancements to digital workflows based on customer journey analytics
Escalate systemic digital channel failures to IT service management with business-impact context

subProcesses.name: Producer & Broker Service Support
steps: Receive service request from producer, broker, or managing general agent via agency portal or phone
Authenticate agency identity and confirm appointment status before disclosing policy information
Retrieve policy or account records for agency's book of business per data-access entitlement
Process agency-submitted service requests — endorsements, certificates, loss runs, and policy copies
Respond to new-business bind and issuance status inquiries within agreed service level
Provide billing, payment, and commission statement information to authorized agency contacts
Resolve billing discrepancy or commission dispute cases with billing and finance teams
Issue evidence of insurance certificates and additional insured endorsements on agency request
Escalate complex coverage or underwriting questions to underwriting service desk
Document all agency interactions and service actions in agency service log
Report recurring agency service issues to distribution management for producer support improvement
Close agency service case and confirm resolution with requesting contact

subProcesses.name: Service Quality Monitoring & Coaching
steps: Define quality monitoring standards — call criteria, documentation requirements, and resolution accuracy
Sample customer interactions for quality review across channels — calls, chats, and written correspondence
Score interactions against quality rubric and document findings per representative
Identify coaching themes — authentication gaps, resolution accuracy, documentation errors, and tone
Deliver individual coaching sessions to representatives with specific behavioral feedback
Track representative improvement trends and escalate persistent performance concerns to supervisors
Calibrate quality scores across evaluators to ensure consistent application of standards
Analyze aggregate quality data to identify team-wide training needs
Update quality standards and call guides when process or product changes occur
Report quality scores, trends, and improvement actions to customer service management
Integrate quality findings into onboarding and ongoing training curriculum
Benchmark internal quality scores against industry best-practice frameworks

subProcesses.name: Customer Experience Insight & Service Improvement
steps: Deploy post-interaction surveys via preferred channel — IVR, SMS, or email — within defined timeframe after contact
Collect and aggregate Net Promoter Score, CSAT, and Customer Effort Score data
Analyze survey results alongside quality monitoring and call recording data to identify service gaps
Identify systemic failure points — repeat contacts, unresolved issues, and escalation drivers
Present service quality findings to operations management in structured monthly review
Prioritize improvement initiatives based on customer impact, volume, and cost-to-serve analysis
Design and implement process or technology changes to address root-cause service failures
Communicate service updates to front-line staff via briefings and knowledge base revisions
Monitor post-change performance metrics to confirm improvement realization
Benchmark service performance against industry standards and peer carrier benchmarks
Integrate voice-of-customer insights into product, underwriting, and claims process reviews
Report service improvement outcomes and remaining gap areas to senior leadership

subProcesses.name: Inbound Mail & Document Intake
steps: Receive inbound mail, fax, email attachments, and portal uploads at centralized document intake
Sort and batch inbound documents by business unit, product line, and document type
Scan paper documents and apply quality verification — legibility, completeness, and orientation
Index scanned documents by policy number, claim number, or contract identifier
Classify document type using automated classification rules or manual review queue
Route classified documents to appropriate work queues — new business, endorsements, claims, and service
Apply document retention classification at intake — permanent, limited-retention, or destroy-after-processing
Log all received documents in document management system with receipt timestamp and source channel
Flag urgent or time-sensitive documents — grace-period responses, regulatory submissions, and court orders
Confirm successful routing of documents and notify requesting business units of availability
Monitor intake volumes and backlogs against SLA targets
Report daily document intake volumes and routing accuracy metrics to operations management

subProcesses.name: Policy Document Composition & Distribution
steps: Receive document production request from policy administration system upon issuance or change event
Select applicable forms, endorsements, and mandatory notices based on state, product, and coverage selections
Compose document package using document management template engine with variable data insertion
Apply state-specific form versions and ensure all required statutory language is included
Perform pre-distribution quality review — variable data accuracy, form completeness, and readability
Determine preferred delivery channel per customer or agent preference — mail, email, or portal
Distribute documents via selected channel and obtain delivery confirmation or e-consent acknowledgment
Post documents to policyholder online portal and confirm portal availability
Archive distributed documents to policy record in document management system
Record delivery confirmation detail — date, channel, and recipient — in policy history
Process document re-issuance requests for lost, damaged, or undelivered items
Report document distribution volumes, channel mix, and delivery failure rates monthly

subProcesses.name: Regulatory & Compliance Correspondence Administration
steps: Receive regulatory correspondence — DOI inquiries, market conduct requests, and examination notices
Log regulatory correspondence with receipt date, regulatory body, required response deadline, and topic
