Document Findings in a formal governance record including decisions, rationale, and accountability assignments
Present Investment Review Board with capital deployment efficiency metrics and ROI actuals
Report & Remediate governance actions by assigning owners and confirming resolution at next review cycle
Escalate unresolved governance actions to Chief Portfolio Officer or equivalent executive for directive
Archive governance records and publish annual Portfolio Performance Report for Board Risk & Audit Committee

subProcesses.name: PMO Standards & Delivery Methodology
steps: Maintain and publish the PMO delivery methodology, templates, and standards library
Review and update PMO standards annually incorporating lessons learned from completed projects
Manage version control of all methodology documents and communicate updates to the project manager community
Deliver PMO capability development programme including project management training and certification
Assess project manager competency against the PMO skills framework and provide targeted development
Operate a community of practice for project and programme managers across the enterprise
Benchmark PMO maturity against industry standards (OPM3, P3M3) and develop improvement roadmap
Facilitate post-project reviews and incorporate findings into methodology updates
Provide methodology guidance and coaching to project managers on complex or novel delivery challenges
Present PMO standards update and methodology improvement plan to PMO leadership annually

subProcesses.name: PMO Continuous Improvement
steps: Define PMO continuous improvement objectives aligned to delivery quality and portfolio performance goals
Collect delivery performance data (on-time, on-budget, benefits realization rates) to identify improvement opportunities
Conduct root-cause analysis on recurring delivery failures and prioritize improvement interventions
Develop PMO improvement roadmap with specific initiatives, owners, and target completion dates
Implement approved PMO improvement initiatives and track progress against milestones
Measure the impact of completed improvement initiatives against baseline delivery metrics
Share successful improvement outcomes through the PMO community of practice and methodology updates
Manage the PPM tool administration including configuration, user access, and data quality governance
Produce PMO performance metrics report covering on-time, on-budget, and benefits delivery rates
Present PMO continuous improvement plan and outcomes to PMO leadership and Portfolio Committee annually

subProcesses.name: Audit Readiness & Compliance Reporting
steps: Maintain a compliance obligations register for all project and portfolio regulatory reporting requirements
Ensure project documentation standards meet internal audit and regulatory examination requirements
Coordinate with Internal Audit on PMO audit schedule and facilitate evidence collection for audit fieldwork
Track and remediate internal audit findings related to project delivery and benefits governance
Prepare regulatory compliance submissions related to programme delivery (e.g., model risk governance, change management attestations)
Conduct annual PMO self-assessment against internal control framework and document results
Maintain records retention schedule for project artefacts and ensure records are held for required periods
Brief project managers on audit readiness requirements and verify documentation completeness at project close
Support external auditor requests for project delivery evidence during annual financial audit
Report PMO compliance status and open audit findings to the Chief Risk Officer quarterly

subProcesses.name: Knowledge Management & Lessons Learned Repository
steps: Operate the enterprise project knowledge base and ensure lessons-learned records are current and searchable
Define a structured taxonomy for categorising lessons by project type, phase, and risk theme
Facilitate lessons-learned workshops at project close and capture insights in the knowledge base
Identify high-value lessons and promote them through the PMO community of practice and methodology updates
Conduct periodic knowledge base reviews to retire outdated content and validate accuracy of retained lessons
Enable project managers to search the knowledge base during project planning to pre-empt known risks
Measure knowledge base utilisation and assess impact on delivery quality metrics
Share cross-industry benchmarking insights through PMO learning events and published delivery guidance
Maintain supplier performance records and incorporate vendor lessons into procurement guidance
Report knowledge management programme outcomes to PMO leadership as part of annual capability review

subProcesses.name: PMO Tool Administration & Performance Reporting
steps: Manage PPM tool administration including user provisioning, access control, and system configuration
Define and enforce data quality standards for project attributes, milestones, and financial data in the PPM tool
Conduct monthly data quality audits of the PPM tool and remediate missing or inaccurate project records
Develop and maintain standard PMO reports and dashboards for portfolio, programme, and project stakeholders
Onboard new project managers to the PPM tool with structured training and guided data-entry walkthrough
Manage PPM tool upgrades and configuration changes through the change control process
Coordinate with IT on PPM tool integration with Finance, HR, and timesheet systems
Produce weekly PMO operational report summarising active project count, stage distribution, and health indicators
Report PPM tool utilisation and compliance metrics to PMO leadership on a quarterly basis
Evaluate PMO tooling against evolving delivery needs and propose enhancements or replacements as required

subProcesses.name: Risk Universe & Taxonomy Maintenance
steps: Define and maintain the enterprise risk taxonomy aligned to ORSA and regulatory frameworks
Catalogue all risk categories (strategic, insurance, credit, market, operational, liquidity) in the risk register
Assign risk owners and accountable executives for each taxonomy node
Conduct annual taxonomy review against emerging risks and industry benchmarks
Identify and document new risk categories triggered by business strategy or regulatory change
Validate taxonomy updates with the Chief Risk Officer and Risk Committee
Publish updated risk taxonomy to all risk owners and governance bodies
Archive prior-year taxonomy versions and document rationale for changes
Align taxonomy mappings to the RCSA and control framework

subProcesses.name: Risk and Regulatory Obligation Assessment
steps: Identify risks through workshops, event data, control self-assessments, and regulatory intelligence
Assess inherent risk likelihood and impact using validated scoring matrices
Evaluate design and operating effectiveness of key controls for each risk
Determine residual risk rating and compare against board-approved risk appetite thresholds
Select risk treatment: accept, mitigate, transfer, or avoid, and document rationale
Assign risk treatment owners and agree remediation timelines
Monitor risk indicators and trigger thresholds on a monthly basis
Prepare and file ORSA Summary Report with state insurance regulators
Aggregate risk profile into enterprise heat map and trend analysis
Report residual risk positions and appetite breaches to Board Risk Committee

subProcesses.name: Risk Appetite Framework & Limits Governance
steps: Draft annual risk appetite statement aligned to strategic plan and capital position
Define quantitative risk tolerances and limits for each material risk category
Obtain Board approval of risk appetite statement and tolerance thresholds
Cascade appetite limits to business unit risk owners and embed in planning processes
Monitor limit utilization monthly using risk dashboards and early-warning indicators
Investigate and escalate limit breaches to senior management within defined SLAs
Propose limit recalibrations when business model or capital position changes materially
Document limit governance decisions and maintain version-controlled appetite register
Report aggregate appetite utilization to Board Risk Committee each quarter

subProcesses.name: Stress Testing & Scenario Analysis
steps: Define annual stress-testing programme including regulatory and management scenarios
Design severe but plausible scenarios in consultation with business units and Actuarial
Source historical loss data, capital model outputs, and macroeconomic variables
Run stress scenarios through the capital model and financial projection engine
Assess impact on RBC ratio, liquidity position, and earnings under each scenario
Prepare reverse stress-test analysis to identify failure points and risk concentrations
Review results with CRO, CFO, and business unit heads and agree management actions
Incorporate scenario results into ORSA narrative and regulatory submissions
Present stress-test findings to Board Risk Committee with commentary on capital resilience
Archive scenario assumptions, model runs, and sign-off documentation

subProcesses.name: Emerging Risk Identification & Horizon Scanning
steps: Scan regulatory bulletins, industry publications, CRO Forum papers, and IAIS guidance for emerging risks
Assess relevance and potential materiality of each emerging risk to ABC Insurance Group
Engage business unit subject matter experts to evaluate likelihood and exposure
Add validated emerging risks to the risk register with initial impact assessment
Commission deep-dive analysis on high-priority emerging risks as required
Incorporate emerging risk intelligence into the annual stress-testing programme
Report top emerging risks and horizon-scanning findings to Board Risk Committee
Monitor selected emerging risks quarterly until they are resolved or absorbed into the taxonomy

subProcesses.name: Risk Reporting & Committee MI
steps: Collect risk data from RCSA, loss event, KRI, and model outputs at month end
Validate data completeness and reconcile discrepancies with risk owners
Produce the enterprise risk dashboard with heat maps, trend indicators, and limit utilization
Prepare the monthly Executive Risk Report for CRO and CEO review
Compile the quarterly Board Risk Committee pack including key risk indicators and emerging risks
Draft the Annual Report risk management disclosures in accordance with NAIC and GAAP requirements
Coordinate with Actuarial and Finance on stress-test results and capital impact narratives
Distribute final reports to committee members and maintain distribution audit trail
Archive approved reports and supporting data packages per records retention policy

subProcesses.name: Risk Culture & Awareness Programme
steps: Design the annual risk culture assessment survey and distribute to all staff
Analyse survey results and identify culture gaps by division and seniority level
Develop targeted risk awareness training modules for identified gaps
Deliver mandatory risk training to all staff, tracking completion rates in the LMS
Run risk culture workshops for senior leadership and risk champions network
Embed risk considerations into performance objectives and appraisal frameworks
Measure culture improvement KPIs and report progress to Board Risk Committee
Publish risk culture results in the annual ORSA and corporate governance disclosures

subProcesses.name: Operational Risk & Control Self-Assessment
steps: Schedule and communicate the RCSA cycle to all business unit risk owners
Facilitate RCSA workshops to identify operational risks within each process area
Score inherent risk likelihood and impact using the enterprise risk scoring matrix
Identify and document key controls for each risk, including control owner and frequency
Rate control design adequacy and operating effectiveness through testing evidence
Calculate residual risk rating and flag appetite breaches for escalation
Consolidate RCSA outputs into the enterprise operational risk register
Review and challenge RCSA results with second-line risk managers
Obtain business unit sign-off on final RCSA outputs
Report RCSA results and risk profile changes to the Operational Risk Committee

subProcesses.name: Loss Event Capture & Root-Cause Analysis
steps: Intake operational loss events from business units via the loss event reporting system
Classify losses by Basel II event type and business line for regulatory reporting
Investigate root cause using structured techniques (5-whys, Ishikawa) and document findings
Quantify gross loss, recovery, and net loss amounts and validate with Finance
Assess whether the event represents a near-miss or boundary event requiring control enhancement
Escalate high-severity events to CRO and Audit Committee within 24 hours
Agree and track corrective actions with business unit owners
Update the loss event database and cross-reference against the RCSA risk register
Prepare operational loss trend analysis for monthly Operational Risk Committee pack
Feed loss data into the capital model for advanced measurement approach inputs

subProcesses.name: Key Risk Indicator Monitoring
steps: Define KRI library aligned to the enterprise risk taxonomy and business unit risk profiles
Set green/amber/red thresholds for each KRI in consultation with risk owners
Collect KRI data from source systems and business unit submissions monthly
Validate KRI data quality and reconcile anomalies with data owners
Produce KRI dashboard highlighting threshold breaches and adverse trends
Investigate amber and red KRI breaches and agree management actions with owners
Escalate persistent red KRIs to the relevant risk committee with recommended responses
Review KRI library relevance annually and update thresholds for changed risk profile
Report KRI status in the enterprise risk dashboard and board pack

subProcesses.name: Model Risk Management
steps: Maintain a complete model inventory covering all pricing, reserving, capital, and credit models
Assign model risk tier (high/medium/low) based on materiality and complexity
Conduct independent model validation for new and materially changed models prior to deployment
Review model assumptions, methodology, and limitations during validation
Document validation findings and conditions for approval in the model validation report
Obtain model approval from the Model Risk Committee before production deployment
Monitor model performance through ongoing back-testing and outcome analysis
Manage model change requests including impact assessment and re-validation triggers
Retire decommissioned models from the inventory and archive documentation
Report model risk profile and validation pipeline status to the CRO quarterly

subProcesses.name: TPRM Intake, Tiering & Due Diligence
steps: Intake vendor need requests from business units and assign risk tier (critical/high/medium/low)
Conduct due diligence on vendor financial stability, security posture, and regulatory compliance
Screen vendor and beneficial owners against OFAC, PEP, and adverse media databases
Assess data privacy and cyber risk exposure associated with vendor access to ABC systems
Review draft contract for mandatory risk, data protection, and audit-right clauses
Coordinate contract red-line review with Legal and Procurement
Obtain third-party risk sign-off from the TPRM function before contract execution
Onboard vendor in the third-party risk management system with assigned risk tier and owner
Issue vendor access credentials and confirm data-handling obligations with the vendor
Notify Information Security of any vendor with access to ABC production environments

subProcesses.name: TPRM Ongoing Monitoring & Exit Management
steps: Conduct periodic risk reviews of in-scope vendors per their risk tier (annually for critical, biannually for high)
Gather and assess updated due diligence documentation, SOC 2 reports, and compliance attestations
Reassess vendor risk tier and recertify or escalate where risk has increased
Review SLA performance metrics and flag persistent service failures for remediation
Track vendor-related incidents and integrate findings into the operational risk register
Manage vendor remediation plans for identified risk gaps and validate closure evidence
Initiate offboarding upon contract termination or vendor exit decision
Verify data return, destruction, or transfer obligations are fulfilled before final closeout
Revoke all vendor access to ABC systems and confirm with Information Security
Archive vendor risk file and document rationale for offboarding in the TPRM system

subProcesses.name: Insurance Risk Appetite & Accumulation Monitoring
steps: Define catastrophe and accumulation limits by peril, geography, and line of business
Ingest policy-level exposure data from underwriting systems into the accumulation engine
Run modelled loss estimates for peak perils using catastrophe model outputs (RMS/AIR)
Compare modelled PML and TIV concentrations against board-approved accumulation limits
Identify and escalate limit breaches to CUO and CRO with recommended actions
Coordinate reinsurance purchase adjustments with Actuarial and Reinsurance to remedy breaches
Produce monthly accumulation monitoring report for the Underwriting Risk Committee
Refresh accumulation limits annually as part of the risk appetite review cycle

subProcesses.name: Regulatory Change Management
steps: Monitor regulatory publications from NAIC, state DOIs, SEC, and federal agencies continuously
Ingest and log all regulatory changes in the regulatory change management register
Triage each change for applicability to ABC Insurance Group's lines of business and jurisdictions
Assign regulatory change owner and impact assessment lead for each applicable item
Assess operational, financial, and compliance impact including gap analysis against current practices
Implement required controls, policy updates, and system changes before effective date
Test implemented controls and document evidence of compliance readiness
Report regulatory change pipeline and implementation status to Compliance Committee monthly
Close completed regulatory change items and archive implementation evidence
Update the compliance obligation register to reflect new or modified requirements

subProcesses.name: Policy & Procedure Governance
steps: Maintain the master policy register including policy owner, version, and review schedule
Trigger policy review cycles aligned to regulatory change, incidents, or calendar schedule
Draft or update policy content in consultation with subject matter experts and Legal
Conduct stakeholder review and incorporate feedback from affected business units
Obtain senior management or Board approval for policies designated as Board-level
Publish approved policies on the intranet and communicate changes to all affected staff
Monitor policy attestation completion rates and escalate non-compliance to line managers
Archive superseded policy versions and maintain version-controlled history
Report policy currency and attestation status to the Compliance Committee quarterly

subProcesses.name: Compliance Testing & Control Surveillance
steps: Develop the annual compliance testing plan based on the compliance risk assessment
Identify controls in scope for each testing cycle and document testing methodology
Request and gather evidence samples from business units within agreed timelines
Assess control design adequacy against regulatory requirements and internal policies
Test operating effectiveness through transaction sampling, observation, and re-performance
Rate control effectiveness and document findings with root-cause analysis
Communicate draft findings to control owners for factual accuracy review
Agree remediation actions and timelines for all control failures identified
Issue final testing report to Compliance Committee and relevant business unit heads
Track remediation completion and re-test controls where significant failures occurred

subProcesses.name: Compliance Issue Response
steps: Intake and triage compliance issues from self-identification, audits, or regulatory findings
Classify the issue by severity (critical/major/minor) and regulatory obligation affected
Assign compliance investigation lead and notify CCO where severity is major or critical
Investigate the potential breach through document review, interviews, and data analysis
Assess whether a reportable breach has occurred and determine regulatory notification obligations
Execute the response plan including voluntary disclosure, remediation, and policy update
Prepare and submit regulatory breach notification within required timeframes where applicable
Capture root-cause findings and update the compliance risk register
Implement control enhancements to prevent recurrence and validate effectiveness
Close the issue after evidence of remediation is validated and file in the compliance register

subProcesses.name: Regulator Engagement & Examinations
steps: Maintain a central regulator relationship log with contact history and outstanding items
Receive and log regulator inquiries, information requests, and examination notices
Assign examination coordinator and business unit leads for each regulatory examination
Prepare and deliver examination opening presentations and document request responses
Coordinate market conduct examinations and MCAS filing submissions within regulatory deadlines
Prepare regulatory notifications, filings, and prior approval submissions
Review draft examination findings with the CRO and CCO and prepare response submissions
Negotiate examination findings with examiners and agree remediation commitments
Monitor fulfilment of regulatory commitments and prepare status updates for regulators
Maintain the regulator engagement log and archive all examination correspondence

subProcesses.name: Remediation Action Tracking
steps: Log all compliance issues and audit findings in the action-tracking system with unique identifiers
Assign action owners and agree target completion dates at the point of issue
Communicate open action items to owners via automated reminders on agreed cadence
Track evidence submission from action owners and validate sufficiency of remediation evidence
Validate evidence quality against the original finding and control requirement
Escalate overdue or at-risk actions to Compliance Committee and business unit heads
Close validated actions in the tracking system and notify issue-raising function
Produce weekly aged-action report highlighting overdue items by owner and severity
Summarise remediation progress in the monthly Compliance Committee MI pack
Report persistent systemic failures to the Board Audit and Compliance Committee

subProcesses.name: Compliance Governance & Reporting
steps: Aggregate compliance management information and key compliance metrics at month end
Analyse trends in compliance breaches, control failures, and regulatory change pipeline
Prepare the monthly Compliance Committee report including MI dashboards and key issues
Compile the quarterly Board Audit and Compliance Committee pack
Maintain the compliance risk register and update risk ratings based on testing outcomes
Coordinate Annual Compliance Certification process with business unit compliance officers
Prepare regulatory reporting submissions including market conduct annual statement (MCAS)
Report compliance status to Board and senior management in line with governance calendar
Maintain records of all governance meetings, decisions, and agreed actions

subProcesses.name: AML Programme Governance
steps: Maintain and annually update the written AML programme in compliance with BSA/AML requirements
Designate the BSA/AML Compliance Officer and document responsibilities in the programme
Conduct annual AML risk assessment to identify and rate money laundering risks by product and channel
Develop risk-based AML policies and procedures for customer due diligence, EDD, and transaction monitoring
Obtain Board approval of the annual AML risk assessment and programme updates
Coordinate independent AML programme audit with Internal Audit or external reviewer
Manage and track AML programme audit findings through to closure
Report AML programme status and key metrics to Board Audit Committee annually

subProcesses.name: Customer Due Diligence & KYC
steps: Collect and verify customer identity documents at policy inception in accordance with CIP requirements
Screen applicants against OFAC SDN list, PEP databases, and adverse media sources
Assign initial AML risk rating (low/medium/high) based on customer, product, and geographic risk factors
Apply enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers including beneficial ownership verification
Obtain senior management approval for business relationships with PEP or high-risk customers
Conduct periodic KYC refresh reviews aligned to customer risk rating (annual for high, triennial for low)
Update customer risk rating when trigger events occur (e.g., large premium, change in beneficial owner)
Document all CDD and EDD findings in the customer risk file
Escalate unresolved CDD gaps to the BSA/AML Compliance Officer for relationship decision
Archive CDD records per BSA five-year retention requirements

subProcesses.name: Transaction Monitoring & Alert Investigation
steps: Define and maintain AML transaction monitoring rules tuned to insurance product risk profiles
Run automated transaction monitoring scenarios against premium payments, claims, and surrenders
Triage generated alerts by priority score and assign to analysts for investigation
Gather account history, transaction records, and customer profile information for each alert
Conduct analyst review and document findings including pattern analysis and risk assessment
Escalate complex or high-risk alerts to senior AML analyst or BSA/AML Compliance Officer
Dismiss false-positive alerts with documented rationale and feedback to tune detection rules
File Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) with FinCEN within 30 calendar days of determination
Track SAR filing register and maintain confidentiality obligations per BSA
Review transaction monitoring rule performance quarterly and adjust thresholds to reduce false positives

subProcesses.name: Suspicious Activity Reporting
steps: Receive and log referrals of suspected suspicious activity from business units and transaction monitoring
Conduct preliminary review to assess whether the activity meets the SAR filing threshold
Gather all relevant documentation: policy files, payment records, claims data, and correspondence
Investigate the activity using structured AML analysis frameworks and pattern recognition
Consult with Legal where the activity involves potential tipping-off risk or law enforcement contact
Complete the SAR narrative clearly describing the suspicious nature and known facts
Obtain BSA/AML Compliance Officer sign-off before SAR submission
File the SAR electronically via FinCEN BSA E-Filing within the required 30-day window
Maintain the SAR register under strict confidentiality and restrict access to authorised staff only
Conduct 90-day continuing activity review and file continuation SARs where warranted

subProcesses.name: AML Training & Awareness
steps: Design the annual AML training curriculum covering BSA requirements, red flags, and reporting obligations
Tailor training content by role: underwriting, claims, customer service, and management
Deploy mandatory AML training via the LMS and track completion rates by department
Deliver enhanced AML training for high-risk functions and new joiners with customer contact
Assess training effectiveness through knowledge checks and post-training assessments
Remediate knowledge gaps identified through low assessment scores or incidents
Maintain training completion records per BSA retention requirements
Report AML training completion rates to the Compliance Committee and BSA/AML Compliance Officer

subProcesses.name: AML Regulatory Reporting & Recordkeeping
steps: Identify BSA recordkeeping obligations applicable to insurance products including Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs) and related records
Collect and validate source data for CTR preparation from premium payment and disbursement systems
Prepare and file CTRs with FinCEN within required timeframes for cash transactions exceeding the regulatory threshold
Maintain the CTR filing register and archive supporting documentation per BSA five-year retention requirements
Prepare the annual BSA/AML compliance report for Board Audit Committee review
Respond to FinCEN and law enforcement information requests and 314(a) inquiries within mandated timeframes
Coordinate with Legal on Grand Jury subpoenas and law enforcement production requests
Update the AML regulatory reporting calendar annually and track all filing deadlines to completion

subProcesses.name: Sanctions Watchlist & Programme Governance
steps: Maintain and update the enterprise sanctions watchlist database including OFAC SDN, OFAC consolidated lists, UN, EU, and internal blocklists, processing list updates within required timeframes
Tune screening engine parameters including name-matching algorithms, fuzzy-match thresholds, transliteration rules, and list-update automation to optimise hit quality
Conduct periodic OFAC programme reviews and update screening parameters following regulatory guidance changes
Document programme audit trail and maintain evidence of watchlist update processing within mandated timeframes
Obtain senior management and Board review of the annual OFAC/sanctions programme assessment
Coordinate independent programme review with Internal Audit or external compliance reviewer
Manage and track sanctions programme audit findings through to validated closure
Report sanctions programme status and screening metrics to the Financial Crime Committee annually

subProcesses.name: Screening Execution & Alert Adjudication
steps: Screen all new policy applicants, payees, claimants, and beneficiaries against the full consolidated sanctions lists at onboarding and at each material transaction
Re-screen existing policyholders and counterparties on scheduled list-update cycles and on trigger events such as renewal or ownership change
Route potential matches to the sanctions compliance team for manual review and true-hit / false-positive adjudication
Conduct reasonable-cause analysis and document disposition rationale for every alert in the sanctions alert management system
Dismiss confirmed false-positive alerts with documented rationale and use findings to refine screening parameters
Escalate potential true hits to the Senior Sanctions Officer for secondary review before any action
Block transactions and freeze assets immediately upon confirmed OFAC match, notifying Legal and senior management
Produce monthly sanctions screening metrics and alert-disposition report for the Financial Crime Committee

subProcesses.name: Sanctions Violation Response & Regulatory Filing
steps: Declare a confirmed sanctions match and immediately block or reject the transaction in accordance with OFAC requirements
Notify Legal, CCO, and senior management within the established escalation timeframe upon confirmed violation
Conduct an internal investigation to determine the full scope and nature of the potential violation
Assess whether the violation was voluntary, self-disclosed, or egregious in accordance with OFAC enforcement guidelines
File OFAC blocking or reject reports with OFAC within mandated timeframes for confirmed sanctions violations
File Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) or SARs with FinCEN where a sanctions match also indicates suspicious activity
Coordinate with Legal on law enforcement notification and regulatory co-operation obligations
Document all violation response actions and maintain the sanctions violation register for regulatory inspection

subProcesses.name: Financial Crime Intelligence & Typology Analysis
steps: Monitor FinCEN advisories, OFAC guidance, FATF typology reports, and industry financial crime intelligence sources
Assess the relevance of new financial crime typologies to ABC Insurance Group's product and distribution profile
Update transaction monitoring scenarios and screening parameters to reflect emerging financial crime methods
Conduct annual financial crime risk assessment covering money laundering, sanctions, fraud, and bribery risks
Share financial crime intelligence with peer institutions through FinCEN 314(b) information sharing arrangements
Incorporate typology analysis into the AML training curriculum and red-flag guidance for front-line staff
Report emerging financial crime risks and typology updates to the Financial Crime Committee quarterly
Archive financial crime intelligence reports and update the financial crime risk assessment on a rolling basis

subProcesses.name: Anti-Bribery & Corruption Controls
steps: Maintain the enterprise anti-bribery and corruption (ABC) policy aligned to the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and UK Bribery Act where applicable
Conduct annual ABC risk assessment covering all business lines, geographies, and third-party relationships
Screen new and existing intermediaries, agents, and business partners for corruption risk indicators
Apply enhanced due diligence for high-risk intermediaries including government-affiliated entities
Monitor gifts, entertainment, and hospitality declarations through the designated approval workflow
Investigate potential FCPA or bribery incidents and document investigation findings
Prepare and submit mandatory disclosures to regulators or law enforcement where required
Report ABC programme status, incident trends, and control effectiveness to the Compliance Committee annually

subProcesses.name: Financial Crime Committee Governance & Reporting
steps: Prepare the monthly Financial Crime Committee agenda, papers, and MI pack covering AML, sanctions, and fraud metrics
Facilitate the Financial Crime Committee meeting and ensure quorum and governance requirements are met
Record minutes, decisions, and action items from each Financial Crime Committee meeting
Track agreed action items through to closure and report progress at subsequent meetings
Escalate material financial crime risks or incidents to Board Audit Committee as required
Coordinate annual Financial Crime Risk Assessment consolidation and present findings to senior management
Prepare the annual financial crime governance report for the Board covering programme effectiveness
Maintain the Financial Crime Committee terms of reference and update for governance changes annually

subProcesses.name: Market Conduct Risk Assessment & Programme Design
steps: Maintain a market conduct risk assessment aligned to state DOI expectations and NAIC handbooks
Identify market conduct risk indicators across sales, rating, underwriting, claims, and cancellation practices
Develop and maintain market conduct policies, procedures, and standards aligned to state requirements
Design the annual market conduct oversight plan covering surveillance priorities and testing scope
Assign market conduct risk owners by product line and distribution channel
Benchmark market conduct programme design against NAIC Market Regulation Handbook and peer practices
Obtain Compliance Committee approval of the annual market conduct programme plan
Report market conduct programme status and risk assessment results to senior management annually

subProcesses.name: Sales Practices & Conduct Surveillance
steps: Define conduct surveillance metrics covering mis-selling indicators, lapse rates, complaint ratios, and persistency
Monitor agent and distributor conduct KPIs monthly against tolerance thresholds
Investigate outlier agents or branches with conduct indicators above threshold
Review sample sales conversations, illustrations, and application records for suitability
Assess compliance with product disclosure requirements and comparative advertising rules
Issue conduct findings to agency management and agree remediation actions
Escalate systemic conduct failures to CCO and consider regulatory notification where warranted
Track conduct remediation actions through to closure in the compliance action-tracking system
Report conduct surveillance results in the quarterly Market Conduct Committee pack

subProcesses.name: Market Conduct Examination Support
steps: Receive market conduct examination notice from state DOI and acknowledge receipt within deadline
Appoint the examination project manager and establish the cross-functional examination team
Prepare the examination management plan covering timelines, data requests, and communication protocols
Respond to document production requests and track fulfilment in the examination data room
Prepare examination opening presentation materials covering company profile and compliance programme
Review sampled transaction files for accuracy and compliance with state requirements before submission
Coordinate on-site or desktop examination sessions and provide SME access as required
Review and respond to draft examination findings within the regulatory comment period
Negotiate final examination findings and agree corrective action plan where applicable
Monitor corrective action completion and file progress reports with the DOI as required

subProcesses.name: Regulatory Conduct Filings & Disclosure
steps: Coordinate the annual MCAS data collection from business units, validating completeness and accuracy
Review MCAS data for anomalies or adverse ratios that may attract regulatory scrutiny before submission
Prepare and submit the Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) to applicable state DOIs within filing deadlines
Prepare and submit market conduct self-assessment reports to regulators as required
Respond to DOI data calls and ad-hoc market conduct information requests within mandated timeframes
Track and report market conduct filing calendar and completion status to the Compliance Committee
Maintain a filing archive with submission confirmations, regulator acknowledgements, and correspondence
Coordinate with Finance and Actuarial on statistical data accuracy in conduct-related regulatory filings
Report filing completion and any regulator feedback on filed data to the CCO

subProcesses.name: Market Conduct Signal Analysis & Root-Cause Review
steps: Aggregate market conduct signal data monthly including complaint ratios, claim denial rates, and rescission rates by product and channel
Identify systemic conduct trends and emerging risk patterns requiring root-cause investigation
Conduct structured root-cause analysis for high-frequency or high-severity market conduct signal categories
Engage business unit process owners to identify the underlying process, training, or incentive failures
Develop corrective action plans addressing root causes with measurable conduct improvement criteria
Implement process, training, or control changes and set effectiveness review date
Monitor conduct signal volumes for targeted categories post-remediation to confirm improvement
Report root-cause findings and remediation progress to the Compliance Committee quarterly

subProcesses.name: Complaint Oversight & Conduct Pattern Review
steps: Receive complaint data feeds from the Operations complaint management system for market conduct analysis
Classify complaint data by regulatory category (claims handling, billing, cancellation, agent conduct, discrimination) for conduct oversight purposes
Assess whether complaint volumes or patterns indicate potential market conduct violations requiring programme response
Conduct targeted market conduct reviews when complaint patterns suggest systemic non-compliance
Coordinate with Operations and Legal on complaint trends that require regulatory notification or disclosure
Track market conduct commitments arising from complaint-driven regulatory interactions
Incorporate complaint pattern intelligence into the annual market conduct risk assessment
Report complaint-driven market conduct risk indicators to the Compliance Committee

subProcesses.name: Control Framework Design & Documentation
steps: Define the enterprise control framework structure aligned to COSO and applicable regulatory requirements
Catalogue all key controls in the central control register with owner, frequency, and control type
Document control design for each key control including objective, description, and evidence requirements
Assess completeness of control coverage against risk taxonomy and regulatory obligations
Identify and document control gaps and assign owners to implement new controls
Maintain the control register as a living document updated for new risks and process changes
Publish the control framework to business unit control owners and second-line risk teams
Review control framework design against peer benchmarks and regulatory expectations annually

subProcesses.name: Control Ownership & Accountability
steps: Assign named first-line control owners to every key control in the enterprise control register
Communicate control ownership responsibilities and evidence requirements to designated owners
Conduct annual control ownership confirmation to verify alignment after organisational changes
Train control owners on their obligations, evidence standards, and self-assessment requirements
Assess control owner performance in meeting evidence submission and self-assessment deadlines
Escalate unresolved control ownership gaps to business unit heads for timely reassignment
Maintain the control ownership register as the authoritative source for accountability mapping
Report control ownership coverage and gaps to the Compliance Committee quarterly

subProcesses.name: First-Line Control Monitoring
steps: Define the first-line monitoring programme aligned to the control register and risk appetite
Communicate monitoring requirements and evidence standards to business unit control owners
Collect and review first-line control performance evidence on the agreed monitoring cycle
Assess evidence quality and sufficiency against the control design and regulatory standard
Identify and log control performance failures or evidence gaps for escalation
Agree improvement actions with business unit control owners for identified monitoring failures
Consolidate first-line monitoring results into the controls assurance dashboard
Report first-line monitoring results and coverage to the second-line assurance function monthly

subProcesses.name: Three Lines Coordination & Assurance Mapping
steps: Maintain the combined assurance map showing coverage by first, second, and third line for each risk
Facilitate annual assurance planning meetings between Internal Audit, Risk, Compliance, and External Audit
Identify assurance gaps and overlaps from the combined assurance map and agree coverage adjustments
Share risk assessment and control testing results across the three lines to optimise coverage
Coordinate timing of second-line compliance testing and third-line audit to minimise business disruption
Report combined assurance coverage and identified gaps to the Audit Committee annually
Facilitate information sharing protocols between lines to support reliance and efficiency
Assess reliance opportunities on second-line work to inform the Internal Audit plan

subProcesses.name: Assurance Programme Planning & Scheduling
steps: Develop the annual second-line assurance programme aligned to the compliance risk assessment and control register
Prioritise assurance activities using a risk-ranked scoring model covering regulatory exposure and control maturity
Allocate assurance resources across planned testing cycles and control review engagements
Schedule assurance activities to achieve complete coverage within the annual programme cycle
Coordinate assurance scheduling with Internal Audit to avoid concurrent reviews of the same business area
Obtain Compliance Committee approval of the annual assurance programme plan
Monitor programme execution progress quarterly and adjust scheduling for emerging risk priorities
Report assurance programme completion and coverage status to the Compliance Committee

subProcesses.name: Combined Assurance Reporting
steps: Aggregate assurance outputs from first, second, and third line into the combined assurance report
Analyse assurance findings for systemic control themes and root-cause patterns across lines
Prepare the quarterly combined assurance report for Audit Committee and senior management
Highlight residual assurance gaps and areas requiring additional coverage in the report
Coordinate with External Audit on assurance opinions relevant to financial statement assertions
Track agreed assurance improvement actions from the combined report through to closure
Update the assurance map to reflect completed activities and revised risk coverage at year end
Present the annual combined assurance opinion to the Board Audit Committee

subProcesses.name: SOX & Financial Reporting Controls Testing
steps: Identify and scope financial reporting controls in scope for SOX compliance (if applicable) or equivalent programme
Document process flows for in-scope financial reporting processes including key control points
Conduct walkthroughs with process owners to confirm control design and key control documentation
Develop the controls testing programme and sample sizes aligned to PCAOB standards
Execute design effectiveness assessments for all in-scope controls
Execute operating effectiveness testing using attribute sampling and population-based approaches
Document test results, exceptions, and conclusions for each control in testing workpapers
Assess deficiency severity (significant deficiency / material weakness) for each control failure
Agree remediation actions for all deficiencies with process and control owners
Prepare the SOX/financial controls attestation package for CFO and Audit Committee sign-off

subProcesses.name: Regulatory Control Testing
steps: Identify regulatory requirements with specific control obligations requiring periodic testing
Map regulatory obligations to the control register and assign compliance testing coverage
Develop risk-based testing programmes for priority regulatory control categories
Execute testing through transaction sampling, document review, and system query
Assess compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies for each control
Document testing results and control deficiencies with supporting evidence
Communicate draft test findings to business unit control owners for factual accuracy review
Issue final regulatory testing report to the Compliance Committee
Track remediation of regulatory control deficiencies through to validated closure
Incorporate regulatory testing results into the annual compliance risk assessment

subProcesses.name: IT General Controls Testing
steps: Scope IT general controls (ITGCs) for in-scope applications, operating systems, and databases
Review change management controls for segregation of duty and authorisation compliance
Test logical access controls including provisioning, de-provisioning, and privileged access reviews
Assess backup and recovery control effectiveness for critical systems
Test system availability and capacity monitoring controls for key insurance platforms
Review IT operations controls including job scheduling, incident management, and problem management
Document ITGC test results and exceptions in testing workpapers
Assess IT deficiency impact on dependent financial and operational application controls
Report ITGC findings to the CAE and coordinate remediation with Technology leadership
Re-test remediated ITGC deficiencies to confirm control restoration before year-end

subProcesses.name: Operational Controls Testing
steps: Identify operational process controls in scope for the annual testing cycle using the risk-ranked assurance plan
Document the testing scope, control objectives, and sampling methodology for each operational control
Request and obtain transaction samples and supporting evidence from business unit control owners
Execute attribute testing to assess whether each sampled transaction was processed in compliance with the control
Document test exceptions with factual description and reference to the control design requirement
Rate control effectiveness and assess the operational impact of each identified exception
Communicate draft operational testing findings to control owners for factual accuracy confirmation
Agree remediation actions and target completion dates for all identified control failures
Issue final operational controls testing report to the Compliance Committee and relevant business heads
Track remediation to closure and re-test controls where failure rates exceeded materiality thresholds

subProcesses.name: Control Deficiency Management
steps: Log all control deficiencies identified through testing, self-assessment, and audit in the deficiency register
Classify deficiency severity as critical, significant, or moderate based on risk impact and likelihood
Assign remediation owners and target completion dates at point of identification
Develop remediation plans addressing root cause for significant and critical deficiencies
Track remediation progress through regular owner updates in the deficiency management system
Validate closure evidence to confirm the root cause has been addressed and the control is operating
Escalate overdue or unresolved significant deficiencies to the Compliance Committee
Re-test remediated controls to confirm effectiveness before marking the deficiency closed
Report deficiency inventory, trends, and closure rates to the Audit Committee quarterly
Incorporate systemic deficiency themes into the RCSA and risk register updates

subProcesses.name: Controls Testing Quality Assurance
steps: Define quality assurance standards for controls testing workpapers, sampling documentation, and conclusion rationale
Conduct supervisory review of all testing workpapers before findings are communicated to control owners
Perform periodic peer reviews of completed testing files to assess consistency and technical quality
Benchmark testing methodology against PCAOB, IIA, and regulatory guidance updates annually
Identify recurring quality gaps from workpaper reviews and develop targeted training for the testing team
Maintain a quality issues log and track improvement actions through to confirmed remediation
Report testing quality metrics and peer review results to the Head of Controls Assurance quarterly
Incorporate quality assurance findings into the annual testing methodology and standards refresh

subProcesses.name: Risk-Based Audit Planning
steps: Assess the audit universe to identify all auditable entities, processes, and IT systems
Update the risk assessment of each audit entity based on inherent risk, control environment, and change factors
Prioritise audit engagements using a risk-ranked scoring model aligned to the enterprise risk register
Allocate audit resources and hours across engagements to build the draft annual audit plan
Draft the Annual Audit Plan including scope, resource allocation, and coverage rationale
Present the draft plan to the CAE and Audit Committee Chair for pre-approval review
Obtain Audit Committee approval of the Annual Audit Plan at the scheduled committee meeting
Coordinate assurance coverage with external auditors to minimise duplication and maximise reliance
Publish the approved Annual Audit Plan and schedule to relevant stakeholders
Manage mid-year plan adjustments for emerging risks and present changes to the Audit Committee

subProcesses.name: Audit Engagement Execution
steps: Issue the engagement notification letter to the audit client and schedule kick-off meeting
Define the engagement scope, objectives, and key risks in the planning memorandum
Conduct walkthroughs of key processes to understand control design and identify control gaps
Develop the detailed test programme covering key controls, transactions, and risk areas
Execute fieldwork: gather evidence through document review, data analytics, and staff interviews
Assess control design adequacy and test operating effectiveness for each key control
Document all testing workpapers in the audit management system with sign-off by the audit lead
Hold preliminary findings meeting with management to confirm factual accuracy of observations
Rate findings by severity (critical/high/medium/low) using the enterprise finding-rating framework
Agree management responses and remediation action plans for each finding

subProcesses.name: Audit Findings, Ratings & Reporting
steps: Draft the audit report including executive summary, findings, ratings, and management responses
Review draft report with the CAE and senior audit manager for quality and tone
Issue the draft report to audit client management for final management response review
Incorporate final management responses and agreed remediation actions into the report
Issue the final audit report to the audit client, CCO, CRO, and Audit Committee
Log all findings in the issues-tracking database with target closure dates and owners
Present significant findings and thematic audit results to the Audit Committee quarterly
Prepare the Annual Summary of Audit Activity for the Board, covering plan completion and overall opinion
Maintain engagement files and audit evidence in the audit management system per retention policy

subProcesses.name: Findings Remediation Tracking & Closure Validation
steps: Track all open audit findings in the issues-management system with current status and owner
Send automated reminder notifications to action owners at 60, 30, and 7 days before target date
Receive and log remediation evidence submitted by management at or before the target date
Assess whether submitted evidence demonstrates that the root cause has been addressed
Request additional evidence or revised plans where closure evidence is insufficient
Escalate overdue high or critical findings to the CAE and Audit Committee Chair
Conduct post-closure re-testing for critical findings to confirm sustained control improvement
Mark findings as closed in the tracking system after evidence validation is complete
Produce monthly aged-findings report for CAE and management
Report closure rates and overdue items to the Audit Committee as part of the standing agenda

subProcesses.name: Audit Data Analytics & Technology-Enabled Audit
steps: Identify high-value data analytics opportunities across the audit plan
Extract and profile relevant data sets from core systems (policy, claims, finance, HR)
Cleanse and validate data quality before applying analytical procedures
Apply analytical techniques including stratification, duplicate detection, and trend analysis
Run automated continuous monitoring routines on high-risk transaction populations
Interpret analytical results and triage exceptions for audit follow-up
Document data analytics methodology and results in audit workpapers
Report insights from data analytics to engagement teams and Audit Committee
Develop and maintain the internal audit data analytics toolkit and standard scripts

subProcesses.name: Quality Assurance & Improvement Programme
steps: Establish and maintain the QAIP framework aligned to IIA Standards and the IPPF
Conduct ongoing internal quality monitoring including workpaper reviews and engagement supervision
Execute periodic internal self-assessments against IIA Standards across all audit activity
Coordinate external quality assessment by an independent, qualified assessor every five years
Communicate external quality assessment results to senior management and the Audit Committee
Develop the QAIP improvement plan to address internal and external assessment findings
Track QAIP improvement actions and validate completion with the CAE
Monitor audit performance KPIs: plan completion rate, report timeliness, finding closure rate
Report QAIP results and performance metrics to the Audit Committee annually
Benchmark internal audit practices against IIA peer surveys and industry benchmarks

subProcesses.name: Internal Audit Governance & Stakeholder Management
steps: Maintain the Internal Audit Charter, approved by the Audit Committee, documenting scope, authority, and independence
Manage the relationship between the CAE, Audit Committee Chair, and senior management
Prepare and present the CAE's report at each Audit Committee meeting
Coordinate with external auditors on the combined assurance model and reliance framework
Manage Internal Audit's budget, resource capacity, and co-source arrangements
Conduct the annual audit staff performance appraisal and professional development planning
Assess and declare potential independence impairments in accordance with IIA Standards
Maintain the Internal Audit function's conformance with IIA Standards and regulatory expectations
Report Internal Audit independence status and resource adequacy to the Audit Committee annually

subProcesses.name: Business Impact Analysis
steps: Define the scope and methodology for the annual Business Impact Analysis (BIA) cycle
Engage business unit leads to identify critical business services and their dependencies
Assess the financial, regulatory, reputational, and customer impact of service disruption at defined time intervals
Determine Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption (MTPD) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for each service
Identify minimum resource requirements (staff, systems, data, premises) to sustain critical services
Map critical service dependencies on IT systems, third parties, and physical infrastructure
Validate BIA findings with business unit heads and incorporate CRO review
Document approved BIA results in the BCM system and update service criticality register
Use BIA outputs to prioritise Business Continuity Plan (BCP) development and testing

subProcesses.name: Business Continuity Planning
steps: Develop and maintain Business Continuity Plans for each critical business service identified in the BIA
Define activation triggers, command structure, and decision authority in the BCP
Document recovery procedures including manual workarounds, alternate site operations, and interim staffing plans
Assign BCP ownership to named business unit BCM coordinators
Integrate BCP procedures with IT Disaster Recovery Plans to ensure end-to-end recovery alignment
Document key contacts, escalation paths, and vendor emergency contacts in the BCP
Obtain senior management review and sign-off of each BCP before the plan enters live status
Version-control BCP documents and trigger updates following significant business or system changes
Archive prior BCP versions and maintain change log

subProcesses.name: BCM Testing & Exercising
steps: Develop the annual BCM testing programme covering tabletop exercises, simulations, and live failover tests
Schedule tests to cover all critical services within the testing cycle and obtain business unit commitment
Conduct tabletop exercises to test decision-making and communication protocols under simulated scenarios
Execute technology failover tests with IT and validate that RTO targets are met
Conduct workplace recovery tests to confirm alternate site readiness and staff capacity
Observe test execution, capture results, and document gaps and improvement actions
Issue test debrief report with findings and remediation plan to BCM owners and senior management
Track test remediation actions through to closure before the next scheduled test
Report test results and programme completion status to the Board Risk Committee annually

subProcesses.name: BCM Programme Governance & Maintenance
steps: Maintain the BCM policy and framework document approved by the Board Risk Committee
Define BCM governance structure including BCM Committee, business unit coordinators, and executive sponsor
Conduct the annual BCM programme review covering BIA currency, plan quality, and test coverage
Manage the BCM awareness training programme and track completion rates across the organisation
Maintain the BCM system as the authoritative repository for plans, tests, and incident records
Manage BCM-related third-party obligations and include BCM requirements in critical vendor contracts
Report BCM programme maturity and improvement actions to senior management annually
Benchmark BCM programme against ISO 22301 and regulatory expectations and identify gaps

subProcesses.name: IT Disaster Recovery Planning
steps: Maintain the IT Disaster Recovery (DR) strategy aligned to RTO and RPO targets established in the BIA
Identify all critical applications and infrastructure components requiring DR coverage
Document IT DR procedures for each critical system including failover steps, recovery sequences, and rollback processes
Assign IT DR ownership to named Technology leads for each critical application and infrastructure tier
Coordinate DR plan integration with business-side BCPs to ensure end-to-end recovery alignment
Test IT DR procedures annually and validate that RTO and RPO targets are achievable under simulated failure conditions
Document DR test results, gaps, and improvement actions and present findings to Technology leadership
Review and update IT DR plans following significant system changes, infrastructure upgrades, or test failures
Report IT DR programme status and test outcomes to the Board Risk Committee annually

subProcesses.name: Crisis Communications Management
steps: Develop and maintain the crisis communications plan covering internal and external communication protocols
Define communication triggers, approval authorities, and spokesperson responsibilities for each incident severity level
Prepare pre-approved communication templates for common disruption scenarios including regulatory notifications
Maintain a current stakeholder contact directory covering employees, regulators, customers, media, and business partners
Exercise crisis communication protocols as part of the annual BCM testing programme
Coordinate regulatory notifications within mandated timeframes during major operational incidents
Manage media enquiries through the designated spokesperson and communications function during incidents
Document all communications issued during incidents and conduct post-incident review of communications effectiveness

subProcesses.name: Important Business Service Definition
steps: Identify and document important business services from the customer and regulatory perspective
Engage senior management and board to confirm the list of important business services requiring resilience oversight
Set impact tolerances for each important business service aligned to regulatory resilience requirements and customer harm thresholds
Document the rationale for each impact tolerance, including the basis for the timeframe and severity definitions
Obtain Board approval of the important business services list and associated impact tolerances
Communicate impact tolerances to business unit heads and technology teams as operational resilience targets
Review and update the important business services list and tolerances annually and following material business changes
Report the approved important business services framework to regulators as required by supervisory expectations

subProcesses.name: Service Mapping & Dependency Analysis
steps: Map end-to-end delivery of each important business service across people, processes, technology, data, and facilities
Identify third-party dependencies embedded in the delivery of each important business service
Document the interconnections between important business services and shared infrastructure or platforms
Validate service maps with business unit heads, technology owners, and third-party relationship managers
Identify single points of failure and critical dependencies that represent the highest concentration risk
Update service maps following significant organisational, technology, or third-party changes
Archive versioned service maps in the operational resilience system as the authoritative dependency record
Use service maps as the basis for vulnerability identification and resilience investment prioritisation

subProcesses.name: Resilience Vulnerability Identification
steps: Review service maps to identify vulnerabilities in people, processes, technology, and third-party dependencies
Assess each vulnerability for its potential to cause disruption beyond the defined impact tolerance
Prioritise vulnerabilities by severity of impact and likelihood of disruption using a risk-based scoring approach
Engage business unit, technology, and third-party management leads to validate identified vulnerabilities
Develop remediation investment plans to address highest-priority resilience vulnerabilities
Obtain senior management approval of the resilience investment and remediation plan
Track remediation progress against milestones and escalate delays to the Board Risk Committee
Update the vulnerability register following remediation and re-assess residual vulnerability annually

subProcesses.name: Resilience Scenario Testing
steps: Design severe but plausible disruption scenarios targeting the delivery of each important business service
Obtain senior management approval of the annual resilience scenario testing programme
Execute resilience tests including technology failure, third-party outage, and people unavailability scenarios
Assess whether the organisation remains within impact tolerances under each scenario during testing
Document test observations, tolerance breaches, and remediation actions in the resilience testing register
Debrief business unit and technology participants following each test and capture lessons learned
Present resilience test results and tolerance compliance to the Board Risk Committee
Incorporate test findings into the annual operational resilience self-assessment and investment plan

subProcesses.name: Incident Response & Crisis Management Governance
steps: Receive incident notification and invoke the incident response protocol
Convene the Crisis Management Team and activate the incident command structure
Assess the nature, scale, and impact of the incident against predefined severity criteria
Activate the relevant BCP and coordinate recovery actions across business and IT teams
Communicate incident status to senior management, Board, regulators, and customers as required
Manage ongoing incident response through regular crisis bridge calls and status updates
Coordinate regulatory notifications within mandated timeframes for major operational incidents
Document all incident decisions, actions, and communications in the incident log
Declare recovery and stand down the Crisis Management Team after service restoration is confirmed
Conduct post-incident review and capture lessons learned within 30 days of resolution

subProcesses.name: Operational Resilience Regulatory Reporting
steps: Prepare the annual operational resilience self-assessment covering service mapping, vulnerability remediation, and tolerance testing results
Obtain Board review and approval of the annual operational resilience self-assessment before regulatory submission
Submit the operational resilience self-assessment to applicable regulators within required timeframes
Respond to regulatory enquiries and supervisory requests for resilience-related information
Coordinate with regulators on resilience supervisory expectations and examination requests
Monitor resilience metrics and early-warning indicators for critical services monthly
Report operational resilience programme status and tolerance test results to the Board Risk Committee
Archive all regulatory submissions, correspondence, and supporting evidence per records retention policy

subProcesses.name: Security Architecture & Design
steps: Define security architecture principles aligned to control frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001) for insurance operations
Inventory business-critical systems and data assets requiring architectural protection decisions
Design control reference architecture covering preventive, detective, and corrective layers
Map regulatory requirements (NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation, HIPAA, SOC 2) to architecture domains
Conduct threat modeling workshops to identify architecture-level risk and design mitigations
Assess current-state architecture against target security architecture and identify gaps
Obtain CISO and business-unit approval on security architecture decisions and design standards
Publish security architecture patterns and technology selection guidance to IT teams
Track architecture implementation progress against approved design milestones
Review and update security architecture annually or after material technology or business changes

subProcesses.name: Control Framework Management
steps: Select and adopt applicable control frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls) as the enterprise baseline
Map each control domain to the regulatory requirements applicable to the insurance carrier
Assess current-state control coverage against the adopted framework and score maturity
Document control gaps, risk acceptance criteria, and the remediation roadmap for each gap
Assign control ownership to accountable process or technology teams
Publish control standards and baseline configuration guides to implementing IT teams
Track control implementation progress and update coverage scores quarterly
Conduct annual control effectiveness review with internal audit and the CISO
Update control framework mappings when new regulations or framework versions are released
Report control maturity scores and remediation progress to the Board Audit & Risk Committee

subProcesses.name: Cybersecurity Policy & Standards Management
steps: Identify policy requirements from regulatory mandates (NYDFS §500, NAIC Model Law) and business risk appetite
Draft or revise cybersecurity policies, standards, and procedures
Route policy drafts through legal, compliance, and business-line review cycles
Obtain executive sign-off and board-level ratification for material policy changes
Publish approved policies to the enterprise policy repository
Communicate policy changes to affected employees and third parties
Deliver policy-awareness training and track completion rates
Monitor adherence to policies through control testing and audit sampling
Log and track exceptions, waivers, and compensating controls
Retire or supersede outdated policy versions and archive change history

subProcesses.name: Cybersecurity Risk Assessment & Register
steps: Define risk taxonomy and scoring methodology aligned to enterprise risk framework
Conduct annual cyber risk assessment across people, process, and technology domains
Gather threat intelligence to contextualize likelihood of identified risk scenarios
Score inherent risk using likelihood and impact scales approved by the risk committee
Evaluate existing controls and calculate residual risk scores
Record risks, owners, and treatment decisions in the cybersecurity risk register
Present risk register findings to CISO and CRO for prioritization
Assign remediation owners and track treatment plans to closure
Report quarterly risk posture trends to the Board Audit & Risk Committee
Update risk register for material incidents, new threats, or business changes

subProcesses.name: Regulatory Compliance & Audit Management
steps: Maintain compliance calendar for all applicable cybersecurity regulatory submissions (NYDFS, SOC 2, PCI DSS)
Coordinate evidence gathering from control owners ahead of audit windows
Conduct internal pre-audit readiness assessments and gap remediation
Facilitate external auditor and regulator access to systems, personnel, and documentation
Track and respond to auditor requests and information notices (RFIs)
Prepare management responses to audit findings and observations
Submit regulatory cybersecurity certifications and attestations on schedule
Monitor remediation of audit-identified deficiencies to closure
Maintain records of audit outcomes, management responses, and evidence packages
Brief executive leadership and board on regulatory examination results

subProcesses.name: Third-Party Cyber Risk Management
steps: Develop third-party cyber risk tiering criteria based on data sensitivity and system access
Conduct cybersecurity due-diligence assessments on prospective vendors (questionnaires, SOC 2 reports)
Review vendor assessment responses and score against minimum security standards
Negotiate contract clauses covering data protection, breach notification, and audit rights
Onboard approved vendors with access provisioned per least-privilege requirements
Schedule and execute periodic reassessments of in-scope vendors based on risk tier
Monitor vendor security incidents and communicate findings to procurement and legal
Track vendor remediation of identified deficiencies within agreed timeframes
Offboard vendors, revoke access, and confirm data deletion upon contract termination
Report third-party cyber risk exposure to CISO and enterprise vendor risk committee

subProcesses.name: Security Metrics, Reporting & Dashboard Management
steps: Define key risk indicators (KRIs) and key performance indicators (KPIs) for cybersecurity program
Collect metrics data from SIEM, vulnerability scanners, IAM tools, and ticketing systems
Validate metric data quality and reconcile discrepancies across source systems
Produce monthly security scorecard for CISO and technology leadership
Prepare board-level cybersecurity dashboard covering risk posture and incident trends
Benchmark metrics against industry peer data (FS-ISAC, insurance-sector surveys)
Identify metric trends requiring management attention and draft commentary
Distribute dashboards to stakeholders and archive versions for audit trail
Review metric definitions annually and adjust for program maturity changes
Incorporate metric outputs into annual cybersecurity strategic planning

subProcesses.name: Security Awareness & Training Program
steps: Assess employee security awareness baseline through phishing simulations and surveys
Design annual training curriculum covering phishing, social engineering, data handling, and insider threat
Develop role-based training modules for privileged users, developers, and claims handlers
Deploy training through LMS and track completion rates by department
Execute quarterly phishing simulation campaigns and record click/report rates
Provide just-in-time coaching to employees who fail phishing simulations
Conduct specialized tabletop exercises for incident responders and IT staff
Report training completion and simulation outcomes to HR and compliance
Update training content for emerging threats and regulatory changes
Evaluate program effectiveness annually and adjust based on incident root-cause trends

subProcesses.name: Identity Lifecycle Management
steps: Receive joiner/mover/leaver notifications from HR systems (Workday integration)
Create or update identity records in the identity provider (IdP/AD) from authoritative HR data
Assign role-based access entitlements per job function and department on day one
Provision accounts across target systems (core policy admin, claims, finance, email, VPN)
Deliver credentials to new joiners through secure, automated onboarding workflow
Process role-change requests when employees transfer departments or change job titles
Disable accounts immediately upon termination trigger from HR and revoke all active sessions
Transfer or archive data owned by departing employees per retention policy
Remove residual access entitlements within 24 hours of account disablement
Reconcile identity records quarterly against HR source-of-truth to detect orphaned accounts

subProcesses.name: Access Request & Approval Workflow
steps: Receive access request via self-service portal with business justification and requester identity
Route request to application owner and manager for dual approval
Validate request against role catalog and segregation-of-duties (SoD) conflict rules
Flag SoD conflicts to the access risk team for compensating control review
Obtain compliance sign-off for sensitive-system access (claims payment, premium disbursement)
Provision approved access in target system within SLA window
Notify requester and manager upon successful provisioning
Log the full approval chain and provisioning action in the access management audit trail
Reject requests that fail policy checks with a clear denial reason and appeal path
Track open requests, SLA compliance, and approval-bottleneck metrics

subProcesses.name: Access Certification & Periodic Reviews
steps: Schedule quarterly and annual access certification campaigns by application risk tier
Extract entitlement snapshots from all in-scope systems into the IGA platform
Assign review tasks to application owners and business-line managers
Send reminders and escalate overdue reviews through automated campaign management
Reviewers certify, modify, or revoke individual entitlements within the campaign window
Automatically remediate revoked entitlements within 48 hours of campaign close
Produce certification completion report with revocation counts and SoD findings
Escalate uncertified access to the CISO for forced revocation decision
Archive certification evidence packages for regulatory and audit use
Analyze certification trends to identify chronically over-privileged roles for role cleanup

subProcesses.name: Single Sign-On & Federation Management
steps: Onboard new applications to the enterprise SSO platform (Okta / Azure AD) using SAML or OIDC
Configure attribute mappings and claims for each application integration
Test SSO flows end-to-end across browser and mobile clients before production cutover
Define and enforce adaptive MFA policies based on user risk score and application sensitivity
Manage identity federation trusts with insurance partners, brokers, and reinsurers
Monitor SSO authentication success/failure rates and alert on anomalous login patterns
Maintain session timeout and reauthentication policies per data-classification tier
Process application decommissions by removing SSO integrations and orphaned service accounts
Patch and upgrade SSO platform components per vendor release schedule
Review federation trust agreements annually with partner security teams

subProcesses.name: Directory Services & Identity Store Management
steps: Operate and maintain Active Directory / LDAP directory infrastructure with high availability
Enforce domain security baseline policies (password complexity, lockout, Kerberos settings)
Manage organizational unit (OU) structure and group policy objects (GPOs) for business units
Process group membership changes within defined change management windows
Monitor directory replication health and alert on synchronization failures
Audit directory for stale, disabled, and orphaned accounts monthly
Harden directory service configurations per CIS benchmark recommendations
Back up directory state and test restoration procedures quarterly
Coordinate directory schema changes with application teams through change advisory board
Produce directory health and security posture report for infrastructure review

subProcesses.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Administration
steps: Define MFA enrollment policy and enforce enrollment for all workforce identities
Onboard employees to authenticator app, hardware token, or FIDO2 key per role requirements
Process MFA reset and recovery requests through identity-verified helpdesk workflow
Monitor MFA bypass and exception requests; log and time-limit all exceptions
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for privileged and remote access
Alert on anomalous MFA push-notification patterns suggesting MFA fatigue attacks
Report MFA enrollment rates and exception counts to CISO monthly
Manage lifecycle of hardware tokens (issuance, replacement, decommission)
Test MFA failover and recovery procedures in tabletop and technical exercises
