Update MFA policies in response to threat intelligence and regulatory guidance

subProcesses.name: Service Account & Non-Human Identity Management
steps: Maintain an authoritative inventory of all service accounts, API keys, and certificates
Enforce naming conventions and ownership registration for all non-human identities
Apply least-privilege permissions to service accounts scoped to required resources only
Rotate service account credentials and API keys on a defined schedule or on demand
Detect and alert on service accounts with interactive logon rights or excessive privileges
Integrate service account credentials with secrets management vault (HashiCorp Vault / CyberArk)
Review service account usage quarterly and decommission orphaned identities
Enforce certificate lifecycle management with automated renewal before expiry
Monitor for expired or near-expiry certificates across all environments
Audit non-human identity activity logs monthly for anomalous behavior

subProcesses.name: Privileged Account Discovery & Onboarding
steps: Scan enterprise environments to discover all privileged accounts (local admin, domain admin, service accounts)
Classify discovered accounts by privilege tier (Tier 0 domain controllers, Tier 1 servers, Tier 2 workstations)
Obtain business owner attestation for each privileged account prior to vault onboarding
Onboard privileged accounts to CyberArk / BeyondTrust vault with defined platform policies
Rotate initial credentials upon vault onboarding and remove standing access from administrators
Configure automatic credential rotation schedules per account type and risk level
Validate vault connectivity and credential verification for each onboarded account
Document onboarding evidence and account inventory in PAM asset register
Notify account owners of vault onboarding completion and access procedures
Schedule post-onboarding review to confirm operability and policy compliance

subProcesses.name: Privileged Session Brokering & Monitoring
steps: Authenticate administrators to the PAM portal using MFA before privileged session launch
Broker just-in-time (JIT) access requests with time-limited session windows
Record privileged sessions (keystrokes and screen capture) for audit and forensic use
Stream session metadata to SIEM for real-time behavioral alerting
Detect and alert on suspicious privileged session activity (off-hours access, bulk data queries)
Terminate sessions that trigger high-severity behavioral alerts automatically
Require checkout approval from a second administrator for highest-risk (Tier 0) targets
Enforce session time limits and require re-authentication for extended sessions
Provide on-demand session replay to security analysts during incident investigations
Audit session recording completeness and alert on recording gaps monthly

subProcesses.name: Credential Rotation & Secrets Lifecycle
steps: Define credential rotation policies by account type (passwords, SSH keys, API tokens, certificates)
Execute automated password rotation on schedule via PAM vault platform
Verify application connectivity after each rotation and roll back if verification fails
Rotate credentials immediately upon departure of privileged account owner
Manage emergency break-glass credential retrieval with dual-control and automatic post-use rotation
Track rotation compliance rate against policy targets and alert on overdue rotations
Integrate secrets delivery with CI/CD pipelines to prevent credential hard-coding
Audit secret access logs for unauthorized retrieval attempts
Report rotation compliance and outstanding exceptions to the PAM governance board
Review and update rotation policies annually based on threat intelligence and audit findings

subProcesses.name: Least Privilege Enforcement & Entitlement Review
steps: Define least-privilege baselines for each privileged role and system type
Conduct quarterly privileged entitlement reviews with system and application owners
Identify and remediate standing privileged access in favor of JIT provisioning
Remove administrative rights from standard workstations and enforce endpoint privilege management
Audit privileged group memberships (Domain Admins, Schema Admins) monthly
Flag and investigate accounts with privilege creep identified during entitlement reviews
Apply segregation-of-duties controls to prevent single individuals from holding conflicting privileges
Report privileged account count and over-privilege findings to CISO
Track reduction in standing privilege accounts as a program maturity KPI
Update least-privilege baselines when new systems or roles are introduced

subProcesses.name: Privileged Activity Auditing
steps: Collect privileged account activity logs from all target systems into centralized log store
Correlate privileged session records with change tickets to identify unauthorized changes
Generate weekly privileged activity summary reports for system owners
Flag privileged actions executed outside of approved change windows for investigation
Detect use of shared or generic privileged accounts and enforce named-account policy
Produce quarterly privileged access audit report for internal audit and regulators
Respond to audit evidence requests for privileged session recordings within SLA
Alert on dormant privileged accounts with recent activity suggesting compromise
Retain privileged activity logs for minimum retention period per regulatory requirements
Review audit trail completeness and close gaps in log collection coverage

subProcesses.name: PAM Platform Operations & Engineering
steps: Operate PAM vault infrastructure with high availability and disaster recovery capability
Apply PAM platform patches and upgrades through change management process
Maintain PAM connector library for target system integrations (Windows, Linux, database, cloud)
Test PAM platform failover and vault recovery procedures quarterly
Configure and tune PAM platform alerting rules in coordination with SOC
Onboard new target system types by developing and testing platform connectors
Monitor PAM platform performance metrics and capacity utilization
Manage PAM platform license compliance and renewal with vendor
Document PAM architecture, runbooks, and incident response procedures
Conduct annual PAM platform security assessment and penetration test

subProcesses.name: Vulnerability Scanning & Discovery
steps: Maintain authenticated scan credential inventory for all asset classes (Windows, Linux, network, cloud)
Schedule credentialed vulnerability scans across all in-scope assets on defined frequency (weekly critical, monthly standard)
Execute scans during approved maintenance windows to minimize production impact
Monitor scan completion rates and investigate assets that fail to scan
Ingest scan results into vulnerability management platform and deduplicate findings
Enrich vulnerability findings with CVSS scores, exploit availability, and asset criticality
Identify net-new vulnerabilities introduced since the prior scan cycle
Produce asset coverage report confirming scan completeness against asset inventory
Flag unmanaged or rogue assets detected during scanning to IT asset management team
Archive scan results for trend analysis and audit evidence retention

subProcesses.name: Vulnerability Prioritization & Risk Scoring
steps: Apply risk-based prioritization model combining CVSS base score, exploit maturity (EPSS), and asset criticality
Classify vulnerabilities into remediation priority tiers (Critical P1 ≤7 days, High P2 ≤30 days, Medium P3 ≤90 days)
Cross-reference vulnerabilities against CISA KEV catalog for expedited critical remediations
Assess exploitability in insurance-specific context (internet-exposed vs. internal-only assets)
Identify vulnerability clusters affecting high-value assets (claims systems, policy admin platforms)
Assign remediation ownership to asset owners, IT operations, and application teams
Communicate prioritized vulnerability lists to system owners with remediation deadlines
Review and approve risk-acceptance requests for vulnerabilities that cannot be patched within SLA
Track risk-accepted vulnerabilities with compensating controls and expiry dates
Report vulnerability risk exposure trends to CISO and security steering committee

subProcesses.name: Patch Remediation Coordination & Tracking
steps: Receive and triage vendor patch releases for applicability to the ABC Insurance environment
Test patches in non-production environment for compatibility with insurance applications (Duck Creek, Guidewire)
Coordinate patch scheduling with Technology through the change advisory board (CAB) process
Track patch deployment execution by Technology teams against SLA targets by priority tier
Validate patch installation success and verify vulnerability remediation through follow-up scan
Escalate failed or overdue patches to application owners and Technology leadership for remediation planning
Process emergency patch coordination for actively exploited vulnerabilities outside normal CAB windows
Monitor patch compliance rate across asset classes and identify systemic deployment barriers
Report patch compliance rates and outstanding patch debt to CISO and IT leadership
Archive patch remediation records for audit and regulatory evidence

subProcesses.name: Security Configuration & Hardening Management
steps: Define CIS Benchmark-aligned hardening baselines for all operating system and platform types
Assess current configuration compliance against hardening baselines using automated scanning
Prioritize configuration deviations by severity and remediation feasibility
Deploy hardening configurations through automated configuration management (Ansible, DSC, Chef)
Verify configuration baseline compliance after deployment and remediate failures
Track configuration drift on a continuous basis and alert on unauthorized changes
Review and update hardening baselines for new platform versions and CIS Benchmark releases
Manage exceptions to hardening standards with documented business justification and compensating controls
Report configuration compliance posture by asset class to CISO monthly
Include configuration compliance in vendor and third-party assessment criteria

subProcesses.name: Penetration Testing & Red Team Exercises
steps: Define annual penetration testing scope covering external perimeter, internal network, and web applications
Select and engage qualified penetration testing vendor through procurement and security vetting process
Conduct pre-engagement scoping meeting to confirm rules of engagement, targets, and out-of-scope systems
Execute external perimeter penetration test and document discovered exploit paths
Execute internal network and application penetration tests with access representative of an insider or compromised endpoint
Deliver penetration test report detailing findings, CVSS scores, and proof-of-concept evidence
Triage penetration test findings into vulnerability management platform for remediation tracking
Validate remediation of critical and high findings through follow-up retest
Conduct red team adversary simulation exercise annually to test detection and response capability
Present penetration test and red team results to CISO and Board Audit Committee

subProcesses.name: Vulnerability Program Reporting & Metrics
steps: Collect vulnerability age, count, and remediation-rate metrics from vulnerability management platform
Calculate mean-time-to-remediate (MTTR) by priority tier and asset class
Produce monthly vulnerability management dashboard for CISO and security leadership
Report critical and high open vulnerability counts as a key risk indicator to board risk committee
Benchmark vulnerability posture against insurance sector peers using available industry data
Identify systemic remediation barriers (e.g., application compatibility, resource constraints) requiring escalation
Track vulnerability recurrence rate to identify root-cause patterns requiring process improvement
Prepare vulnerability management program status for annual regulatory examinations
Contribute vulnerability metrics to enterprise cyber risk register updates
Review reporting frequency and metric definitions annually with security governance

subProcesses.name: Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC)
steps: Integrate security requirements gathering into project initiation and business-analysis phases
Conduct threat modeling workshops with development teams for new and materially changed applications
Define security acceptance criteria as part of user story definition and sprint planning
Perform static application security testing (SAST) in CI pipeline with policy-enforced pass/fail gates
Conduct software composition analysis (SCA) to identify vulnerable open-source dependencies
Execute dynamic application security testing (DAST) against staging environment before release
Perform security code review for high-risk features (authentication, payment, data export)
Track and remediate security findings in development backlog with SLA aligned to severity
Conduct pre-production security sign-off review before major releases to insurance applications
Measure and report on SSDLC adoption rate, vulnerability-introduction rate, and remediation time

subProcesses.name: Web Application Firewall Management
steps: Inventory all external-facing web applications requiring WAF protection coverage
Deploy WAF in detection mode and baseline normal traffic patterns before enabling blocking
Configure OWASP Top 10 rule sets tuned for insurance application traffic patterns
Enable bot management rules to protect producer portals and customer-facing quote engines
Tune WAF rules to reduce false positives against legitimate insurance application workflows
Monitor WAF alert dashboards and escalate confirmed attack traffic to SOC
Test WAF effectiveness through simulated injection and XSS attacks quarterly
Review and update WAF rules for newly discovered vulnerabilities and attack patterns
Manage WAF platform patching and configuration through change management
Report WAF block rates, false-positive rates, and attack trends to security leadership monthly

subProcesses.name: API Security Management
steps: Inventory all internal and external APIs, documenting endpoints, authentication methods, and data classifications
Enforce API authentication standards (OAuth 2.0, mutual TLS) across all consumer-facing and partner APIs
Apply rate limiting and throttling policies to prevent abuse of insurance APIs (quote, claims status, policy lookup)
Conduct API security testing covering OWASP API Top 10 vulnerabilities before production deployment
Deploy API gateway controls to centralize authentication, authorization, and threat detection
Monitor API traffic for anomalous call patterns indicating enumeration, scraping, or credential stuffing
Scan OpenAPI specifications for exposed sensitive fields, excessive data return, and broken object references
Coordinate with development teams to remediate API vulnerabilities within severity-based SLAs
Review API inventory quarterly and decommission deprecated or unused API endpoints
Report API security posture and outstanding findings to application security leadership monthly

subProcesses.name: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)
steps: Connect cloud accounts (AWS, Azure, GCP) to CSPM platform with read-only audit permissions
Run continuous posture assessments against CIS Cloud Benchmarks and NIST CSF controls
Prioritize misconfiguration findings by exploitability and data sensitivity of affected resources
Assign cloud misconfiguration findings to cloud platform and DevOps teams with remediation SLAs
Enforce guardrails through infrastructure-as-code policy checks (OPA, AWS Config, Azure Policy)
Monitor for publicly exposed storage buckets, databases, and API endpoints
Track cloud resource inventory changes and alert on unauthorized or untagged resource creation
Produce weekly cloud security posture dashboard for cloud governance committee
Conduct cloud security architecture reviews for new workloads before production deployment
Report cloud compliance posture to CISO and include in quarterly board risk report

subProcesses.name: Container & DevSecOps Security
steps: Scan container images for vulnerabilities in CI pipeline before push to registry
Enforce image signing and verify signatures before deployment to production Kubernetes clusters
Define and enforce pod security standards (restricted profile) across Kubernetes namespaces
Monitor container runtime behavior for anomalous process execution or file system changes
Scan infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, CloudFormation) for security misconfigurations before apply
Implement secrets management integration to eliminate hardcoded credentials in container manifests
Conduct Kubernetes cluster hardening assessment against CIS Kubernetes Benchmark
Enforce network policies limiting pod-to-pod communication to required service paths only
Produce monthly DevSecOps security metrics covering pipeline scan coverage and vulnerability trends
Train development teams on secure container development practices and security-as-code patterns

subProcesses.name: Data Security & Encryption Management
steps: Classify insurance data assets by sensitivity (PII, PHI, financial, proprietary) and regulatory category
Enforce encryption-at-rest for all classified data stores (databases, file shares, cloud storage)
Enforce encryption-in-transit (TLS 1.2+) for all data flows carrying sensitive information
Manage enterprise key management infrastructure with hardware security modules (HSMs)
Rotate encryption keys on defined schedules and upon suspicion of key compromise
Deploy data loss prevention (DLP) controls on endpoints and email to detect sensitive data exfiltration
Monitor DLP alerts and escalate confirmed policy violations to security and compliance teams
Audit database access controls and activity monitoring on systems holding policyholder data
Conduct data security assessments for cloud migrations involving sensitive insurance data
Report data security control effectiveness to CISO and privacy officer quarterly

subProcesses.name: Endpoint Security Management
steps: Maintain enterprise endpoint security platform (EDR) covering all managed workstations, laptops, and servers
Ensure EDR agent deployment coverage meets policy targets and investigate gaps
Configure EDR detection policies tuned for insurance-sector threat actor behaviors
Respond to EDR alerts and isolate endpoints exhibiting confirmed malicious behavior
Enforce application allowlisting or controlled folder access on high-value endpoints
Manage endpoint encryption (BitLocker, FileVault) and verify encryption compliance across fleet
Coordinate endpoint hardening with IT operations to enforce CIS benchmark settings
Deploy mobile device management (MDM) policies for corporate and BYOD mobile devices
Monitor EDR telemetry for indicators of insider threat or data exfiltration on endpoints
Report endpoint security coverage, alert volume, and compliance posture to CISO monthly

subProcesses.name: Application Security Assessment Program
steps: Maintain annual security assessment schedule covering applications, cloud, and infrastructure
Conduct application security assessments for high-risk insurance applications (claims, underwriting, payment)
Execute API security testing covering authentication, authorization, and injection vulnerabilities
Perform cloud security architecture reviews for new or modified cloud workloads
Coordinate annual third-party application penetration tests for customer-facing portals
Track assessment findings in vulnerability management platform with ownership and remediation plans
Validate remediation of critical and high findings through rescanning and manual verification
Produce application security assessment report for CISO and technology leadership
Maintain assessment methodology documentation updated for new attack techniques
Report security testing coverage and finding trends to security governance committee

subProcesses.name: Security Monitoring & Event Collection
steps: Maintain SIEM data source inventory covering endpoints, network, cloud, and application logs
Onboard new log sources through log ingestion pipeline with parsing and normalization
Validate log source coverage against asset inventory and identify collection gaps
Monitor log ingestion volumes and alert on source failures or unexpected drops
Tune log retention policies per regulatory requirements (NYDFS 6-year log retention)
Enrich events with threat intelligence feeds and asset context at ingest time
Monitor security event volumes and detect anomalous spikes requiring analyst attention
Maintain SIEM platform health (indexing, storage, query performance) with infrastructure team
Produce monthly data source coverage report for SOC manager review
Test log source failover and backup ingestion paths quarterly

subProcesses.name: Detection Engineering & Use Case Management
steps: Maintain detection use-case library mapped to MITRE ATT&CK tactics and insurance threat scenarios
Develop new detection rules based on threat intelligence, incident post-mortems, and red team findings
Test detection rules in staging environment against representative log samples before production deployment
Deploy rules through change management process with rollback capability
Monitor new rules for false-positive rate during a 30-day tuning period
Tune detection thresholds and exclusions to reduce analyst alert fatigue
Retire outdated detection rules that no longer reflect current threat landscape
Track detection coverage gaps against MITRE ATT&CK matrix quarterly
Report detection library health, alert volume, and mean-time-to-detect to SOC leadership
Collaborate with threat intelligence team to translate new TTPs into actionable detections

subProcesses.name: Alert Triage
steps: Receive and acknowledge new security alerts from SIEM within defined SLA by tier
Perform initial triage to assess alert severity, affected assets, and potential business impact
Enrich alert with contextual data (user identity, asset criticality, threat intel hits)
Determine if alert constitutes a true positive, false positive, or requires escalation
Correlate related alerts across time window to identify coordinated attack patterns
Close false-positive alerts with tuning recommendation fed back to detection engineering
Communicate preliminary threat findings to affected business units and asset owners
Escalate confirmed threats to Tier 2 / Tier 3 analysts using documented escalation criteria
Document initial triage findings, evidence gathered, and disposition in case management system
Report alert volume, escalation rate, and mean-time-to-triage metrics weekly

subProcesses.name: Threat Investigation & Analysis
steps: Receive escalated cases from Tier 1 triage with initial alert context and enrichment
Define investigation scope based on affected systems, user identities, and threat indicators
Conduct deep log analysis across SIEM, EDR, and network telemetry to reconstruct attack sequence
Apply MITRE ATT&CK framework mapping to characterize threat actor tactics and techniques
Query threat intelligence platform to identify known threat actor attribution or campaign linkages
Assess lateral movement potential and determine additional assets requiring investigation
Produce investigation report documenting evidence, attack timeline, and analyst conclusions
Recommend containment or remediation actions to SOC manager and asset owners
Hand off confirmed incidents to the Incident Response team with full evidence package
Contribute investigation findings to detection engineering for improved rule development

subProcesses.name: Security Orchestration & Automated Response (SOAR)
steps: Identify high-volume, repetitive analyst tasks suitable for SOAR automation
Design and implement SOAR playbooks for phishing triage, malware containment, and account lockout
Test playbooks in sandbox environment against simulated alert scenarios
Deploy approved playbooks with manual override capability for analyst intervention
Monitor playbook execution success rates and automated action accuracy
Review and update playbooks quarterly based on threat landscape and workflow changes
Integrate SOAR with ticketing, EDR, firewall, and IAM platforms for automated response actions
Measure analyst time savings and false-positive reduction attributable to automation
Maintain playbook documentation and train analysts on override and manual escalation procedures
Report SOAR automation coverage and ROI to SOC leadership

subProcesses.name: Threat Intelligence Operations
steps: Subscribe to and ingest threat intelligence feeds relevant to insurance sector (FS-ISAC, CISA, commercial feeds)
Process and normalize threat indicators (IPs, domains, hashes, TTPs) into SIEM and TIP
Correlate threat intelligence with internal telemetry to identify active threats or compromised assets
Produce weekly threat intelligence digest for SOC analysts and security leadership
Participate in FS-ISAC intelligence sharing and submit indicators observed in ABC Insurance environment
Track threat actor campaigns targeting financial services and insurance sector
Provide threat context to incident responders during active investigations
Evaluate new intelligence sources and onboard high-quality feeds through procurement process
Retire low-value feeds and manage threat intelligence platform license costs
Brief CISO and board on significant emerging threats quarterly

subProcesses.name: SOC Performance & Continuous Improvement
steps: Define SOC SLA targets for alert acknowledge, triage, and escalation by severity tier
Collect operational metrics from SIEM, case management, and SOAR platforms
Produce weekly SOC operations report covering alert volume, SLA compliance, and escalation trends
Conduct monthly retrospective to identify analyst workflow bottlenecks and improvement opportunities
Manage SOC analyst shift scheduling to ensure 24x7 coverage with appropriate skill mix
Track analyst training completion and certifications (SANS, CompTIA, vendor certs)
Run purple team exercises with red team to validate SOC detection and response capability
Benchmark SOC performance against industry peers using FS-ISAC and SANS survey data
Report SOC capability maturity to CISO and present improvement roadmap
Review and update SOC playbook library annually or after significant incidents

subProcesses.name: Security Event Escalation to Incident Response
steps: Apply incident classification criteria to determine when triage escalates to declared incident
Notify incident response lead and SOC manager upon incident declaration
Transfer investigation context and evidence package to incident response team
Maintain SOC involvement in monitoring and detection support throughout incident lifecycle
Isolate or contain affected assets at SOC direction pending IR team takeover
Preserve original alert data and initial investigation notes for forensic chain-of-custody
Coordinate with IT operations for emergency change actions during containment
Provide continuous monitoring for re-infection or lateral movement during recovery
Contribute SOC-sourced findings to the post-incident review
Implement detection improvements identified during the incident post-mortem

subProcesses.name: Incident Preparedness & Planning
steps: Maintain and annually review the Cyber Incident Response Plan (CIRP) aligned to NIST SP 800-61
Define incident severity classification matrix mapping technical indicators to business impact levels
Establish and maintain incident response team (IRT) roster with primary and backup contacts
Develop playbooks for priority incident types (ransomware, data breach, insider threat, DDoS)
Integrate CIRP with business continuity and crisis communication plans
Maintain retainer agreements with external incident response and digital forensics firms
Conduct annual IR tabletop exercise with executive leadership and business-unit representatives
Execute technical simulation exercises (fire drill, purple team) to test IR procedures
Train IR team members on updated playbooks after each major incident or tabletop
Review and update incident notification contact lists and escalation trees quarterly

subProcesses.name: Incident Detection & Declaration
steps: Receive potential incident notifications from SOC, helpdesk, employees, and external parties
Apply incident classification criteria to determine severity (P1 Critical through P4 Low)
Declare incident formally and activate appropriate IR playbook
Notify IR team lead, CISO, and executive sponsor within time thresholds defined by severity
Open incident case in IR management platform and assign primary IR analyst
Establish incident command bridge (war room) for P1/P2 incidents
Communicate initial situation report to stakeholders within 1 hour of P1 declaration
Determine need for external IR retainer activation and initiate if warranted
Document incident timeline from initial detection signal to formal declaration
Notify legal and compliance team for all incidents involving potential data exposure

subProcesses.name: Incident Investigation & Scope Determination
steps: Assign investigation lead and define initial scope based on affected systems and indicators
Preserve forensic evidence by imaging affected systems and collecting volatile memory where warranted
Analyze attacker TTPs against MITRE ATT&CK framework to reconstruct intrusion timeline
Identify patient zero and initial attack vector through log analysis and endpoint forensics
Determine lateral movement scope by analyzing authentication logs and network flows
Assess data exposure scope: identify what data was accessed, exfiltrated, or encrypted
Continuously expand or narrow investigation scope as new evidence surfaces
Maintain chain-of-custody documentation for all forensic evidence collected
Provide regular situation reports to incident commander and executive stakeholders
Coordinate parallel forensic workstreams for large-scale incidents requiring multiple analysts

subProcesses.name: Containment & Eradication
steps: Implement short-term containment actions (network isolation, account lockout) to limit threat spread
Validate containment effectiveness through monitoring and confirm no further lateral movement
Develop and execute eradication plan to remove threat actor tools, malware, and persistence mechanisms
Rebuild or reimage compromised systems from known-good gold images
Reset credentials for all accounts touched by the threat actor
Patch or mitigate the initial access vulnerability exploited during the attack
Verify eradication completeness through endpoint detection tool scanning and behavioral analysis
Coordinate containment actions with IT operations to minimize business disruption
Communicate containment status to affected business units and executive stakeholders
Document all containment and eradication actions with timestamps for post-incident record

subProcesses.name: Regulatory Notification & Legal Coordination
steps: Assess incident against breach notification triggers: NYDFS §500.17, state data breach laws, HIPAA
Engage legal counsel and privacy officer to evaluate notification obligations within 72 hours of discovery
Determine affected individual count and data element categories for notification scoping
Prepare regulatory notification draft for DFS, HHS, or applicable state attorneys general
Submit regulatory notifications within statutory deadlines (72 hours NYDFS for material incidents)
Draft and send consumer notification letters through approved mailing vendor
Coordinate with PR and communications on public disclosure statements where required
Engage cyber insurance carrier and submit claim notification within policy-required timeframe
Preserve all incident-related records as potential litigation hold material
Track regulatory notification deadlines and submission receipts in legal matter management system

subProcesses.name: Recovery & Service Restoration
steps: Develop recovery plan prioritizing restoration of business-critical systems per BCP tiers
Restore systems from clean backups following validated eradication of threat
Conduct parallel monitoring during restoration to detect re-infection or threat actor return
Perform smoke testing of restored applications with business owners before production cutover
Coordinate with IT operations to execute phased restoration to minimize service disruption
Validate data integrity of restored systems through checksums and application-level testing
Declare recovery complete and stand down incident command bridge upon stakeholder confirmation
Communicate all-clear to affected business units and executive leadership
Document recovery timeline and total downtime for business impact assessment
Initiate transition from incident response mode to post-incident review within 5 business days

subProcesses.name: Post-Incident Review & Lessons Learned
steps: Convene post-incident review (PIR) within 2 weeks of incident closure with all key responders
Reconstruct complete incident timeline from detection through recovery
Identify root causes of both the incident and any response shortcomings
Determine which detection or prevention controls failed and why
Document lessons learned and generate concrete improvement action items with owners and due dates
Update affected playbooks, runbooks, and detection rules based on PIR findings
Brief CISO and executive leadership on PIR findings and remediation roadmap
Track PIR action items to closure through security program management process
Submit PIR findings to regulatory examiners if requested as part of post-incident reporting
Incorporate persistent root-cause patterns into annual cyber risk assessment updates

subProcesses.name: IT Service Continuity Planning
steps: Identify and inventory all IT services and systems supporting critical insurance operations (claims, policy admin, billing)
Determine recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) for each IT service in collaboration with business owners
Document IT service continuity plans covering failover procedures for each tier of system criticality
Assign IT service continuity ownership to infrastructure and application teams with defined accountabilities
Integrate cyber incident scenarios into IT service continuity plans alongside infrastructure failure scenarios
Identify manual workaround procedures for critical business functions (claims intake, policy issuance) during IT outages
Review and update IT service continuity plans annually and following material system or architecture changes
Distribute approved IT service continuity plans to plan owners and store in offline-accessible repository
Report IT service continuity coverage gaps to CISO and CTO for remediation planning
Align IT service continuity plans with regulatory requirements for insurance carrier technology resilience (NAIC guidance)

subProcesses.name: Disaster Recovery Infrastructure & Runbook Management
steps: Maintain DR runbooks covering failover procedures for core insurance platforms (policy admin, claims, billing)
Configure and verify data replication to DR site or cloud secondary region at defined RPO intervals
Maintain DR environment in a state ready for activation within defined RTO
Test DR runbook accuracy through quarterly tabletop walkthroughs with IT operations teams
Update DR runbooks after system changes, infrastructure upgrades, or incident learnings
Manage DR infrastructure capacity and confirm resource availability to support full production failover
Coordinate DR environment access and change management with infrastructure and cloud platform teams
Validate network routing, DNS failover, and load balancer configurations in DR environment quarterly
Document DR architecture diagrams and dependency maps for all Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems
Report DR readiness posture to CISO, CTO, and board risk committee

subProcesses.name: DR Testing & Validation
steps: Define annual DR test schedule covering full failover tests for Tier 1 systems and recovery tests for Tier 2 systems
Prepare test plans specifying success criteria, rollback procedures, and business-impact safeguards
Execute annual full DR failover test for Tier 1 systems and document results against success criteria
Validate recovery from backup for Tier 2 systems annually and record restoration times
Conduct parallel monitoring during DR tests to confirm no impact to production services
Document all DR test outcomes including achieved RTO/RPO versus targets
Identify and log gaps discovered during DR testing and assign remediation owners with target dates
Validate remediation of prior test gaps before the next scheduled test cycle
Archive DR test evidence packages for regulatory examination and audit purposes
Report DR test results and outstanding gaps to CISO and technology leadership

subProcesses.name: Backup & Data Recovery Operations
steps: Define backup policy covering frequency, retention, and encryption requirements by data classification
Operate enterprise backup platform covering on-premises servers, cloud workloads, and SaaS applications
Monitor backup job completion daily and investigate and remediate failed backup jobs within 24 hours
Test data restoration from backup for critical systems monthly and document test outcomes
Maintain offsite and immutable backup copies per 3-2-1 backup strategy requirements
Validate backup encryption key availability and integrity before relying on encrypted backups for recovery
Report backup coverage gaps and restore-test failure rates to CISO and infrastructure team
Audit backup retention compliance against regulatory data retention requirements
Manage backup platform capacity and forecast storage growth for budgeting
Update backup policy and platform configuration when new systems or data stores are introduced

subProcesses.name: Cyber Resilience & Ransomware Preparedness
steps: Assess cyber resilience posture covering backup integrity, network segmentation, and recovery capability
Implement immutable backup copies for all Tier 1 systems using air-gapped or vault-based storage
Test ransomware recovery procedures including clean restoration from immutable backups
Define and document ransomware response playbook covering detection, isolation, and recovery decision tree
Conduct executive tabletop exercise simulating ransomware attack on claims processing environment
Assess cyber insurance policy coverage against ransomware response and business interruption scenarios
Implement network segmentation controls to limit ransomware lateral movement between business segments
Validate offline recovery capability for critical systems that must operate without network connectivity
Review and update ransomware preparedness posture based on FS-ISAC threat intelligence
Report cyber resilience readiness assessment findings to CISO and Board Cyber Committee

subProcesses.name: Cyber Continuity Regulatory Reporting
steps: Track regulatory requirements for cybersecurity and IT resilience reporting (NYDFS §500, NAIC, state DOIs)
Prepare annual certification of compliance with NYDFS §500 cybersecurity program requirements
Compile DR and backup test evidence for regulatory examination submissions
Submit IT resilience and cyber continuity reports to state insurance regulators on required schedules
Respond to regulatory information requests related to technology recovery and cyber continuity capability
Coordinate with risk and actuarial teams on operational risk capital reporting requiring IT resilience data
Brief board risk committee on cyber continuity regulatory obligations and program compliance status
Maintain records of all regulatory submissions with version control and submission receipts
Assess impact of new regulatory guidance on cybersecurity and IT resilience program requirements
Update compliance calendar for regulatory deadlines affecting cybersecurity and IT continuity reporting

subProcesses.name: Data Standards & Policy Management
steps: Define enterprise data standards, naming conventions, and policy framework
Socialize draft standards with data owners, stewards, and business stakeholders
Conduct gap analysis between current practices and target data standards
Approve and publish data standards in the enterprise policy repository
Communicate standards changes to data producers and consumers
Establish data classification tiers (PII, PHI, confidential, public) and handling rules
Review and update data standards on a defined annual cadence
Track policy compliance against standards across business domains
Escalate persistent non-compliance to data governance council for resolution

subProcesses.name: Data Ownership & Stewardship
steps: Assign data domain ownership to accountable business executives
Appoint data stewards for each domain and document stewardship responsibilities
Onboard new stewards with training on governance tools and obligations
Maintain a current register of data owners, stewards, and deputy stewards
Facilitate regular stewardship council meetings to resolve cross-domain issues
Arbitrate data ownership disputes between competing domain teams
Review stewardship assignments after org changes or personnel transitions
Measure steward engagement and compliance metrics quarterly
Report stewardship health to the Chief Data Officer and governance council

subProcesses.name: Data Catalog & Lineage Management
steps: Ingest new data asset metadata into the enterprise catalog via automated crawlers
Manually curate business definitions, glossary terms, and ownership for each asset
Map end-to-end data lineage from source systems through transformations to consumers
Validate lineage accuracy against pipeline code and ETL documentation
Publish certified data assets and flag uncertified or deprecated datasets
Link catalog entries to regulatory classifications and retention policies
Monitor catalog completeness and coverage metrics by domain
Respond to consumer requests for lineage tracing and impact analysis
Archive lineage records for decommissioned assets per retention schedule

subProcesses.name: Data Quality Profiling & Monitoring
steps: Profile data quality across all critical data elements to establish baseline metrics
Define data quality rules and thresholds for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness
Instrument automated quality checks at ingestion, transformation, and serving layers
Detect quality issues via alerting and anomaly detection dashboards
Log and categorize quality failures by severity, domain, and upstream source
Assign remediation tickets to responsible data stewards or engineering teams
Track remediation progress and escalate unresolved issues per SLA
Remediate data quality issues and validate corrections against quality rules
Report data quality scores and trends to governance council on a monthly basis
Conduct root-cause analysis on recurring quality failures and drive permanent fixes

subProcesses.name: Data Retention & Lifecycle Management
steps: Define retention schedules and legal hold requirements per data classification and regulatory jurisdiction
Configure automated archival jobs to migrate records to lower-cost storage tiers at retention schedule milestones
Enforce secure disposal of records that have exceeded their maximum retention period across all storage tiers
Maintain evidence of disposal actions including timestamps, record counts, and approving authority
Apply legal hold flags to records subject to litigation or regulatory investigation and suspend automated purge
Coordinate with legal and compliance teams to lift holds and resume normal retention processing after resolution
Conduct annual retention schedule review to incorporate regulatory changes and new data asset classes
Audit retention compliance across storage platforms and remediate gaps identified in sampling reviews
Report retention SLA adherence and outstanding disposal backlogs to data governance council

subProcesses.name: Data Privacy Controls
steps: Define privacy control requirements (masking, minimization, tokenization) per data classification and regulatory obligation
Apply masking, minimization, and tokenization to sensitive fields at the point of ingestion into the data platform
Conduct privacy impact assessments for new data products, processing activities, or third-party data sharing
Respond to data subject access requests (DSARs) within regulatory deadlines, coordinating with source system owners
Test privacy controls for effectiveness via periodic audit sampling and synthetic data injection
Identify and remediate control gaps discovered in audits, regulatory reviews, or incident investigations
Maintain consent records and preference management integration for data assets subject to consumer opt-out
Train data engineers and analysts on privacy-by-design principles and handling obligations for sensitive data
Report privacy control effectiveness metrics and open remediation items to the Chief Privacy Officer quarterly

subProcesses.name: Data Access Management
steps: Define access policies and entitlements by data classification and user role
Receive and evaluate data access requests via the service catalog
Validate business justification, need-to-know, and regulatory eligibility
Provision data access in catalog and cloud IAM tooling
Enforce attribute-based and role-based access controls at the platform layer
Conduct quarterly access certification campaigns with data owners
Certify and revoke data access for departing employees and role-change events
Investigate unauthorized access alerts and remediate within defined SLA
Produce access audit reports for compliance review and external examination

subProcesses.name: Data Demand Intake & Prioritization
steps: Receive and triage data demand via intake form from business and IT requestors
Define data requirements and use case in collaboration with requesting team
Assess feasibility, source availability, and compliance implications
Estimate effort and classify request as data product, report, or ad-hoc extract
Score and prioritize data product request against portfolio backlog criteria
Obtain governance approval for high-sensitivity or high-effort demand items
Source and license external data if internal sources are insufficient
Communicate prioritization decision and expected delivery timeline to requestor
Create and assign delivery work items to engineering or analytics squads
Track fulfillment progress and report intake pipeline metrics monthly

subProcesses.name: Master Data Domain Definition
steps: Identify and scope enterprise master data domains (policy, party, product, location, provider)
Document golden record definition, key attributes, and business rules per domain
Align domain definitions with regulatory reporting requirements and external schemas
Publish domain specifications to data catalog and notify consuming applications
Review domain definitions annually or after major product or regulatory changes
Maintain version history of domain definitions for audit traceability
Resolve conflicts between domain definitions raised by stewards or consumers
Retire obsolete domain definitions and migrate consumers to replacement schemas

subProcesses.name: Reference Data Management
steps: Collect reference data change requests from business owners and regulatory bodies
Validate proposed reference values against authoritative external sources (ISO, NAIC, state DOIs)
Approve reference data additions, modifications, or deprecations via governance workflow
Publish approved reference data to the enterprise reference data store
Distribute reference data updates to downstream systems via API or event stream
Version-stamp all reference data releases for traceability and rollback
Monitor downstream adoption of updated reference values and resolve sync failures
Decommission obsolete code lists and update documentation accordingly
Produce reference data quality metrics and report to data governance council

subProcesses.name: Master Data Matching & Survivorship
steps: Ingest entity records from source systems into the MDM hub staging layer
Execute probabilistic and deterministic matching algorithms to identify duplicate candidates
Route low-confidence match clusters to data stewards for manual review
Apply survivorship rules to construct the golden record from best-of-breed attributes
Validate golden record completeness and quality against domain rules
Publish golden records to the MDM hub and notify downstream consumers
Monitor match rate, merge rate, and survivorship accuracy metrics continuously
Reprocess unmatched records after rule refinement or new source onboarding
Audit matching decisions for regulatory and internal review purposes

subProcesses.name: Master Data Distribution & Synchronization
steps: Design and maintain the canonical distribution architecture for each MDM domain
Configure real-time event streams and batch sync jobs for golden record distribution
Monitor distribution pipeline health and SLA adherence for critical consumers
Investigate and remediate synchronization failures within defined resolution windows
Manage consumer subscriptions and onboard new downstream system integrations
Test distribution integrity after schema or survivorship rule changes
Produce distribution audit logs for regulatory review and incident investigation
Decommission legacy point-to-point feeds replaced by MDM hub distribution

subProcesses.name: Data Certification & Trust Scoring
steps: Define trust scoring criteria for data assets (lineage completeness, quality scores, stewardship)
Certify data sets that meet minimum quality, lineage, and governance thresholds
Publish certification badges and trust scores in the enterprise data catalog
Notify data consumers of certification status changes via catalog subscription alerts
Review and recertify datasets on a defined periodic schedule or after significant changes
Revoke certification for datasets that fall below quality or compliance thresholds
Track certification coverage across domains and report to data governance council
Investigate consumer disputes over data trust scores and adjudicate via stewardship process

subProcesses.name: MDM Platform Operations & Governance
steps: Administer MDM platform configuration, user roles, and access controls
Apply platform patches and version upgrades following change management process
Monitor platform performance, storage utilization, and job queue health
Conduct capacity planning and scale infrastructure ahead of demand peaks
Run disaster recovery tests for MDM hub and associated data stores
Maintain MDM platform documentation and runbooks for operations team
Report platform availability, incident counts, and SLA compliance monthly
Coordinate platform roadmap with vendor and align with enterprise architecture standards

subProcesses.name: Data Ingestion & Source Onboarding
steps: Receive ingestion request and assess source system connectivity and data contract
Profile source data for schema, volume, cadence, and quality characteristics
Design ingestion pattern (batch, micro-batch, or streaming) aligned with SLA requirements
Build and configure ingestion connectors, change-data-capture feeds, or API integrations
Implement schema validation and data contract enforcement at the ingestion boundary
Test ingestion pipeline end-to-end in non-production environment with representative data
Validate data completeness and latency against defined acceptance criteria
Approve and publish ingestion pipeline to production via CI/CD deployment process
Monitor initial production runs and tune performance or error handling as needed
Hand off pipeline to operations with runbook and alerting configuration complete

subProcesses.name: Data Transformation & Enrichment
steps: Receive transformation requirements from data product or analytics team
Design transformation logic, including business rules, joins, aggregations, and enrichment sources
Implement transformations in approved orchestration framework (dbt, Spark, or equivalent)
Unit-test transformation logic against expected output using curated test datasets
Run integration tests in staging environment and validate against downstream consumers
Optimize query plans and resource utilization before production promotion
Deploy transformation jobs through CI/CD with automated rollback capability
Monitor job execution metrics (duration, row counts, error rates) post-deployment
Remediate transformation failures and notify downstream consumers of reprocessing
Update data lineage catalog entries to reflect new or modified transformation steps

subProcesses.name: Streaming & Real-Time Data Engineering
steps: Define streaming use case requirements including latency, throughput, and ordering guarantees
Design event schema and publish contract to schema registry for producer/consumer alignment
Build streaming processor (Kafka Streams, Flink, or Spark Structured Streaming) with exactly-once semantics
Implement dead-letter queue handling and poison-message detection
Conduct load testing to validate throughput and latency targets under peak conditions
Deploy streaming application with auto-scaling configuration and health probes
Monitor consumer lag, partition utilization, and end-to-end latency in real time
Tune partition counts, parallelism, and back-pressure settings based on production telemetry
Coordinate schema evolution with producers and consumers via backward-compatible contract changes
Document event topology and maintain schema registry entries for catalog discoverability

subProcesses.name: Pipeline Orchestration & Scheduling
steps: Define pipeline dependencies, scheduling windows, and SLA targets in the orchestration tool
Configure DAGs or workflow definitions for all batch and event-driven pipeline executions
Implement retry logic, circuit breakers, and failure notification handlers
Test orchestration flow end-to-end in staging, including failure and retry scenarios
Deploy orchestration definitions through version-controlled change management process
Monitor pipeline run status, queue depths, and SLA breach alerts in real time
Investigate and resolve late-running or failed pipelines within priority-based SLA windows
Perform on-call triage and escalation for critical pipeline failures affecting business processes
Review and tune scheduling windows quarterly to reduce contention and improve throughput
Maintain orchestration documentation and on-call runbooks for common failure scenarios

subProcesses.name: Data Pipeline Testing & Quality Gates
steps: Define data quality gate specifications for each pipeline stage (ingestion, transform, serving)
Implement automated row count, null rate, and referential integrity checks in pipeline code
Configure quality gate thresholds and alert routing in monitoring tooling
Integrate quality gate results into CI/CD pipeline as mandatory pass criteria
Review quality gate failures and determine whether to halt, quarantine, or alert
Quarantine records failing quality gates for steward review before downstream propagation
Produce pipeline quality scorecards and trend reports for engineering review
Tune quality gate thresholds based on historical data distribution and stakeholder feedback
Escalate systemic quality failures to data stewards and source system owners for root-cause fix

subProcesses.name: Data Pipeline CI/CD & DevOps
steps: Maintain version-controlled repositories for all pipeline code, DAGs, and configuration
Define CI pipeline stages: lint, unit test, integration test, and security scan
Configure automated code review gates and branch protection policies
Build and tag immutable pipeline artifacts and store in artifact registry
Execute automated integration tests against non-production data environment on each merge
Promote pipeline releases to staging and conduct acceptance testing with data consumers
Deploy to production via automated CD pipeline with canary or blue-green strategy
Monitor post-deployment pipeline health and trigger automated rollback on failure criteria
Maintain deployment runbooks and release notes for each production promotion
Track lead time, deployment frequency, and change failure rate as engineering health metrics

subProcesses.name: Data Pipeline Monitoring & Incident Management
steps: Instrument pipelines with structured logging, metrics emission, and distributed tracing
Configure threshold-based and anomaly-detection alerts for pipeline health indicators
Receive and triage pipeline incident alerts via on-call rotation and ticketing system
Investigate root cause using logs, metrics, and lineage tooling
Execute remediation actions (reruns, hotfixes, or source escalation) per runbook
Communicate pipeline incident status and ETA to affected data consumers
Verify pipeline recovery and downstream data correctness after remediation
Conduct post-incident review and document corrective actions within 48 hours
Track MTTR, failure frequency, and SLA compliance metrics on monthly engineering scorecard

subProcesses.name: Data Architecture Design & Governance
steps: Define data architecture principles, patterns, and technology standards for the enterprise
Design and maintain service topology and dependency maps across the data platform
Conduct architecture review of proposed new data products and platform components
Assess alignment of proposals with target architecture and identify deviations
Approve architectural exceptions with compensating controls and sunset dates
Publish architecture decisions as ADRs in the enterprise knowledge base
Facilitate quarterly architecture guild reviews to evolve standards and retire technical debt
Maintain data platform roadmap aligned with business capability demands and cloud strategy
Produce architecture health metrics (tech debt, compliance to standard) for CTO review

subProcesses.name: Data Modeling & Design
steps: Receive modeling request and gather requirements from data product team or analytics lead
Design logical and physical data models for target domain area
Define data product structure and contracts including schema, SLA, and ownership
Review model designs with data architects and domain stewards for consistency
Validate design against enterprise standards, naming conventions, and normalization rules
Prototype model in development environment and validate against sample data
Approve model design and publish to data catalog as draft data product specification
Implement physical model in target platform (data warehouse, lakehouse, or graph store)
Conduct performance testing of model under expected query and write load
Hand off approved model documentation to engineering team for pipeline build

subProcesses.name: Data Lakehouse & Warehouse Platform Management
steps: Administer cloud data platform (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, or equivalent) configuration
Manage compute cluster provisioning, auto-scaling policies, and cost optimization settings
Apply platform patches, version upgrades, and configuration changes via change management
Enforce storage tier policies (hot, warm, cold) and automated lifecycle transitions
Monitor storage consumption, query performance, platform SLA adherence, and cost utilization
Conduct capacity planning and provision additional resources ahead of peak demand
Manage platform access controls, virtual warehouses, and resource groups
Run disaster recovery drills and validate RTO/RPO targets for critical data assets
Produce monthly platform utilization and availability reports for IT leadership

subProcesses.name: Data Platform Security Engineering
steps: Define platform security baseline controls aligned with enterprise security policy
Implement encryption at rest and in transit for all data platform storage and transport
Configure network isolation, private endpoints, and egress controls for data platform
Integrate data platform IAM with enterprise identity provider for centralized access governance
Remediate security findings from vulnerability scans and penetration tests within priority-based SLA windows
Conduct penetration testing and red-team exercises on data platform perimeter annually
Review security configuration after platform upgrades or architectural changes
Implement secrets management controls for service accounts, API keys, and database credentials
Track open security findings, remediation velocity, and control coverage on monthly security scorecard

subProcesses.name: Data Platform Compliance & Audit
steps: Run automated compliance scans against CIS benchmarks and internal security standards on a scheduled basis
Map data platform controls to SOX, HIPAA, and state privacy regulatory requirements
Maintain evidence packages and control documentation for regulatory and internal audit inspections
Coordinate data platform audit responses and provide requested evidence to internal audit and examiners
Track compliance findings, management responses, and remediation closure deadlines
Conduct control self-assessments prior to scheduled external examinations to identify gaps
Remediate audit findings and document corrective action evidence for auditor sign-off
Report compliance posture, open findings count, and remediation SLA adherence to CISO quarterly
Update platform compliance baseline after regulatory guidance changes or new control requirements are issued

subProcesses.name: Telemetry Instrumentation & Observability Platform
steps: Define requirements for observability coverage across data platform components
Develop approach for metrics, logs, and traces collection aligned with OpenTelemetry standards
Build and configure telemetry agents, exporters, and collection pipelines
Deploy observability platform management infrastructure for metrics, logs, and traces
Configure dashboards, SLI/SLO definitions, and alert routing in observability tooling
Validate telemetry coverage against instrumentation requirements checklist
Activate and hand off observability dashboards to data platform operations team
Tune sampling rates and retention policies to balance cost and diagnostic fidelity
Conduct quarterly observability reviews and expand coverage for newly deployed components

subProcesses.name: Data Platform Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity
steps: Define RTO and RPO targets for each data platform tier and critical data asset class
Design DR architecture including backup strategy, replication topology, and failover approach
Implement automated backup jobs and cross-region replication for critical data stores
Document DR runbooks covering failover, failback, and data integrity validation procedures
Schedule and conduct tabletop DR exercises with data platform and operations teams
Execute full DR failover drills against production-equivalent environments annually
Validate data completeness and pipeline integrity after each DR drill and remediate gaps
Maintain DR test evidence for compliance audits and regulatory inspections
Review and update DR plan after major platform changes, incident learnings, or RTO/RPO target revisions

subProcesses.name: Analytics & MI Requirements & Design
steps: Define analytics and MI requirements in collaboration with business stakeholders
Assess data availability, quality, and lineage adequacy for the proposed analytics use case
Design solution architecture (self-service BI, embedded analytics, or operational report)
Select visualization types and define KPI definitions, filters, and drill-down paths
Create low-fidelity mockups and review with business owners for alignment
Document data model dependencies and agree on refresh cadence and SLA with engineering
Obtain sign-off on requirements and design from product owner before build commences
Establish acceptance criteria and UAT plan for deliverable review
Log approved requirements in the analytics delivery backlog for sprint planning

subProcesses.name: Report & Dashboard Development
steps: Build reports and dashboards in approved BI tooling (Tableau, Power BI, or equivalent)
Implement data source connections, calculated fields, and aggregation logic
Apply corporate branding standards, accessibility guidelines, and naming conventions
Conduct developer self-review against requirements and design mockup
Validate outputs with data steward for metric accuracy and business logic correctness
Perform performance testing under concurrent user load and optimize slow queries
Execute UAT with business stakeholders and log and resolve defects
Obtain sign-off from product owner on final deliverable before production deployment
Deploy and configure row-level security and distribution permissions in BI platform
Publish MI artifacts by scheduling refreshes and enabling subscriber notifications

subProcesses.name: Self-Service Analytics Enablement
steps: Define self-service data layer (semantic model, certified datasets) for business user consumption
Publish certified datasets to the self-service BI workspace with data dictionary documentation
Develop and deliver end-user training programs for self-service BI tools
Provide office-hours support and respond to ad-hoc analytics queries from business teams
Monitor self-service adoption metrics (active users, report creation rate, data refresh errors)
Curate and refresh the library of certified reusable components and starter templates
Govern self-service content via periodic review and archival of stale or inaccurate reports
Escalate complex analytical requests beyond self-service scope to analytics engineering team
Report self-service health metrics and adoption trends to analytics leadership quarterly

subProcesses.name: Advanced Analytics & Statistical Modeling
steps: Receive advanced analytics request and frame problem statement with business sponsor
Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand distributions, correlations, and gaps
Identify relevant actuarial, statistical, or predictive techniques appropriate to the use case
Source and prepare feature dataset from enterprise data assets and catalog
Build and tune analytical model or statistical analysis using validated methodology
Interpret results and translate findings into business-relevant insights and recommendations
Validate analytical outputs with domain experts (actuaries, underwriters, claims managers)
Document methodology, assumptions, limitations, and reproducibility instructions
Present findings to business sponsor and agree on action or further investigation
Publish validated analytical asset to catalog and hand off to BI or product team for operationalization

subProcesses.name: Regulatory & Actuarial Reporting Analytics
steps: Receive regulatory or actuarial reporting data requirements from finance and actuarial teams
Map reporting requirements to available enterprise data assets and assess completeness gaps
Build data extracts and aggregations required for statutory, GAAP, and IFRS 17 filings
Validate extract accuracy against source systems and prior period comparisons
Deliver certified data packages to actuarial and finance teams for sign-off
Maintain audit trail of extract logic, run dates, and validation evidence for regulatory inspection
Support regulators and external auditors with ad-hoc data provision under legal hold
Remediate data issues identified during actuarial review and rerun impacted extracts
Archive extract artifacts and validation evidence per regulatory retention requirements

subProcesses.name: Analytics Governance & Metric Management
steps: Define the enterprise metrics catalog with agreed business definitions and calculation logic
Govern metric definitions through a formal change request and approval process
Resolve disputes between business units over conflicting metric interpretations
Enforce metric consistency standards across BI tools, reports, and data products
Audit deployed reports for compliance with approved metric definitions
Publish the metrics catalog in the enterprise data catalog for discoverability
Train analytics developers and business analysts on metrics governance process
Report metrics catalog coverage, disputes resolved, and compliance scores to governance council

subProcesses.name: Analytics Operations & Refresh Management
steps: Monitor automated report and dashboard refresh jobs for failures or late-running completions
Triage and remediate refresh failures within priority-based SLA windows
Communicate refresh incidents and data staleness to affected business consumers
Manage extract schedules and optimize refresh windows to minimize platform contention
Conduct quarterly audit of active reports to identify and archive unused content
Apply version upgrades to BI platform following change management and testing procedures
Track report inventory, refresh SLA compliance, and incident counts on monthly scorecard
Coordinate with data engineering on upstream pipeline changes that affect BI data sources

subProcesses.name: AI & Analytics Use Case Framing
steps: Frame AI use case and success measures in partnership with business sponsor
Conduct feasibility assessment covering data availability, regulatory constraints, and build complexity
Define model performance KPIs, business value hypothesis, and go/no-go decision criteria
Identify similar prior models in inventory to assess reuse or adaptation opportunities
Produce use case brief and obtain data science leadership and governance pre-approval
Scope minimum viable model and define phased delivery milestones
Stand up project workspace with approved data access, compute, and tooling
Brief data stewards and privacy officer on data usage and consent requirements for the use case
Confirm regulatory classification (SR 11-7 tier, algorithmic bias risk) before model build begins

subProcesses.name: Feature Engineering & Feature Store Management
steps: Define requirements for features needed to support model training and scoring
Develop approach for feature derivation from raw data sources and transformation pipeline
Build and configure feature computation pipelines and register features in the feature store
Validate feature distributions, leakage risk, and alignment with business definitions
Approve and publish features to the enterprise feature store for shared team consumption
Monitor feature freshness, null rates, and distribution drift in the feature store
Deprecate stale or superseded features following a defined sunset notification process
Document feature lineage, business definition, and approved use cases in the catalog
Enforce access controls on sensitive features (PII-derived, protected class proxies)

subProcesses.name: Model Training & Experiment Tracking
steps: Define requirements for the model training experiment including algorithm candidates and hyperparameter search space
Develop approach for train/validation/test splits and cross-validation strategy
Build and configure training pipeline with reproducible seed, environment, and dependency pinning
Execute training runs and log all parameters, metrics, and artifacts in experiment tracker
Implement model explainability components (SHAP, LIME, or equivalent) to support interpretability requirements
Compare experiment results against baseline and prior model versions
Validate model performance on hold-out test set against predefined acceptance thresholds
Conduct bias and fairness evaluation across protected classes per responsible AI policy
Approve and publish selected model artifact to the model registry as a candidate for deployment
Document training methodology, data lineage, and known limitations in the model card

subProcesses.name: Model Validation & Peer Review
steps: Assign independent validator (separate from model developer) per model risk policy
Review model documentation, model card, and intended use statement for completeness
Replicate key training results and verify reproducibility of performance metrics
Stress-test model under distribution shift, adversarial inputs, and edge-case data scenarios
Assess conceptual soundness of feature selection and algorithm design choices
Evaluate bias, fairness, and disparate impact metrics against regulatory thresholds
Document validation findings, required remediations, and conditional approval status
Obtain sign-off from model risk officer for models classified as high-tier under SR 11-7
Log validation outcome and approval status in model registry and governance tracking system

subProcesses.name: Model Documentation & Model Card Management
steps: Populate standardized model card template covering purpose, data, performance, and limitations
Document intended use, prohibited use cases, and out-of-scope population coverage
Record fairness and bias evaluation results and mitigation measures applied
Attach training data lineage, feature list, and preprocessing pipeline documentation
Obtain model developer, validator, and risk officer sign-off on model card contents
Publish approved model card to the model registry alongside the model artifact
Update model card after retraining, drift detection events, or scope changes
Archive superseded model card versions for regulatory inspection and audit history

subProcesses.name: MLOps Handoff & Deployment Readiness
steps: Confirm model artifact, model card, and validation sign-off are complete before handoff
Conduct knowledge transfer session with MLOps engineer covering model interface, inputs, outputs, and dependencies
Document serving requirements including latency SLA, compute profile, and scaling expectations
Verify feature store pipeline compatibility and confirm feature availability in production environment
Package model with dependency manifest and environment specification for reproducible deployment
Register final model artifact in model registry with all required metadata for CI/CD gate checks
Participate in shadow deployment review to confirm model outputs align with expected production behavior
Archive all training artifacts, data splits, and experiment logs for regulatory audit traceability
Notify model risk governance team of new model ready for formal production deployment

subProcesses.name: Model Registry & Versioning
steps: Define requirements for model registry structure, metadata schema, and access controls
Develop approach for model artifact storage, versioning, and immutable lineage tracking
Build and configure model registry with integration to training, validation, and serving systems
Validate registry metadata completeness and artifact integrity on registration
Approve and publish registry configuration and onboard all active models from existing inventory
Manage model lifecycle state transitions (candidate, staging, production, deprecated, retired)
Enforce registry access controls and approval workflows for state promotions
Audit registry contents quarterly for stale candidates and unmaintained model versions
Produce registry metrics (active models by tier, age, last retrain date) for governance review

subProcesses.name: CI/CD for Models & Pipeline Automation
steps: Define requirements for model CI/CD pipeline stages and quality gate criteria
Develop approach for automated testing including unit tests, integration tests, and shadow scoring
Build and configure CI pipeline with model-specific quality gates (performance, bias, schema checks)
Integrate model CI/CD with model registry and approval workflow tooling
Validate CI/CD pipeline by running candidate model through all automated gate checks
Approve and publish CI/CD configuration and onboard all model teams to standardized pipeline
Monitor CI/CD pipeline execution metrics and enforce mandatory gate pass rates
Maintain pipeline-as-code in version control and apply changes through peer-reviewed PRs
Report CI/CD reliability, gate failure rates, and deployment lead times on monthly scorecard

subProcesses.name: Model Deployment & Serving
steps: Define requirements for model serving pattern (REST API, batch score, embedded, or streaming)
Develop deployment configuration including compute, scaling, and latency SLA specifications
Build and configure serving infrastructure with health checks, load balancing, and circuit breakers
Execute shadow deployment and compare outputs against incumbent model in production traffic
Conduct canary rollout with progressive traffic shifting and automated rollback triggers
Validate production serving metrics against SLA targets before full promotion
Approve and publish model to full production traffic and notify consuming applications
Monitor serving endpoint availability, latency, and error rates post-deployment
Execute rollback to prior model version if performance or availability thresholds are breached

subProcesses.name: Model Performance & Drift Monitoring
steps: Plan and scope monitoring strategy covering predictive performance, data drift, and concept drift
Configure statistical drift detection (PSI, KS test, or equivalent) on input feature distributions
Instrument model endpoints to log prediction distributions and ground truth labels as available
Collect performance metrics (AUC, Gini, precision/recall) on rolling windows
Assess drift alerts against predefined thresholds and model risk tier requirements
Document findings in drift monitoring report and classify as informational, warning, or critical
Escalate critical drift alerts to model owner and data science team for remediation
Trigger retraining evaluation when performance degrades beyond acceptable threshold
Archive monitoring evidence for model risk governance review and regulatory inspection

subProcesses.name: Model Retraining & Lifecycle Management
steps: Define requirements for retraining trigger conditions (schedule, drift threshold, business event)
Develop approach for retraining data selection, including recency weighting and leakage prevention
Build and configure automated retraining pipeline with feature and model registry integration
Execute retraining run and compare challenger model performance against production champion
Validate challenger model for performance, bias, and regulatory compliance
Approve and publish challenger to production following validation and risk officer sign-off
Retire and decommission superseded models from registry and serving infrastructure
Update model card, registry metadata, and governance documentation post-retraining
Communicate retraining outcome and champion change to consuming application teams

subProcesses.name: Responsible AI & Model Risk Governance
steps: Maintain model inventory and risk tiering for all production and development models
Plan and scope annual model risk review calendar aligned with regulatory and internal policy
Gather model performance, drift, and usage data for the review period
Assess models against fairness, explainability, and accuracy standards
Document findings in model risk report with risk ratings and required remediation actions
Present findings to model risk committee and track remediation to closure
Coordinate with Actuarial and Compliance on state insurance regulatory algorithmic requirements
Respond to regulatory examinations and provide model documentation packages on request
Update model risk framework policies annually based on regulatory guidance and industry practice

subProcesses.name: AI Policy & Ethical Framework
steps: Define enterprise AI ethics principles and responsible AI policy aligned with regulatory guidance
Map applicable regulations to AI use cases (NAIC model bulletin, state algorithmic accountability laws)
Publish AI use policy covering permitted use cases, prohibited uses, and human oversight requirements
Socialize AI policy with data science, technology, legal, and business leadership stakeholders
Establish AI ethics review board with cross-functional membership and governance charter
Define escalation path for novel AI use cases requiring ethics board deliberation
