Review and update AI policy annually or after material regulatory or technology changes
Maintain training program ensuring all model developers complete responsible AI certification

subProcesses.name: Algorithmic Bias & Fairness Testing
steps: Define protected class attributes and fairness metrics applicable to each model use case
Source or construct representative test datasets with demographic labels for bias evaluation
Execute fairness testing suite measuring disparate impact, equal opportunity, and calibration
Compare bias metrics against regulatory thresholds and internal fairness policy limits
Document bias findings and proposed mitigation strategies in bias assessment report
Implement bias mitigation techniques (re-sampling, adversarial debiasing, threshold adjustment)
Retest model after mitigation to validate improvement and absence of new bias introduction
Obtain legal and compliance sign-off on bias assessment results before model deployment
Maintain bias test evidence packages for regulatory examination and internal audit

subProcesses.name: Model Explainability & Consumer Disclosure
steps: Define explainability requirements by model tier and regulatory jurisdiction
Implement post-hoc explainability methods (SHAP, LIME, counterfactual) for customer-facing models
Validate explainability outputs for fidelity and alignment with model's actual decision logic
Design consumer-facing explanations for adverse actions (declination, surcharge, rate variation)
Review consumer-facing explanations with legal and compliance for regulatory accuracy
Integrate explanation generation into decisioning systems for automated adverse action notices
Test explanation quality with consumer research groups for comprehensibility
Maintain audit log of explanations generated for regulatory inspection and dispute resolution
Update explanation methodology after model retraining or significant feature changes

subProcesses.name: Generative AI & LLM Risk Management
steps: Define risk classification framework for generative AI and large language model use cases
Conduct risk assessment for each proposed GenAI use case covering hallucination, privacy, and bias
Establish approved GenAI tooling list and vendor assessment criteria for enterprise use
Implement human-in-the-loop controls for high-risk GenAI outputs (adverse decisions, customer comms)
Define and enforce data handling rules for data submitted to external LLM providers
Monitor GenAI outputs for accuracy, harmful content, and policy compliance via spot-check program
Respond to GenAI incidents (hallucination events, data leakage, unauthorized use) per incident process
Report GenAI risk posture and control effectiveness to AI ethics board quarterly
Update GenAI risk framework as regulatory guidance and technology capabilities evolve

subProcesses.name: AI Regulatory Examination & Reporting
steps: Monitor evolving AI and algorithmic insurance regulatory requirements across all operating states
Maintain a regulatory tracking register mapping requirements to impacted models and processes
Prepare model disclosure documentation packages for state insurance department examinations
Coordinate with actuarial and legal teams to respond to regulatory data and model inquiries
Submit required model-use filings or notifications to state regulators by statutory deadline
Conduct pre-examination readiness assessments and remediate identified gaps before exam date
Support examiners with document production, system walk-throughs, and Q&A sessions
Track examination findings, corrective action commitments, and closure evidence
Report regulatory examination status and open items to Chief Compliance Officer monthly

subProcesses.name: Third-Party AI & Vendor Model Risk
steps: Maintain inventory of all third-party AI and vendor-supplied model products in production use
Conduct initial due diligence on new vendor AI products covering model risk, bias, and data handling
Negotiate contractual rights for model validation access, bias testing, and audit documentation
Integrate vendor models into enterprise model inventory and apply internal risk tiering
Monitor vendor model performance and drift using available inputs and outcome data
Review vendor model updates and assess change impact before accepting new model versions
Conduct annual vendor model reassessment and update risk rating based on performance evidence
Escalate unresolved vendor model risk issues to procurement and legal for contract action
Report third-party model risk posture to model risk committee and Chief Risk Officer

subProcesses.name: AI Incident Management & Learning
steps: Define AI-specific incident categories (model error, bias event, data poisoning, GenAI misuse)
Receive and triage AI incident reports from internal teams, regulators, or consumers
Conduct preliminary impact assessment to determine scope, affected models, and remediation urgency
Invoke incident response playbook appropriate to incident category and severity tier
Execute containment actions (model rollback, output suppression, access revocation) as required
Investigate root cause using model monitoring evidence, audit logs, and data lineage tooling
Notify affected business units, legal, compliance, and regulators as required by severity tier
Produce post-incident report with root cause, corrective actions, and timeline of events
Incorporate lessons learned into AI policy, governance controls, and model risk framework updates

subProcesses.name: Service Topology & Dependency Mapping
steps: Build and maintain service topology and dependency maps for all data platform components
Discover service dependencies via automated service mesh interrogation and agent-based scanning
Validate auto-discovered topology against architecture documentation and known integrations
Update dependency maps following infrastructure changes, deployments, or decommissions
Publish service topology to observability platform for alert enrichment and blast-radius analysis
Review topology accuracy with platform engineers on a quarterly basis
Alert operations team when new undocumented dependencies are detected in production
Archive topology snapshots before major infrastructure changes for rollback reference

subProcesses.name: ML-Based Anomaly Detection
steps: Define anomaly detection scope covering platform metrics, pipeline throughput, and data quality signals
Train and tune anomaly detection models on historical time-series telemetry
Deploy anomaly detection models to the AIOps platform with production scoring configuration
Detect and log anomalies identified by model in real-time telemetry streams
Triage and assign anomaly alerts to relevant platform or data engineering teams
Investigate anomaly root cause using correlated logs and dependency context
Resolve and verify that anomalous conditions have been remediated and metrics returned to baseline
Close and report anomaly event with feedback on detection accuracy for model retraining cycle

subProcesses.name: Event Correlation & Noise Reduction
steps: Detect and log incoming alert events from monitoring tools into the AIOps event pipeline
Apply deduplication rules to suppress duplicate alerts from multiple monitoring sources
Execute ML-based correlation to group related events into actionable incident candidates
Triage and assign correlated incident candidates to on-call engineers with enriched context
Tune correlation rules and noise suppression models based on analyst feedback
Investigate and act on correlated incidents using enriched topology and historical context
Resolve and verify incident resolution by confirming event stream returns to normal baseline
Close and report incident with correlation accuracy score for model feedback loop

subProcesses.name: Alert Enrichment, Scoring & Routing
steps: Capture raw alerts from all monitoring sources into the central event bus
Enrich alert context with service topology, CMDB, and deployment data
Score alert priority using ML model trained on historical incident severity and business impact
Apply routing rules to direct enriched alerts to appropriate team queues and escalation paths
Deliver enriched alerts to on-call engineers via PagerDuty or equivalent tool
Track acknowledgment rates and response SLA compliance to validate routing accuracy
Escalate alerts that exceed team scope to incident management for major incident process
Tune scoring model and routing rules monthly based on escalation and false-positive feedback

subProcesses.name: Runbook Automation
steps: Capture runbook automation request from operations team or postmortem findings
Assess manual runbook steps for automation feasibility and risk classification
Design automation workflow with human approval gates for high-risk remediation actions
Build and configure automation script or workflow in the orchestration platform
Test automation in staging environment against representative failure scenarios
Validate automation output against expected state changes and safety constraints
Approve automation for production use following peer review and change management approval
Hand off automated runbook to operations with monitoring and disable procedure documented
Review automation effectiveness quarterly and retire obsolete runbooks

subProcesses.name: Auto-Remediation & Self-Healing
steps: Detect and log triggering condition matching an approved auto-remediation policy
Validate triggering conditions against remediation pre-conditions and safety interlocks
Execute automated remediation action (restart, scale-out, failover, or purge) per policy
Notify on-call engineer in parallel for human awareness and oversight
Escalate to engineer-led resolution if auto-remediation does not resolve condition within defined timeout
Verify successful remediation by confirming system health metrics return to normal

Close service request in ITSM platform and capture customer satisfaction data
Report recurring request patterns to demand management for automation consideration
Review SLA compliance for fulfilled requests and escalate breaches to service management

subProcesses.name: Monitoring & Alert Intake
steps: Configure monitoring coverage scope and alert thresholds aligned to service SLAs
Receive and triage incoming alerts from observability platform and third-party monitoring tools
Classify alert severity using defined priority matrix and assign to on-call engineer
Suppress duplicate or correlated alerts to reduce noise during active incidents
Escalate alerts meeting P1 or P2 criteria to incident management process
Gather initial diagnostic evidence from monitoring dashboards and log queries
Assess whether alert represents an incident, change artifact, or known issue
Document alert handling outcome and update runbook based on investigation findings
Report alert volume, false-positive rates, and MTTR metrics in weekly operations review
Conduct quarterly alert hygiene review and retire or adjust stale thresholds

subProcesses.name: Major Incident & Service Recovery
steps: Detect and log potential major incident from monitoring alert or stakeholder notification
Declare major incident and assign incident commander and communication lead
Triage and assign technical resolver teams to incident bridge
Notify impacted stakeholders through defined communication channels with initial impact statement
Investigate root cause using observability data, logs, and recent change activity
Execute remediation actions including failover, rollback, or emergency configuration change
Resolve service and verify recovery through functional smoke tests and monitoring confirmation
Issue all-clear notification to stakeholders with summary of impact duration and affected services
Close incident record and schedule post-incident review within five business days
Publish post-incident report to technology leadership and affected business stakeholders

subProcesses.name: Post-Incident Review & Root-Cause Analysis
steps: Initiate post-incident review and capture timeline, contributing factors, and impact data
Conduct blameless root-cause analysis using structured technique such as 5-Whys or fishbone
Identify contributing factors across people, process, technology, and environment dimensions
Define remediation actions with owners, priorities, and target completion dates
Validate root-cause finding with engineering and operations subject-matter experts
Assess adequacy of existing monitoring and alerting coverage that was in place at incident time
Identify detection and response gaps that contributed to extended mean time to restore
Obtain sign-off on post-incident report from incident commander and technology leadership
Publish post-incident review findings to engineering community for organizational learning
Archive post-incident report with supporting evidence in incident record for compliance audit

subProcesses.name: Resilience Improvement
steps: Execute and track remediation actions from post-incident reviews through to verified closure
Validate improvement through monitoring metrics and recurrence rate tracking
Update runbooks, alerting rules, and architectural diagrams with lessons learned
Contribute resilience improvement patterns to engineering standards library
Report open and closed remediation actions in monthly reliability review
Review recurring incident themes and escalate systemic issues to architecture for strategic remediation
Plan and execute chaos engineering or game-day exercises to validate system resilience
Define and track service error budgets to prioritize reliability work against feature delivery
Assess and improve failover and disaster recovery runbook coverage for critical services
Present resilience improvement outcomes and trend data to technology leadership quarterly

subProcesses.name: Operational Handoff & Post-Release Support
steps: Assess release against production readiness checklist before hypercare period begins
Review runbooks, monitoring dashboards, and on-call assignments for new service or feature
Plan hypercare and cutover support schedule including war room availability
Execute hypercare support with enhanced monitoring and expedited escalation paths
Triage and resolve post-release defects under expedited SLA during hypercare window
Communicate hypercare status daily to product owner and business stakeholders
Verify stability exit criteria including error rate, latency SLO, and defect count thresholds
Formally accept service into steady-state operations and hand over to run team
Document lessons learned and update operational runbooks with release-specific guidance
Close hypercare and confirm standard support SLA applies to the delivered service

subProcesses.name: SLA Management & Service Reporting
steps: Define service level objectives and availability targets for all production services
Instrument SLO tracking using observability platform with defined error budget calculations
Produce weekly service health report covering uptime, incident volume, and error budget consumption
Identify services at risk of SLO breach and initiate reliability improvement discussions
Conduct monthly service review with business stakeholders covering SLA performance and incident trends
Review and update SLA definitions annually to reflect business criticality and technology evolution
Manage SLA exception process for planned maintenance and approved exclusion events
Track mean time to detect and mean time to restore metrics per service tier
Escalate chronic SLA underperformance to engineering leadership for prioritized remediation
Produce annual service reliability report for technology governance and business leadership

subProcesses.name: Cloud Cost Visibility & Reporting
steps: Ingest cloud provider billing data into FinOps platform on daily basis
Validate billing data completeness and reconcile provider invoices to usage data and general ledger
Analyse cost trends by service, account, environment, and business unit dimension
Identify cost anomalies using automated spend anomaly detection rules and thresholds
Alert cost owners of anomalies with contextual spend data and recommended investigation steps
Produce monthly cloud cost report covering actuals, variance to budget, and trend analysis
Distribute showback and chargeback reports to business unit cost owners
Escalate material unresolved anomalies to FinOps governance committee
Maintain cost reporting dashboard in FinOps tooling with self-service access for stakeholders
Archive monthly billing reconciliation records for audit and regulatory review

subProcesses.name: Cloud Tagging & Cost Allocation
steps: Define cost allocation taxonomy aligned to business units, products, and cost centres
Publish and enforce cloud resource tagging standards through policy-as-code controls
Monitor tagging compliance rate and alert resource owners of missing or incorrect tags
Remediate untagged resources through automated tagging pipelines where feasible
Allocate shared platform costs using agreed-upon allocation keys and apportionment rules
Reconcile allocated costs to financial system cost centres at month-end close
Review and update cost allocation methodology annually with finance and business stakeholders
Report tagging compliance and allocation accuracy metrics to FinOps governance committee
Validate allocation accuracy by reconciling allocated totals to provider billing totals each period
Document allocation methodology decisions and maintain version history for finance audit

subProcesses.name: Showback & Chargeback Reporting
steps: Define showback and chargeback policy covering which business units receive each report type
Prepare monthly showback report for non-chargeback business units to drive cost awareness
Produce formal chargeback invoices for business units operating under chargeback policy
Validate chargeback amounts against approved allocation methodology before distribution
Distribute reports and invoices to business unit finance contacts on agreed monthly schedule
Receive and investigate chargeback disputes raised by business unit stakeholders
Resolve disputes by reviewing allocation evidence and adjusting entries where warranted
Communicate dispute outcomes to business unit finance and update records accordingly
Report chargeback coverage, dispute volume, and resolution rates to FinOps governance committee
Review and update showback and chargeback policy annually with finance and business leadership

subProcesses.name: Commitment & Rate Optimization
steps: Analyse 90-day usage history to identify stable workloads suitable for commitment coverage
Model commitment options including Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and committed-use discounts
Assess coverage gaps and calculate incremental savings opportunity for each commitment type
Prepare commitment purchase recommendation with break-even analysis and risk assessment
Obtain approval from FinOps committee and finance for commitment purchase above threshold
Execute commitment purchase through cloud provider console or programmatic API
Track coverage rate and utilisation for active commitments in FinOps platform
Monitor unused commitment waste and initiate re-sale or modification where provider supports it
Produce quarterly commitment portfolio review covering coverage, savings realised, and renewal forecast
Renew or replace expiring commitments based on updated usage analysis and business forecast

subProcesses.name: Resource & Usage Optimization
steps: Run automated rightsizing analysis across compute, database, and storage resource types
Detect and log idle, stopped, and underutilised resources in optimization backlog
Triage and assign optimization recommendations to resource-owning engineering teams
Investigate recommendations with application owners to confirm safe optimization actions
Execute approved rightsizing, idle resource termination, or storage tier changes
Verify performance and availability SLOs are maintained following optimization actions
Track realized savings from executed optimizations and report against FinOps savings targets
Identify architectural waste patterns including over-provisioned clusters and data transfer inefficiencies
Escalate architectural optimization opportunities to cloud platform engineering for systemic resolution
Close optimization cycle and produce savings realization report for FinOps governance

subProcesses.name: Cloud Budgeting & Forecasting
steps: Gather cloud spend actuals and business growth projections as inputs to annual budget cycle
Define cloud budget by account, service, and business unit aligned to approved headcount and project plans
Develop cloud spend forecast using trend analysis, commitment coverage, and planned project activity
Validate forecast with engineering leads and business unit finance partners
Approve and publish annual cloud budget and monthly forecast baseline
Conduct monthly budget-vs-actuals review and update rolling 12-month forecast
Investigate and explain material budget variances with contributing factor analysis
Escalate forecast overruns above materiality threshold to FinOps governance committee for remediation
Update budgeting methodology and allocation models based on business structure changes
Report cloud budget performance and forecast accuracy to CTO and CFO on quarterly basis

subProcesses.name: Cloud Unit Economics
steps: Define unit economic metrics mapping cloud infrastructure spend to business value drivers per policy, per claim, and per transaction
Collect and normalize unit cost inputs including compute, storage, and network spend per workload
Build and maintain cloud unit cost model with automated refresh from FinOps billing data
Validate unit cost model accuracy with engineering and finance stakeholders on quarterly basis
Analyse unit cost trends over rolling 12-month period to identify efficiency improvements
Benchmark unit economics against industry peers and cloud provider benchmarks where available
Identify workloads with unit cost deterioration and escalate to engineering for architectural review
Incorporate unit economics into investment case evaluations for new platform and product initiatives
Report cloud unit economics trends to CTO and CFO for strategic investment decisions
Update unit cost model definitions and metrics as business products and technology platforms evolve

subProcesses.name: FinOps Governance, Policy & Sustainability
steps: Define and publish FinOps policy covering tagging standards, optimization targets, and governance thresholds
Establish FinOps governance committee charter with engineering, finance, and business representation
Plan and scope FinOps maturity assessment against industry framework such as the FinOps Foundation model
Gather evidence of FinOps practice adoption across engineering and business stakeholder groups
Assess and score FinOps practices against maturity criteria in each domain
Document findings including gaps, risks, and prioritised improvement recommendations
Report FinOps maturity assessment outcomes and improvement roadmap to technology leadership
Track remediation and improvement action completion through governance committee
Integrate cloud sustainability and carbon-efficiency metrics into FinOps reporting
Review and update FinOps policy and governance framework on annual basis
